This page fixes the framework and the quantity conventions of the
non-relativistic quantum mechanics category before any derived result is
stated. The arena is the Newtonian one: the affine time space with absolute
time, Euclidean simultaneous slices and their smooth structure
([[def-nrqm-framework-newtonian-spacetime]]), whose elementary coordinate
transformations are the Galilean maps with their parameter quadruples
([[def-nrqm-framework-galilei-transformations]]) forming a group of bijections
of the coordinate space ([[lem-nrqm-framework-galilei-transformations-form-a-group]]).
The inertial frames of the model are the adapted charts determined by an event
origin, a fixed time vector $u$ with $\tau(u)=1$, and a positively oriented
orthonormal spatial triad, changed only by the Galilean class
([[def-nrqm-framework-inertial-frames]]), and the
macroscopic apparatus and preparation devices are described by classical
trajectories with the frame time as parameter
([[def-nrqm-framework-classical-apparatus-trajectories]]); a quantum particle
is not assigned a definite worldline between preparations and detections. The
dimension group, the SI reference units, the exact defining constants of the
current SI and the dimensions and mathematical types of the framework's
quantities are recorded in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], and
the canonical commutator of the position and momentum acts is proved on the
Schwartz core in [[lem-nrqm-framework-ccr-on-the-schwartz-core]].

consumer_reviews.snippet:
(a) the declared polarisation analyser at angle $\theta$ is a declared ideal
sharp measurement with outcome structure $(P_{\theta},P_{\theta}^{\perp})$, the
outcome labels $+1$ and $-1$ naming the first and second projection, in
the sense of clause (a) of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]:
$P_{\theta}$ and $P_{\theta}^{\perp}$ are bounded orthogonal projections with
$P_{\theta}P_{\theta}^{\perp}=0$ and $P_{\theta}+P_{\theta}^{\perp}=I$;

(b) the spectral projection-valued measure $E$ of the bounded self-adjoint
operator $P_{\theta}$ (assigned with unit $1$; its values on the two outcomes
are $1$ and $0$, while the analyser labels are $+1$ and $-1$) satisfies
$$E(\{1\})=P_{\theta},\qquad E(\{0\})=P_{\theta}^{\perp},\qquad E(\mathbb R\setminus\{0,1\})=0,$$
consequently the outcome law of the assigned sharp quantity $P_{\theta}$ in a
preparation $\rho\in D(V)$ is
$$p_{+1}(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{\theta}),\qquad p_{-1}(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{\theta}^{\perp})=1-p_{+1}(\rho),$$
which is exactly the law of the declared analyser;

(c) for the linear-polarisation preparation $\psi_{\varphi}$ and a general
pure preparation with unit vector $\psi=\alpha e_{1}+\beta e_{2}$,
$$p_{+1}(\psi_{\varphi})=\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi),\qquad p_{-1}(\psi_{\varphi})=\sin^{2}(\theta-\varphi),\qquad p_{+1}(\psi)=|\alpha\cos\theta+\beta\sin\theta|^{2};$$
for a statistical mixture $\rho=\sum_{n}w_{n}\rho_{n}$ of preparations the law
is affine, $p_{+1}(\rho)=\sum_{n}w_{n}p_{+1}(\rho_{n})$;

(e) if $p_{+1}(\rho)>0$, the conditional state after the outcome $+1$ of the
analyser is $\rho_{+1}=P_{\theta}\rho P_{\theta}/p_{+1}(\rho)$; for the pure
preparation $[\psi_{\varphi}]$ with $\cos(\theta-\varphi)\ne0$ it is the pure
state of the analysed ray $[e_{\theta}]$, and a second analyser at angle
$\theta'$ then gives the conditional probability
$\cos^{2}(\theta'-\theta)$ for the outcome $+1$. If the outcome is discarded,
the state is $\Phi(\rho)=P_{\theta}\rho P_{\theta}+P_{\theta}^{\perp}\rho P_{\theta}^{\perp}$;

[F3] **Spectral atoms.** For a self-adjoint operator $A$ with spectral measure $E$, the projection $E(\{\lambda\})$ is the orthogonal projection onto $\ker(A-\lambda)$; hence at an eigenvalue $\lambda$ with eigenspace $\mathbb C u$, $u$ unit, one has $E(\{\lambda\})=T_{u,u}$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(\{\lambda\}))=\langle u,\rho u\rangle$ ([[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clause (a)).

1.3 [Pure preparations] Let $\psi=\alpha e_{1}+\beta e_{2}$ be a unit vector. Since $E(\{1\})=P_{\theta}$, the probability is $\|P_{\theta}\psi\|^{2}=\langle\psi,P_{\theta}\psi\rangle=|\langle\psi,e_{\theta}\rangle|^{2}=|\alpha\cos\theta+\beta\sin\theta|^{2}$; for $\psi=\psi_{\varphi}$ this equals $\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$ by [F4], and then $p_{-1}=1-p_{+1}=\sin^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$. [F1, F3, F4, algebra]

consumer_reviews.snippet:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1 and the observable and
probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]), the radiation extension
postulate
([[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]]),
the radiation sector definition
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]] and
the declared ideal counting model
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-ideal-counting-and-detection-model]]. Assume the
Axioms of Countable Choice, Dependent Choice and Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a unit mode vector $\varphi\in\mathfrak h$, a
dimensionless label $z\in\mathbb C$, and write $U:=U_\varphi$ for the fixed-mode isometry of
[[lem-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-number-isometry]]. Then:

(a) for every $n\in\mathbb N$ the $n$-quanta mode vector $Ue_{n}=\varphi^{\otimes n}$
is a unit vector of the $n$-photon sector; the count law of the declared ideal
total-number detector in the preparation of its ray is
$p_{m}=\delta_{mn}$, and the number readout is $n$ with probability one;

(c) if $\varphi\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$, with unit-mode coordinates
$\varphi(k)$ in $\mathrm m^{3/2}$ under $d^{3}k$ as in clause (b) of
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]], and writing
$\bar\varepsilon:=\langle\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}\varphi,\varphi\rangle=\hbar c\int|k|\,\|\varphi(k)\|^{2}\,d^{3}k$,
the energy means of the assigned free-field energy observable are
$$\langle H_f\rangle_{Ue_{n}}=n\,\bar\varepsilon,\qquad \langle H_f\rangle_{U\psi_{z}}=|z|^{2}\,\bar\varepsilon ;$$

(d) under the same condition $\varphi\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$, writing
$\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}:=\|\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}\varphi\|^2$,
the energy variances are
$$\operatorname{Var}_{Ue_{n}}(H_f)=n\bigl(\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}-\bar\varepsilon^{2}\bigr),\qquad \operatorname{Var}_{U\psi_{z}}(H_f)=|z|^{2}\,\overline{\varepsilon^{2}} ;$$
the first is strictly positive for every $n\ge1$ and the second is strictly
positive for every $z\ne0$, so neither preparation has sharp energy;

(e) *full-sector Gibbs limitation*: let $\beta>0$ have SI unit
$\mathrm J^{-1}$, so that $\beta H_f$ is dimensionless. The bounded operator
$e^{-\beta H_f}$ is not compact and hence not trace class; therefore it does
not define a density operator by trace normalization on the full transverse
continuum sector. This conclusion rules out only that trace-normalized
full-sector Gibbs form. Other mode-selected, regularized or otherwise
separately defined preparations are outside this theorem; no identification of
$\beta$ with an inverse thermodynamic temperature and no thermal interpretation
of any state is asserted here;

(f) all assertions are conditional on P1, P2 and the adopted radiation model
and use only the declared ideal counting model. No measured count, frequency,
efficiency or temperature is asserted, and no sampling model is introduced.

**Given:** the postulates P1, P2 and the adopted radiation model with transverse space $\mathfrak h$, Fock space $F(\mathfrak h)$, sectors $\mathfrak H_{n}^{+}$, projections $\Pi_{n}$, number operator $N$, energy $H_f$ with $\varepsilon(k)=\hbar c|k|$, a unit mode vector $\varphi$ with coordinate units $\mathrm m^{3/2}$ under $d^{3}k$, a dimensionless label $z\in\mathbb C$ and the isometry $U=U_\varphi$.

[F3] **Coherent vector coefficients.** $\psi_{z}=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\sum_{n}\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}e_{n}$ is unit with $\langle e_{n},\psi_{z}\rangle=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\frac{\bar z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}$ and $|\langle e_{n},\psi_{z}\rangle|^{2}=e^{-|z|^{2}}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!}$ ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-mode-number-law]] clauses (b),(c)).

[F4] **Energy moments on mode sectors.** For a unit $\varphi\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$, put $\bar\varepsilon=\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle$ and $\overline{\varepsilon^2}=\|\varepsilon\varphi\|^2$. Then $\Phi_n=\varphi^{\otimes n}\in D(T_n)$, $\langle T_n\Phi_n,\Phi_n\rangle=n\bar\varepsilon$ and $\|T_n\Phi_n\|^2=n\overline{\varepsilon^2}+n(n-1)\bar\varepsilon^2$. The last is the spectral second moment, not an assertion of membership in $D(T_n^2)$ ([[lem-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-number-isometry]] clause (d)).

[F6] **Non-compactness of the free Gibbs operator.** For every $\beta>0$ read with SI unit $\mathrm J^{-1}$, the operator $e^{-\beta H_f}$ is not compact and in particular not trace class ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]] clause (d)).

1.1 [Number states] By [F1] each $Ue_{n}=\varphi^{\otimes n}$ is a unit vector of the sector $\operatorname{ran}P_{+}^{(n)}$; by [F2] $N$ acts on it as $n$ times itself, so the number readout is $n$ with probability one by the atom law of P2 ([[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]]), and the count law of the declared detector is $p_{m}=\operatorname{tr}(T_{Ue_{n},Ue_{n}}\Pi_{m})=\langle\Pi_{m}Ue_{n},Ue_{n}\rangle=\delta_{mn}$. This proves (a). [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 [Poisson moments] Put $x:=|z|^{2}\ge0$. By [F5], $\sum_{n\ge1}n\frac{x^{n}}{n!}=x\sum_{m\ge0}\frac{x^{m}}{m!}=xe^{x}$ and $\sum_{n\ge2}n(n-1)\frac{x^{n}}{n!}=x^{2}e^{x}$, so the mean is $e^{-x}xe^{x}=x$ and the second moment is $e^{-x}(x^{2}+x)e^{x}=x^{2}+x$; hence the variance is $x$. For $z\ne0$ the law is supported on more than one value, so the preparation is not a number state. This proves (b). [F3, F5, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 [Energy means] The sector diagonality of $H_f$ and orthogonality of the sectors give, for the coherent preparation, $$\langle H_fU\psi_{z},U\psi_{z}\rangle=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}|\langle e_{n},\psi_{z}\rangle|^{2}\,\langle T_{n}\varphi^{\otimes n},\varphi^{\otimes n}\rangle=\Bigl(\sum_{n}|\langle e_{n},\psi_{z}\rangle|^{2}n\Bigr)\bar\varepsilon=|z|^{2}\bar\varepsilon,$$ where the middle identity is [F1] and [F4] and the last is the Poisson mean of step 2.1; the number-state value is the $n$-th instance of [F1]. The Poisson second number moment is finite by step 2.1, so [F1] places $U\psi_z$ in the actual domain of $H_f$ and justifies the graph-truncation passage. The mean exists because both sides are finite: $\bar\varepsilon<\infty$ by $\varphi\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$ and Cauchy-Schwarz, and $\sum_{n}n|\langle e_{n},\psi_{z}\rangle|^{2}=x<\infty$. This proves (c). [F1, F2, F4, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [Energy variances] For the number state, $\|H_fUe_n\|^2=\|T_n\varphi^{\otimes n}\|^2=n\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}+n(n-1)\bar\varepsilon^{2}$ by [F4], so the variance is $n(\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}-\bar\varepsilon^{2})$, which is strictly positive for $n\ge1$ by clause (d) of [[lem-nrqm-photons-transverse-restricted-momentum-and-energy-multipliers]] (the energy multiplier has no eigenvalues, so $\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}-\bar\varepsilon^{2}=\operatorname{Var}_\varphi(\varepsilon)>0$). For the coherent preparation, its Poisson second moment and [F1] give $U\psi_z\in D(H_f)$; the orthogonal-sector norm expansion therefore gives $$\|H_fU\psi_z\|^2=\sum_{n}|\langle e_{n},\psi_{z}\rangle|^{2}\bigl(n\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}+n(n-1)\bar\varepsilon^{2}\bigr)=x\,\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}+x^{2}\bar\varepsilon^{2},$$ using the Poisson first and second factorial moments of step 2.1; subtracting the square of the mean $x\bar\varepsilon$ from step 3.1 gives $x\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}$, which is strictly positive for $x=|z|^{2}>0$ because $\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}=\|\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}\varphi\|^{2}>0$: $\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}\varphi$ vanishes only where $\varphi$ vanishes off the null set $\{k=0\}$, so a unit $\varphi$ cannot satisfy $\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}\varphi=0$ in $\mathfrak h$. This proves (d). [F1, F4, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

- **Poisson versus geometric.** The mode-coherent count law is Poisson, with variance equal to its mean; the declared single-mode Gibbs-type preparation of [[ex-nrqm-photons-single-mode-number-statistics-coherent-and-thermal]] has a geometric count law with larger variance at the same mean. Both are conditional model computations; distinguishing them in a laboratory requires a declared detector, preparation and sampling model and reported data.
- **No temperature identification.** The parameter $\beta$ in (e) has unit $\mathrm J^{-1}$ so that $\beta H_f$ is dimensionless. Identifying it with $(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ is an additional physical assumption not made here.

consumer_reviews.snippet:
Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero and action constant $\hbar>0$, with a **compact-support-class** potential
$V$ supported in the ball $B_{R}$, and adopt the declared stationary elastic
beam model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-stationary-beam-and-cross-section-model]] at wave number
$k>0$, direction $d\in S^2$ and the declared $n_{\mathrm{inc}}>0$ in
$\mathrm{m^{-3}}$, with incident energy $E=\hbar^2k^2/(2m)$.
The construction below retains the dimensionless unit-incident shape
$\Psi$; its physical beam field is $\Phi=\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}\Psi$.
Put
$$W:=\frac{2m}{\hbar^{2}}V,\qquad G_{k}(z):=\frac{e^{ik|z|}}{4\pi|z|},\qquad (K_{k}f)(x):=\int_{B_{R}}G_{k}(x-y)W(y)f(y)\,dy$$
for $f\in L^{2}(B_{R};\mathbb C)$ and $x\in B_{R}$. Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

[F4] **Unit-shape and physical current readings.** The mathematical current functional is $\mathbf j^{\mathrm{unit}}[\psi]=(\hbar/m)\operatorname{Im}(\overline\psi\nabla\psi)$. For the unit incident shape its value is $(\hbar k/m)d$, and for the exact outgoing shape $fe^{ikr}/r$ its radial value is $(\hbar k/m)|f|^2/r^2$ ([[lem-nrqm-scattering-three-dimensional-current-and-flux]] clause (c)). For the declared constant $n_{\mathrm{inc}}>0$, the beam model reads the physical field as $\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}\psi$, so the quadratic functional gives $\mathbf j[\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}\psi]=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\mathbf j^{\mathrm{unit}}[\psi]$, and its cross sections are ratios with $J_{\mathrm{inc}}=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\hbar k/m$ ([[def-nrqm-scattering-stationary-beam-and-cross-section-model]] (b)-(d)).

[F5] **The beam model's solubility vocabulary.** A generalized stationary solution is a $C^{2}$ function on the complement of $\operatorname{supp}V$ satisfying the stationary equation there with an outgoing asymptotic reading and a scattering amplitude read in metres ([[def-nrqm-scattering-stationary-beam-and-cross-section-model]] clause (c)).

2.1 The kernel $G_{k}(x-y)W(y)$ on $B_{R}\times B_{R}$ is square-integrable because $|x-y|^{-2}$ is locally integrable in three dimensions and $B_{R}$ is bounded, so $K_{k}$ is Hilbert-Schmidt and [F2] gives bounded invertibility of $I+K_{k}$; [F1] then gives $\Psi\in H^{2}_{\mathrm{loc}}$, the distributional equation $(-\Delta+W-k^{2})\Psi=0$ and $\Psi|_{B_{R}}=u$, which is (a). [F2, F1, step 1.1, algebra]

4.1 By [F1] the unit-shape scattered field $\Psi_{\mathrm{sc}}=\Psi-e^{ikd\cdot x}$ has radial mathematical current $(\hbar k/m)|f_k|^2/r^2+O(r^{-3})$ uniformly. Write $\Psi_{\mathrm{sc}}=u+iv$; the physical field has real and imaginary parts $\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}u,\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}v$. Since the scale is constant, its current is $(\hbar/m)[(\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}u)\nabla(\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}v)-(\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}v)\nabla(\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}u)]=n_{\mathrm{inc}}(\hbar/m)(u\nabla v-v\nabla u)$ by [F4]. Thus the physical scattered current is the display in (c), and the same calculation on the unit incident plane wave gives $J_{\mathrm{inc}}=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\hbar k/m>0$. Dividing yields $\lim_{r\to\infty}r^2j_r^{\mathrm{sc}}/J_{\mathrm{inc}}=|f_k|^2$. Smoothness and boundedness of $f_k$ on the sphere, with [F1]'s uniform error, give the finite total cross section $\sigma=\int_{S^2}|f_k|^2d\Omega$. The unit-shape amplitude stays in metres and the density cancels from both cross-section readings. This is (c). [F1, F4, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 By step 2.1 and step 3.1 the constructed $\Psi$ is $C^{2}$ on the complement of the essential closed support of $V$: near each such point the convolution integrates the compactly supported $L^1$ density $Wu$ against $G_k(x-y)$ at a positive distance from its singularity, so its derivatives of every fixed order are bounded on a smaller neighborhood and differentiation under that integral is valid; the incident exponential is smooth too. The total field $\Psi$ satisfies the stationary equation there by step 2.1 and has the outgoing reading with amplitude $f_{k}$ in metres by step 3.1; by [F5] it is a generalized stationary solution of the beam model at energy $E$ and direction $d$, and the construction determines it through the explicit invertible problem, so no other function with the same equation and outgoing reading arises from this construction. This is (d) and completes the proof. [F5, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

- **What is read, and what is not.** The amplitude and cross sections are
  computed from the explicitly constructed stationary field; the pair asserts
  nothing about a preparation that would realize the incident plane-wave
  reading, and no measured count rate is predicted. Converting these model
  quantities into an expected count rate requires a declared target, fluence
  and detector model with its own uncertainties.
- **Normalization.** With physical coordinates $x$ in metres and $k$ in
  inverse metres, the unit-incident shape $\Psi$ is dimensionless, the reduced
  potential $W=(2m/\hbar^2)V$ is in $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$, and the displayed
  integral for $f_k$ has dimension length. The physical beam field
  $\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}\Psi$ is in $\mathrm{m^{-3/2}}$; its number currents
  are in $\mathrm{m^{-2}s^{-1}}$. The common density factor cancels, leaving
  $d\sigma/d\Omega$ in $\mathrm{m^2\,sr^{-1}}$ independently of its value.

consumer_reviews.snippet:
(a) *Well-posedness of the declared model.* The family $U$ is the unique family of bounded operators on $\mathfrak H$ that is jointly norm-continuous on $I\times I$, unitary-valued, satisfies $U(s,s)=I$ and the cocycle $U(t,r)=U(t,s)U(s,r)$, and solves $i\hbar\partial_{t}U(t,s)=H(t)U(t,s)$ together with its second-endpoint equation $i\hbar\partial_{s}U(t,s)=-U(t,s)H(s)$ in operator norm. In particular the model's clause (c)(i) declaration has exactly one solution: the driven model in the bounded norm-continuous class is well posed.

(c) *Evolved states and outcome laws.* For every preparation $\rho$ specified at time $s$ the operator $\rho(t):=U(t,s)\rho(s)U(t,s)^{*}$ is a preparation of the model with $\operatorname{tr}\rho(t)=1$ for every $t\in I$, and the specification is consistent with the cocycle: evolving first from $s$ to $r$ and then from $r$ to $t$ gives the same preparation. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi(s)$ the vector $\psi(t):=U(t,s)\psi(s)$ is unit and spans a pure preparation for every $t$. For every assigned sharp observable $(A,u_{A})$ ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]) and every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$, the number $\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)$ is the model's outcome probability at time $t$.

(d) *Error of the unnormalized truncated quadratic estimate.* Let $\psi(s)$ be a unit vector, put $\psi^{N}(t):=\sum_{n=0}^{N}U_{n}(t,s)\psi(s)$ and let $(A,u_{A})$ be an assigned sharp observable with $A\in\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ bounded. Then for every $t\in I$ and every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$,
$$\bigl|\mu^{A}_{\psi(t)}(B)-\mu^{A}_{\psi^{N}(t)}(B)\bigr|\le (1+\|\sum_{n=0}^NU_n(t,s)\|)\,\|R_N(t,s)\|\le 2\,e^{K\tau}\frac{(K\tau)^{N+1}}{(N+1)!},$$
where the truncated quantity is the unnormalized quadratic form $\mu^{A}_{\psi^{N}(t)}(B):=\|E_{A}(B)\psi^{N}(t)\|^{2}$ of the truncated vector, whose norm is at most $e^{K\tau}$. It is an approximation to the normalized exact Born law and need not itself be a probability law; for $N=1$ the bound also implies the looser estimate $2e^{K\tau}(K\tau)^{2}$.

[F1] **Dyson propagator.** Under the hypotheses of the Statement, $\|U_{n}(t,s)\|\le(K|t-s|)^{n}/n!$; the series $U=\sum_{n\ge0}U_{n}$ converges in operator norm uniformly on $I\times I$, is jointly norm-continuous, satisfies $U(s,s)=I$, $\|U(t,s)-I\|\le e^{K|t-s|}-1$, is the unique continuous $\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$-valued solution of the integral equation $U(t,s)=I-\frac{i}{\hbar}\int_{s}^{t}H(r)U(r,s)\,dr$ for fixed $s$, and has operator-norm derivatives $\partial_{t}U(t,s)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}H(t)U(t,s)$, $\partial_{s}U(t,s)=+\frac{i}{\hbar}U(t,s)H(s)$; every $U(t,s)$ is unitary with $U(t,s)^{*}=U(s,t)$ and the cocycle holds ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-norm-dyson-series-and-uniqueness]] clauses (a)-(d)).

[F3] **State and outcome readings of the model.** The model declares the evolved preparation $\rho(t)=U(t,s)\rho(s)U(t,s)^{*}$ and states that it is a preparation for every $t$ by unitarity and [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]; the outcome law of an assigned sharp observable $(A,u_{A})$ in a preparation is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{A}(B))$, for a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi$ the value $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}$ ([[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] clauses (c)(i), (d); [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (a), (b); [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]; [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]; [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]).

[F4] **Inner-product and projection estimates.** The pairing is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second with $|\langle u,v\rangle|\le\|u\|\|v\|$ ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-for-real-and-complex-inner-product-spaces]], [[def-inner-product-space]]); the spectral projections $E_{A}(B)$ of a self-adjoint bounded $A$ satisfy $0\le E_{A}(B)\le I$ and $\|E_{A}(B)\|\le1$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]); and for unit vectors $u,v$ and a contraction $Q$ one has $|\|Qu\|^{2}-\|Qv\|^{2}|\le 2\|u-v\|$.

1.1 [Well-posedness and the properties of the propagator] The family $H$ is norm-continuous with bounded self-adjoint values on the compact interval $I$, so [F1] applies and supplies the norm-convergent unitary propagator $U$ with the cocycle, the inverse relation, joint norm-continuity and the two operator-norm endpoint equations; uniqueness of the continuous solution of the integral equation with $U(s,s)=I$ for fixed $s$ is clause (c) of [F1], and the differential equation together with $U(s,s)=I$ implies that integral equation by integration. Hence the family declared in clause (c)(i) of the model is exactly $U$, and it is unique; this is clause (a). [F1, given]

1.3 [Evolved preparations and outcome laws] By [F3] the model's evolved preparation is $\rho(t)=U(t,s)\rho(s)U(t,s)^{*}$, and it is a preparation for every $t$ because $U(t,s)$ is unitary [F1]; the cocycle of [F1] gives $U(t,r)\rho(r)U(t,r)^{*}=U(t,s)U(s,r)\rho(s)U(s,r)^{*}U(t,s)^{*}=\rho(t)$ for $r$ between $s$ and $t$, so the result does not depend on the intermediate time. For a unit vector $\psi(s)$, $\|\psi(t)\|=\|\psi(s)\|=1$ by unitarity, so $[\psi(t)]$ is a pure preparation. The outcome probability at time $t$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)$ by [F3], the reading of P2. This is clause (c). [F1, F3, given]

2.1 [Error of the unnormalized truncated estimate] Let $S_N=\sum_{n=0}^NU_n(t,s)$, $u=U(t,s)\psi(s)$ and $v=S_N\psi(s)$ for a unit initial vector. Then $\|u\|=1$, $\|v\|\le\|S_N\|\le\sum_{n=0}^N(K\tau)^n/n!\le e^{K\tau}$ by [F1], and $\|u-v\|\le\|R_N\|$. For the spectral projection $Q=E_A(B)$, the exact Born probability is $\|Qu\|^2$ while $\|Qv\|^2$ is the stated unnormalized quadratic estimate. Their difference equals $\langle Q(u-v),Qu\rangle+\langle Qv,Q(u-v)\rangle$; Cauchy-Schwarz and contraction of $Q$ bound its absolute value by $(1+\|S_N\|)\|R_N\|\le(1+e^{K\tau})\|R_N\|$. Crucially [F2] supplies the stronger unitary remainder $\|R_N\|\le(K\tau)^{N+1}/(N+1)!$, so the result is at most $2e^{K\tau}(K\tau)^{N+1}/(N+1)!$, preserving the advertised final bound. For $N=1$ it is at most $e^{K\tau}(K\tau)^2$, and hence also the stated looser $2e^{K\tau}(K\tau)^2$. At $K\tau=0$ both quantities coincide. No unit norm or density interpretation is assigned to the truncated vector. This proves (d). [step 1.1, step 1.2, F1, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

- **The stronger unitary bound.** Because every $U(t,s)$ is unitary, the truncation lemma also records the bound $\|R_{N}(t,s)\|\le(K\tau)^{N+1}/(N+1)!$, which does not grow exponentially; the theorem states the exponential version because it is the one used to convert to the outcome-law estimate with the same constant.
- **From propagator error to probability error.** Clause (d) is the mechanism by which the Dyson truncation of the page's amplitude theorems becomes a bound on an outcome probability; it applies to every Borel outcome set and every bounded assigned sharp observable, and it requires no additional physical assumption beyond P2.

**(i) Declared charged pair and relative coordinate.** Take the declared

outcome law $\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$, $\sin^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$ of the
declared ideal analyser, its affinity over mixtures, its phase invariance and

[[pthm-nrqm-photons-one-photon-number-energy-and-momentum-laws]] proves that a
normalisable one-photon preparation has the sharp number readout one, the
frequency and energy laws given by the push-forwards of $\|f(k)\|^{2}\,d^{3}k$
under $c|k|$ and $\hbar c|k|$ (a unit packet coordinate $f(k)$ has units
$\mathrm m^{3/2}$ under $d^{3}k$), their means under the first-moment condition, and
the corresponding momentum-component laws and means under absolute
first-moment integrability. Frequency, energy and momentum variances are
strictly positive and finite on the corresponding multiplier domains; the
singleton probabilities vanish for every normalisable unit vector without a
moment-domain hypothesis.
[[pthm-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-number-and-energy-statistics]] proves the sharp
count of the $n$-quanta mode state, the Poisson count law and moments of the
mode-coherent preparation, the energy means and variances of those
preparations, and that $e^{-\beta H_f}$ is not trace class for the full
continuum sector when $\beta>0$ has unit $\mathrm J^{-1}$. Thus its
trace-normalized full-sector Gibbs density is unavailable; other preparations
are outside the theorem. All these are conditional consequences of P1, P2 and
the adopted radiation model; their units are recorded in

(b) *Flow.* The family $U(t):=\exp(-itH_{\kappa}/\hbar)$ is the model's
strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group; the Schroedinger equation
$i\hbar\frac{d}{dt}\psi(t)=H_{\kappa}\psi(t)$ holds in the norm-differentiable
sense exactly for initial vectors $\psi(0)\in D(H_{\kappa})$, and for other
vectors the evolution is continuous but the equation is not asserted; density
preparations evolve by $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$ with $\rho(t)$ a density
operator for every $t$;

(d) *Position reading.* In a unit vector $\psi$ the position outcome law is
$\mu^{G}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{B}|\psi|^{2}dx$; if $\psi$ is in addition a unit
eigenvector of $H_{\kappa}$ with eigenvalue $E$, then the position density
$|\psi|^{2}$ and the energy point mass at $E$ are readings of the same
preparation through the declared observables, with no joint-measurement claim;

[F4] **Assigned observables and outcome laws.** For an assigned sharp observable $(A,u_{A})$, the spectral measure and outcome law are $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{A}(B))$, the outcome law of a unit pure vector is $\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}$, the outcomes lie in $\sigma(A)$, and the reading of an exact value is the singleton probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$, which vanishes unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (a)-(e), [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]).

[F5] **Flow and stationarity.** The flow $U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)$ of an assigned energy observable is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group whose generator is $-iH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$; the norm-differentiable Schroedinger equation holds exactly on $D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$; a nonzero $\psi$ gives a stationary pure preparation exactly when it is an eigenvector, and then every bounded assigned sharp observable has a time-independent outcome law, in particular the energy law is time-independent ([[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clauses (b), (c), (e), [[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-stationary-states-and-energy-conservation]] clauses (a), (c)).

[F6] **Position law.** In the spin-zero model the Born position law of a unit $\psi$ is $\mu^{G}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{B}|\psi|^{2}dx$ for Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$ ([[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]] clause (b)).

1.1 [Energy observable and spectrum] By [F1], $H_{\kappa}$ is self-adjoint on the dense domain $H^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$; with the declared unit joule the pair $(H_{\kappa},\mathrm J)$ is an assigned sharp observable in the sense of [F4]. Write $c_{0}:=\hbar^{2}/2m>0$, so that $H_{\kappa}=c_{0}C_{\gamma}$. By [F3] applied to $A=C_{\gamma}$, $c_{0}A$ is self-adjoint and $\sigma(c_{0}A)=c_{0}\sigma(A)$, whence $\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(H_{\kappa})=c_{0}\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(C_{\gamma})=c_{0}[0,+\infty)=[0,+\infty)$. A point $\lambda\in\sigma(H_{\kappa})\cap(-\infty,0)$ has $\lambda/c_{0}\in\sigma(C_{\gamma})\cap(-\infty,0)$, so by [F2] it is an eigenvalue of $C_{\gamma}$ of finite multiplicity isolated in $\mathbb R$; by clause (d) of [F3] the eigenspaces correspond exactly under the scaling, so $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $H_{\kappa}$ of the same finite multiplicity, isolated because $c_{0}$ is a homeomorphism of $\mathbb R$, and the set of such $\lambda$ is at most countable as the image of an at-most-countable set. Boundedness below is [F2] together with the scaling, and the action formula is [F1]. This proves (a). [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

2.1 [Flow] By (a) and [F5] the family $U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\kappa}/\hbar)$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group; the Schroedinger equation holds in the norm-differentiable sense exactly for $\psi(0)\in D(H_{\kappa})$; density preparations evolve as $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$. This is (b). [step 1.1, F5]

consumer_reviews.snippet:
Adopt the postulates P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]],
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] and
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]] for a
declared particle of mass parameter $m>0$ and spin label $s$, with state space
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, $r=2s+1$, componentwise operators
$Q_{j},P_{k}$ and translations $T_{a}$
([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (c));
assume the Axiom of Choice, the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of
Dependent Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]). Consider the **free model**, the bounded-potential
model with $V\equiv0$:
$$H_{0}:=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2},\qquad D(H_{0})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}),$$
with flow $U(t)=\exp(-itH_{0}/\hbar)$, momentum unitary $U^{(r)}$
([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]]) and
$f_{t}(p):=e^{-it|p|^{2}/(2m\hbar)}$. Then:

(c) **Momentum conservation.** For every $k$ the momentum component $P_{k}$ is
a conserved observable of the free model: for every preparation $\rho$, Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and $t$,
$$\mu^{P_{k}}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{P_{k}}_{\rho(0)}(B),$$
and for a unit vector $\psi(0)\in D(P_{k})$ the mean and second moment of the
law of $P_{k}$ are finite and independent of $t$, with time-zero values
$\langle P_{k}\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|P_{k}\psi\|^{2}$; the coordinate
translations satisfy $T_{te_{k}}=e^{-itP_{k}/\hbar}$, so the momentum
components are the generators of the translational symmetry groups;

**Given:** The postulates P1, P2, P4, P5, P6 in the stated readings; the
Axioms of Choice, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice; the state space
$H_{s}$; the operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$ and translations $T_{a}$; the free
operator $H_{0}$ with flow $U(t)$; the momentum unitary $U^{(r)}$; a
preparation $\rho$; a unit vector $\psi$; a Borel set $B$; $a\in\mathbb R^{3}$,
$k\in\{1,2,3\}$, $t\in\mathbb R$.

[F1] **Free operator.** $H_{0}=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k}P_{k}^{2}$ with domain
$W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ is self-adjoint and generates the
strongly continuous unitary group $U(t)=e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}$
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clauses (b),(c), [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]
clause (a), [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]]).

[F2] **Translations.** $T_{a}$ is unitary, $T_{a}D(Q_{j})=D(Q_{j})$,
$T_{a}Q_{j}T_{a}^{-1}=Q_{j}-a_{j}I$, $T_{a}D(P_{k})=D(P_{k})$,
$T_{a}P_{k}T_{a}^{-1}=P_{k}$, $T_{a}W^{2,2}=W^{2,2}$, and
$T_{te_{k}}=e^{-itP_{k}/\hbar}$
([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clauses (c),(d)).
For a real bounded measurable $V$ with $V_{a}(x)=V(x-a)$ one has
$T_{a}H_{V}T_{a}^{-1}=H_{V_{a}}$, and $T_{a}$ is a symmetry of $H_{V}$ if and
only if $V_{a}=V$ almost everywhere; if $V$ is almost everywhere constant,
the momentum components are conserved with the law and moment statements of
(c) ([[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-translation-invariance-and-momentum-conservation]]
clauses (a)-(c)).

[F3] **Momentum representation.** $U^{(r)}$ is unitary, maps
$\mathcal S^{(r)}$ onto itself, satisfies $U^{(r)}P_{k}=M_{p_{k}}U^{(r)}$ on
the momentum domains, and conjugates the translations to multipliers:
$U^{(r)}T_{a}^{(r)}U^{(r)-1}=M_{e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}}$
([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]] clauses (b),(d)).

[F5] **Bounded multipliers commute.** For bounded measurable $g,h$ on
$\mathbb R^{3}$ the pointwise multiplication operators on
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3},dp;\mathbb C^{r})$ satisfy $M_{g}M_{h}=M_{gh}$ and
$\|M_{g}\|\le\sup|g|$, and the real case is the multiplication convention of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (a); the complex case follows from the same pointwise definition
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-hilbert-space]]). In particular the unimodular multipliers
$M_{e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}}$ and $M_{f_{t}}$ are unitary and commute with each
other, since $e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}f_{t}(p)=f_{t}(p)e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}$ for
every $p$.

1.2 [Multiplier commutation and explicit conjugation] By [F3] and [F4], conjugating $T_{a}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}T_{a}^{-1}$ by the unitary $U^{(r)}$ gives $M_{e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}}M_{f_{t}}M_{e^{ia\cdot p/\hbar}}$; by [F5] the multipliers commute and are unitary, with $M_{e^{ia\cdot p/\hbar}}=M_{e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}}^{-1}$, so this product equals $M_{f_{t}}$, which is $U^{(r)}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}U^{(r)-1}$. Hence $T_{a}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}T_{a}^{-1}=e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}$, which is the second display of (a) and, equivalently, $T_{a}U(t)=U(t)T_{a}$ for all $a,t$: the first display of (b). [F3, F4, F5, given, algebra]

mathematics: the explicit factorisation of the single-vertex emission

proves the single-vertex emission and absorption amplitudes of the model, the

explicit Dyson tail, and the exact mirror relation between emission into and
absorption from a unit one-photon vector.

limit of the single-vertex coefficient per unit time and declares the model
rate coefficient $\Gamma_{b}=2\pi\eta_{0}^{2}J_{b}(\Delta)/\hbar$ under a
continuous positive mode density, with the above-cutoff case tending to zero.
[[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-stimulated-dipole-drive-transitions]] proves the
first-order amplitudes of the prescribed classical drive, the equal
stimulated emission and absorption coefficients for the same physical gap and prescribed real field, and
the exact identification of declared two-level Pauli data with the circular
and linear two-level drive models of the driven-dynamics page.

angular and parity conditions on the uncompressed dipole matrix elements, and
transfers their vanishing to compressed matrices when the declared finite-level

orthonormal basis is chosen from that same subfamily. All of these are
conditional consequences of the cited postulates, mathematics and model data;
their units are those of

norm of [[def-operator-norm]] and [[def-bounded-linear-operator]], and

for $\Omega\in S^{2}$, read in metres. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice
and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).
Then:

[F1] **Controlled Born amplitude error.** Assume Countable Choice. Adopt the hypotheses and notation of the nondimensional stationary outgoing integral theorem for a real bounded potential $V_{0}$ supported in $B_{R}$: $q=\|K_{k}\|$, $u=(I+K_{k})^{-1}e_{\mathrm{inc}}$ and $f_{k}$ the amplitude. If $q<1$, then $\|u-e_{\mathrm{inc}}\|_{2}\le\frac{q}{1-q}\|e_{\mathrm{inc}}\|_{2}$ and $|f_{k}(\Omega)-f_{B}(\Omega)|\le\frac{\|V_{0}\|_{\infty}|B_{R}|^{1/2}}{4\pi}\frac{q}{1-q}\|e_{\mathrm{inc}}\|_{2}$ uniformly in $\Omega$; for $V_{\eta}=\eta V_{0}$ with $|\eta|q<1$ the scaling displays hold with $u_{\eta}=(I+\eta K_{k})^{-1}e_{\mathrm{inc}}$ and the same amplitude integrals, for real and complex $\eta$, with no base condition on $q$ ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-controlled-born-amplitude-error]] clauses (a), (b), (c)).

**Proof technique:** direct; instantiate the abstract controlled Born theorem with the energy-divided physical-coordinate potential $W=W_x$ (in $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$), retaining physical $k$, $R$ and the amplitude in metres, then rewrite its constants in the model's symbols.

- **Reading the condition.** In the model's variables the condition of (a)-(b)
  is the operator-norm condition $q=\|K_{k}\|<1$ on the declared potential,
  radius and wave number; the examples of this pair verify it for a uniform
  ball potential through an explicit Hilbert-Schmidt bound of the kernel, so
  no vague smallness of the potential is used.
- **Complex coupling.** The scaling form is algebraic in $\eta$ and does not
  use the real-potential flux conclusions; for complex $\eta$ the pair
  asserts no unitarity or cross-section reading of the resulting amplitude
  beyond the displayed estimate.

has dimension $N(M)=\#\{m\in\{-s,\dots,s\}:M-m\in\{-t,\dots,t\}\}$, and the

the unique unit vector in the kernel of $S^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}$ up to a phase;

$J^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i}:=J^{(s)}_{i}\otimes I+I\otimes J^{(t)}_{i}$ are
self-adjoint with the angular momentum commutators,
$J^{\mathrm{tot}2}=J^{(s)2}\otimes I+I\otimes J^{(t)2}+2\sum_{i}J^{(s)}_{i}\otimes J^{(t)}_{i}$,

$V_{s}\otimes V_{t}=\bigoplus_{j=|s-t|}^{s+t}W_{j}$ with $\dim W_{j}=2j+1$,

Each $S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i}$ is self-adjoint, so its square is self-adjoint; because the space is finite-dimensional, their sum $S^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}$ is self-adjoint. 1.2 [Singlet computation] Let $s=t=\tfrac12$ and $\Psi=\tfrac1{\sqrt2}(e^{(s)}_{1/2}\otimes e^{(t)}_{-1/2}-e^{(s)}_{-1/2}\otimes e^{(t)}_{1/2})$; by [F1] $J^{(s)}_{+}e^{(s)}_{1/2}=0$, $J^{(s)}_{+}e^{(s)}_{-1/2}=e^{(s)}_{1/2}$ and $J^{(s)}_{-}e^{(s)}_{1/2}=e^{(s)}_{-1/2}$, $J^{(s)}_{-}e^{(s)}_{-1/2}=0$, and analogously for $t$; hence $J^{\mathrm{tot}}_{+}(e^{(s)}_{1/2}\otimes e^{(t)}_{-1/2})=e^{(s)}_{1/2}\otimes e^{(t)}_{1/2}=J^{\mathrm{tot}}_{+}(e^{(s)}_{-1/2}\otimes e^{(t)}_{1/2})$ and $J^{\mathrm{tot}}_{-}(e^{(s)}_{1/2}\otimes e^{(t)}_{-1/2})=e^{(s)}_{-1/2}\otimes e^{(t)}_{-1/2}=J^{\mathrm{tot}}_{-}(e^{(s)}_{-1/2}\otimes e^{(t)}_{1/2})$, so $J^{\mathrm{tot}}_{\pm}\Psi=0$ and therefore $J^{\mathrm{tot}}_{1}\Psi=J^{\mathrm{tot}}_{2}\Psi=J^{\mathrm{tot}}_{3}\Psi=0$ by $J^{\mathrm{tot}}_{\pm}=J^{\mathrm{tot}}_{1}\pm iJ^{\mathrm{tot}}_{2}$; $\Psi$ is unit because the product basis is orthonormal. [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 [Decomposition and Clebsch-Gordan data] Transferring [F2] to the total spin operators by the rescaling of step 1.1 gives the orthogonal decomposition $V_{s}\otimes V_{t}=\bigoplus_{j=|s-t|}^{s+t}W_{j}$ with $\dim W_{j}=2j+1$, the unitary equivalence with the spin-$j$ matrices on each block and hence $S^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}=\hbar^{2}j(j+1)I$ on $W_{j}$, the weight multiplicity of (c) and the identity basis; the block bases $v_{j,k}$ have the displayed ladder actions with the stated phase convention, which are (b) and (c). 3.1 [Uniqueness of the singlet] For $s=t=\tfrac12$ the decomposition of step 2.1 has the two blocks $j=0$ and $j=1$ with dimensions $1$ and $3$, and $S^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}=0$ on the one-dimensional block $W_{0}$ and $S^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}=\hbar^{2}\cdot2I$ on $W_{1}$; hence $\ker S^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}=W_{0}$ is one-dimensional, and since $\Psi\ne0$ satisfies $S^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}\Psi=0$ by step 1.2, it spans $W_{0}$: the kernel is the line $\mathbb C\Psi$. (b) if $T_{a}$ is a symmetry for every $a\in\mathbb R^{3}$, then $V$ is almost
everywhere constant; in that case $H_{V}=H_{0}+cI$ on $W^{2,2}$ for
$H_{0}=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k}P_{k}^{2}$ and $c$ the constant, and the translations
form a strongly continuous unitary group of symmetries;

(c) **Momentum conservation for translation-invariant models.** Let $V$ be
almost everywhere constant and let $c$ be that constant. Then for every
$k\in\{1,2,3\}$ the momentum component $P_{k}$ is a conserved observable of the
model with energy $H_{V}$: for every preparation $\rho$, every Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and every $t$,
$$\mu^{P_{k}}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{P_{k}}_{\rho(0)}(B);$$
if $\psi(0)\in D(P_{k})$ is a unit vector, the mean and second moment of the
law of $P_{k}$ are conserved with time-zero values $\langle P_{k}\psi,\psi\rangle$
and $\|P_{k}\psi\|^{2}$; and the coordinate translations satisfy
$T_{te_{k}}=e^{-itP_{k}/\hbar}$ for all $t$, so the generators of the
one-parameter symmetry groups are the momentum components;

**Given:** The postulates P1, P2, P4, P5, P6 in the stated readings; the Axioms
of Choice, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice; the state space $H_{s}$; the
operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$ and translations $T_{a}$; a real bounded measurable $V$;
the operator $H_{V}$; a preparation $\rho$; a unit vector $\psi$; a Borel set
$B$; $a\in\mathbb R^{3}$; $k\in\{1,2,3\}$; $t\in\mathbb R$.

[F1] **Translations and the bounded-potential operator.** $T_{a}$ is unitary
with $T_{a}D(Q_{j})=D(Q_{j})$, $T_{a}Q_{j}T_{a}^{-1}=Q_{j}-a_{j}I$,
$T_{a}D(P_{k})=D(P_{k})$, $T_{a}P_{k}T_{a}^{-1}=P_{k}$, and
$T_{a}W^{2,2}=W^{2,2}$; $T_{a}H_{V}T_{a}^{-1}=H_{V_{a}}$; and
$T_{te_{k}}=e^{-itP_{k}/\hbar}$ with the generator identification of the
translation group ([[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-translation-covariance]] clause (c),
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clauses (c),(d)).

[F2] **Multipliers.** $M_{V}$ is the bounded self-adjoint multiplication
operator by the real bounded class $V$; for two real bounded measurable
functions $W_{1},W_{2}$ one has $M_{W_{1}}=M_{W_{2}}$ if and only if
$W_{1}=W_{2}$ almost everywhere; and $H_{V}=H_{0}+M_{V}$ is self-adjoint with
domain $W^{2,2}$ and generates a strongly continuous unitary group
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clauses (a),(c), [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]).

[F3] **Mollifiers and Lebesgue points.** Let $\rho(x)=q(|x|)$ be the
unit-mass radial mollifier supported in $B_1(0)$ and
$\rho_\varepsilon(x)=\varepsilon^{-3}\rho(x/\varepsilon)$ its family
([[def-mollifier-family-generated-by-a-unit-mass-smooth-bump]],
[[def-radial-mollifier-family-in-rn]]). Since $q$ is continuous with compact
support, $\Phi(r):=\sup_{u\ge r}|q(u)|$ is bounded, nonincreasing, vanishes
for $r\ge1$, and satisfies $|\rho(y)|\le\Phi(|y|)$ and
$\int_{\mathbb R^3}\Phi(|y|)\,dy<\infty$. The radial-majorant recovery lemma
therefore applies: for $f\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ and a Lebesgue point $x$ of
$f$, $(f*\rho_\varepsilon)(x)\to f(x)$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$
([[lem-radial-majorized-kernels-recover-lebesgue-point-values]],
[[def-lebesgue-point-and-lebesgue-set]]); almost every point is a Lebesgue
point of $f$ ([[thm-almost-every-point-is-a-lebesgue-point]]). For bounded
measurable $V$, each integral against $\rho_\varepsilon(x-\cdot)$ is
absolutely convergent because the kernel is bounded with compact support.

[F4] **Conservation theorem.** For a declared isolated system with energy
$H_{\mathrm{op}}$ and flow $U(t)$, a self-adjoint $A$ with
$e^{-isA/\hbar}U(t)=U(t)e^{-isA/\hbar}$ for all $s,t$ has a time-independent
outcome law, conserved moments for vectors in $D(A)$, and a unitary symmetry
$S$ of the dynamics satisfies $SU(t)=U(t)S$
([[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-generator-conservation]] clauses (a)-(c)).

2.1 [Lebesgue points and constancy] For each positive integer $n$ put $B_n:=B(0,n)$ and $f_n:=V\mathbf 1_{B(0,n+1)}\in L^{1}(\mathbb R^{3})$. By [F3] almost every $x\in B_n$ is a Lebesgue point of $f_n$, so choose one such point $x_n\in B_n$; for $0<\varepsilon<1$ the support of $\rho_\varepsilon(x_n-\cdot)$ lies in $B(0,n+1)$, and the recovery lemma gives $c_\varepsilon=(V*\rho_\varepsilon)(x_n)=(f_n*\rho_\varepsilon)(x_n)\to f_n(x_n)=V(x_n)=:c_n$. For every Lebesgue point $x\in B_n$ of $f_n$, the same support argument and recovery lemma give $V(x)=\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}c_\varepsilon=c_n$; hence $V=c_n$ almost everywhere on $B_n$. The balls $B_n$ are nested and each has positive measure, so their constants agree and $V$ is almost everywhere constant on $\mathbb R^3$. Calling that constant $c$, [F2] gives $H_V=H_0+cI$, and the translations are symmetries by (a) and form a strongly continuous unitary group by [F1]. This proves (b). [step 1.2, F1, F2, F3, given, algebra]

3.1 [Momentum conservation] Let $V=c$ almost everywhere, so $H_{V}=H_{0}+cI$ on $W^{2,2}$. For fixed $k$, the group $W(s):=e^{-isP_{k}/\hbar}=T_{se_{k}}$ of [F1] consists of unitaries $S$ with $SD(H_{V})=D(H_{V})$ and $SH_{V}S^{*}=H_{V}$: the identity for $P_{k}$ in [F1] gives $T_{se_{k}}P_{k}T_{se_{k}}^{-1}=P_{k}$ and hence the same for $P_{k}^{2}$ and for $H_{V}$ with its domain. By [F4] applied to the unitary symmetry $S=T_{se_{k}}$, $W(s)U(t)=U(t)W(s)$ for all $s,t$, where $U$ is the flow of $H_{V}$; hence the conservation conclusion of [F4] applies with $A:=P_{k}$, giving the displayed time-independence of the momentum law for every preparation and, for $\psi(0)\in D(P_{k})$, the conservation of the mean and second moment with the time-zero values of [F4] and [F5]. The generator statement is [F1]. This proves (c). [step 2.1, F1, F4, F5, given, algebra]

Let $U(t)=\exp(-itH_1/\hbar)$ be the model's flow, let $\Psi_z$ be the coherent state of label $z\in\mathbb C$, put $z(t):=ze^{-i\omega t}$, and define $x_0:=\sqrt2\,\ell\operatorname{Re}z$, $p_0:=\frac{\sqrt2\,\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}z$ for every $z\in\mathbb C$. Then:

**Given:** the adopted postulates P1, P2, P4, P5; the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice; the one-dimensional oscillator model with parameters $m,\omega,\hbar>0$, length $\ell$ and energy operator $H_1$; the coherent states $\Psi_z$; a complex number $z$ and a real number $t$.

[F1] **The model's flow.** $H_1$ is the model's assigned energy observable, and the model's flow is the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group $U(t)=\exp(-itH_1/\hbar)=\int e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\,dE_{H_1}(\lambda)$ of the autonomous-dynamics reading of the model definition, whose generator is $-\frac{i}{\hbar}H_1$ with domain $D(H_1)$ ([[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clause (c); [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clauses (a), (b), (c); [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]).

[F2] **Explicit flow and coherent evolution.** The family $U(t)f=\sum_ne^{-i\omega(n+\frac12)t}\langle f,\psi_n\rangle\psi_n$ is the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group with generator $-\frac{i}{\hbar}H_1$, so it is the flow of [F1]; and for every $z$, $U(t)\Psi_z=e^{-i\omega t/2}\Psi_{ze^{-i\omega t}}$, while the evolved coherent means and variances are $\langle Q\rangle_{z(t)}=\sqrt2\ell\operatorname{Re}z(t)$, $\langle P\rangle_{z(t)}=\frac{\sqrt2\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}z(t)$, $\operatorname{Var}(Q)_{z(t)}=\ell^{2}/2$, $\operatorname{Var}(P)_{z(t)}=\hbar^{2}/(2\ell^{2})$ with $z(t)=ze^{-i\omega t}$ ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-evolution-and-variance]] clauses (a), (b), (c), (e), (f); [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clause (c)).

[F3] **Coherent coefficients and the energy law.** $\Psi_z=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\sum_n\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}\psi_n$ with coefficients $\langle\Psi_z,\psi_n\rangle=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}$; the mean of the assigned excitation-number outcome law in unit $1/\mathrm{count}$ is $\langle N_\psi\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle=|z|^{2}$, since $\Psi_z\in D(N_\psi)$ by [[def-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-states]] clause (c), the numerical value is given by [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-state-convergence]] clause (e), and the outcome-law moment formula is [[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]] clause (a). The energy outcome law of the assigned observable $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ is $\mu^{H_1}_{\Psi_z}(B)=\sum_{n:E_n\in B}|\langle\Psi_z,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}$ with $E_n=\hbar\omega(n+\frac12)$; its mean is $\langle H_1\rangle_z=\hbar\omega(|z|^{2}+\frac12)$ by $H_1=\hbar\omega(N_\psi+\frac12I)$ and the same moment formula, using $D(H_1)=D(N_\psi)$ from [[pthm-nrqm-oscillator-energy-spectrum-and-completeness]] clause (b). ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-state-convergence]] clauses (a), (e); [[def-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-states]] clause (b); [[pthm-nrqm-oscillator-energy-spectrum-and-completeness]] clauses (b), (c); [[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]] clause (a); [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-closed-ladder-domains]] clause (e)).

[F5] **Means and spreads.** For an assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ and a unit vector $f\in D(A)$ the mean and second moment of the outcome law exist with mean $\langle Af,f\rangle$ and variance $\|(A-\langle Af,f\rangle I)f\|^{2}$, and the preparation spread is its square root ([[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]] clauses (a), (b); [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]] clauses (b), (c), (d)).

1.1 [The flow and its coherent action] By [F1] the model's flow is the strongly continuous unitary group generated by $-\frac{i}{\hbar}H_1$; by [F2] the explicit spectral family $U(t)f=\sum_ne^{-i\omega(n+\frac12)t}\langle f,\psi_n\rangle\psi_n$ has the same generator, so by the uniqueness of the generator recorded in the autonomous-dynamics reading the two families agree, and $U(t)\Psi_z=e^{-i\omega t/2}\Psi_{z(t)}$ for every $z$ and $t$. [F2] **The indicator potential.** $B(0,1)=\{x\in\mathbb R^{3}:|x|<1\}$ is the
Euclidean unit ball ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-metric-ball]]);
$V_{0}=1_{B(0,1)}$ is real, measurable with $0\le V_{0}\le1$, and nonconstant
since $V_{0}(0)=1$ and $V_{0}(2e_{1})=0$. For every $x$,
$$V_{0,a}(x)=1\iff x-a\in B(0,1)\iff |x-a|<1,$$
so $\{x:V_{0}(x)\ne V_{0,a}(x)\}=\{x:|x|<1\le|x-a|\}\cup\{x:|x-a|<1\le|x|\}$.

**Proof technique:** direct; take the indicator of the unit ball, exhibit a
point where the shifted potential differs, show that a whole ball lies in the
difference set, and use the positivity of Lebesgue measure of balls to
conclude that the potentials are not equal almost everywhere, so that the
symmetry criterion fails.

1.1 [A point where the shifted potential differs] Put $u:=a/|a|$, a unit vector, and $\delta:=\min\{|a|/2,1/2\}>0$, and set $x_{0}:=-(1-\delta)u$. Then $|x_{0}|=1-\delta<1$, so $V_{0}(x_{0})=1$; and $x_{0}-a=-(1-\delta+|a|)u$, so $|x_{0}-a|=1-\delta+|a|>1$ because $|a|>\delta$ for $\delta\le|a|/2$, whence $V_{0,a}(x_{0})=0$. Thus $x_{0}$ lies in the difference set $\{V_{0}\ne V_{0,a}\}$ of [F2]. [F2, F3, given, algebra]

[[def-nrqm-potentials-one-dimensional-line-model]] and the declared zero-range
model of [[def-nrqm-potentials-interval-and-delta-models]] clause (d) with
mass parameter $m>0$, spin label $s=0$, coupling $g\in\mathbb R$ (in joule
metres) and $\alpha_{g}=2mg/\hbar^{2}$. Let
$H_{g}=(\hbar^{2}/2m)A_{\alpha_{g}}$ be the assigned energy operator of the
zero-range model on the domain $D(H_{g})=D(A_{\alpha_{g}})$ of the interface
operator. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) $D(H_{g})$ consists exactly of the classes $u\in H^{1}(\mathbb R)$ whose
restrictions to $(0,\infty)$ and $(-\infty,0)$ are of class $H^{2}$, subject to
the interface condition
$$u'^{*}(0+)-u'^{*}(0-)=\frac{2mg}{\hbar^{2}}\,u^{*}(0),$$
On that domain, $(H_gu)|_{\mathbb R_\pm}=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}D^2(u|_{\mathbb R_\pm})$, where $\mathbb R_+=(0,\infty)$, $\mathbb R_-=(-\infty,0)$ and each second weak derivative is taken on its open half-line; these two $L^2$ classes are glued across the null point $0$. The action is not the global weak second derivative of $u$ on $\mathbb R$. $(H_{g},\mathrm J)$ is
an assigned sharp observable: $H_{g}$ is densely defined and self-adjoint on
$D(H_{g})$.

(c) *Attractive coupling.* If $g<0$, then $H_{g}$ has exactly one negative
eigenvalue, namely
$$E_{g}=-\frac{mg^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}}<0,$$
and its eigenspace is one-dimensional, spanned by the unit class
$$\psi_{g}(x)=\sqrt{\frac{m|g|}{\hbar^{2}}}\;\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{m|g|}{\hbar^{2}}|x|\Bigr).$$
For $g<0$ this is the unique bound-state preparation of the zero-range model: every
eigenvector of $H_{g}$ with negative eigenvalue is a nonzero multiple of
$\psi_{g}$, the preparation $[\psi_{g}]$ is stationary with energy $E_{g}$, and
the energy outcome law assigns probability one to $\{E_{g}\}$.

[F2] **Negative eigenvalues of the interface operator.** For $\alpha\ge0$ the operator $A_{\alpha}$ has no negative eigenvalue, and $0$ is not an eigenvalue for any $\alpha\in\mathbb R$; for $\alpha<0$ the number $-\alpha^{2}/4<0$ is an eigenvalue with one-dimensional eigenspace spanned by $\psi_{\alpha}(x)=\sqrt{-\alpha/2}\,e^{\alpha|x|/2}$, which is a unit vector, and it is the unique negative eigenvalue: every eigenvector with negative eigenvalue is a multiple of $\psi_{\alpha}$; moreover for $\hbar,m>0$ and $\alpha<0$ the scaled operator $(\hbar^{2}/2m)A_{\alpha}$ on the same domain is self-adjoint and has $\psi_{\alpha}$ as eigenvector with eigenvalue $-\hbar^{2}\alpha^{2}/(8m)$ ([[thm-nrqm-intervals-delta-unique-bound-state]] clauses (a)-(c)).

[F4] **Assigned observables and stationary states.** An assigned sharp observable is a densely defined self-adjoint operator with a declared unit; a nonzero $\psi$ gives a stationary preparation of the autonomous model exactly when it is an eigenvector of the assigned energy observable, and the energy law of a unit eigenvector is the point mass at its eigenvalue ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a), [[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-stationary-states-and-energy-conservation]] clause (c), [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clause (b), [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]).

1.1 [Domain and self-adjointness] By [F1] the operator $A_{\alpha_{g}}$ is self-adjoint on the displayed domain, and $H_{g}=(\hbar^{2}/2m)A_{\alpha_{g}}$ on the same domain; by [F3] with $c=\hbar^{2}/2m>0$, $H_{g}$ is self-adjoint. The domain description is unchanged; the action is the class formed by the two half-line weak second derivatives in [F1], multiplied by $-\hbar^2/(2m)$. These restrictions lie in $L^2$ by the domain condition, so their glued class is in $L^2(\mathbb R)$; no global $L^2$ second derivative is required. This proves (a). [given, F1, F3, algebra]

3.1 [Attractive coupling] Let $g<0$, so that $\alpha_{g}=2mg/\hbar^{2}<0$. By [F2] the unique negative eigenvalue of $A_{\alpha_{g}}$ is $-\alpha_{g}^{2}/4$ with one-dimensional eigenspace spanned by the unit vector $\psi_{\alpha_{g}}$, and [F3] scales the eigenvalue by $c=\hbar^{2}/2m$ while preserving the eigenvector: $E_{g}=c\,(-\alpha_{g}^{2}/4)=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\cdot\frac{1}{4}\bigl(\frac{2mg}{\hbar^{2}}\bigr)^{2}=-\frac{m^{2}g^{2}}{2m\hbar^{2}}=-\frac{mg^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}}$. The eigenfunction is, by [F2], $\psi_{g}(x)=\sqrt{-\alpha_{g}/2}\,e^{\alpha_{g}|x|/2}$ with $-\alpha_{g}/2=m|g|/\hbar^{2}$ and $\alpha_{g}/2=-m|g|/\hbar^{2}$, that is the displayed $\sqrt{m|g|/\hbar^{2}}\,e^{-m|g||x|/\hbar^{2}}$, and it is a unit vector. Since the eigenvectors of $H_{g}$ are exactly those of $A_{\alpha_{g}}$ by [F3], the negative eigenspace of $H_{g}$ is one-dimensional and spanned by $\psi_{g}$; by [F4] the preparation $[\psi_{g}]$ is stationary with energy $E_{g}$ and its energy law is the point mass at $E_{g}$. This is (c). [step 2.1, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

4.1 [Reading and scope] The pair $(H_{g},\mathrm J)$ meets the definition of an assigned sharp observable by steps 1.1 and [F4], with the joule as declared energy unit; the coupling $g$, the interface condition and the absence of an $L^{2}$ potential are the declared model data of clause (d) of [[def-nrqm-potentials-interval-and-delta-models]], and the exclusions of (d) are exactly its recorded scope. [step 1.1, step 3.1, F4] ∎

- **Sign conventions.** The interface condition is
  $u'^{*}(0+)-u'^{*}(0-)=\alpha_{g}u^{*}(0)$ with
  $\alpha_{g}=2mg/\hbar^{2}$, the convention of the cited interface operator;
  with $g<0$ the jump is negative and the single bound state appears. The
  statement makes no claim about any other sign convention or normalization of
  the formal coupling.
- **What is not asserted.** The theorem proves the self-adjointness of the
  declared interface operator and its exact negative spectrum on the line. It
  does not compute transmission or reflection through the interface, does not
  treat the delta interaction on an interval or in higher dimension, and makes
  no empirical claim.

consumer_reviews.snippet:
**(i) Energy operator.** An **isolated autonomous system** of the sector has a declared **energy operator** $H_{\mathrm{op}}:D(H_{\mathrm{op}})\subset H\to H$ that is self-adjoint ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]) and a declared energy unit in which its spectral coordinate is read. The energy operator is part of the model specification of the system; for a massive particle it is fixed by the kinematics postulate P5, and singular or unbounded model Hamiltonians require their own self-adjointness statements.

**(ii) Evolution.** The time evolution of the model is the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group
$$U(t):=\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tH_{\mathrm{op}}\Bigr)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),\qquad U(t+s)=U(t)U(s),\quad U(t)^{*}=U(t)^{-1},$$
defined by the spectral calculus of the self-adjoint generator ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]], [[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]], [[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]). The energy unit enters the argument of the exponential so that $H_{\mathrm{op}}t/\hbar$ acts in the dimensionless spectral variable.

**(iv) Time-dependent families.** A prescribed time-dependent family $t\mapsto H(t)$ of self-adjoint operators is a different model assumption: a norm-continuous finite-dimensional Hermitian family is used only through the unitary two-time propagator that its family defines, and the exponential of the integral of $H(t)$ is not identified with that propagator unless the family commutes with itself at different times. The general unbounded time-dependent case requires a separate existence and domain theorem of its own and is not adopted by this postulate; the driven-dynamics page states its own assumptions for the models it treats.

**(v) Open systems.** A non-unitary evolution of the reduced description of a system coupled to an environment is an extension obtained from an explicitly chosen environment model and a declared reduction, not a replacement for clause (ii); no environment model is adopted by this postulate.

- **Domain matters.** The Schroedinger equation is a statement about vectors in $D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$; for a vector outside the domain only the unitary group acts, and the expression $H_{\mathrm{op}}\psi$ is undefined. Statements about the derivative of expected values require the common-domain hypotheses stated with them.
- **Autonomous only.** An isolated system evolves autonomously; driven evolution is an additional model assumption of the pages that treat it.
- **Units.** The energy unit is declared with the observable; energies and times enter the phase $H_{\mathrm{op}}t/\hbar$ so that the combination is dimensionless in the declared units.

$B\subseteq[0,\infty)$ read in joules the **declared ideal energy-window
detector of window $B$** is the declared ideal sharp measurement with outcome
structure
$$\bigl(E_{H_f}(B),\ I-E_{H_f}(B)\bigr),$$
where $E_{H_f}$ is the spectral projection-valued measure of the assigned
free-field energy observable $(H_f,\mathrm J)$; its **window law** in the
preparation $\rho$ is $p_{B}(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{H_f}(B))$ and its
complement probability is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(I-E_{H_f}(B)))$, the reading
of P2. A finite-resolution detector is described by such a window or by a
declared family of pairwise disjoint windows covering $[0,\infty)$; the
statement that a laboratory spectrometer realizes a declared window, with what
resolution and calibration, is an identification under P7.

consumer_reviews.snippet:
**(a) The quantised-model ratio.** Consider the pure one-photon polarisation
preparation of the ray $[e_{1}]$ and the declared ideal analyser at angle
$\theta$. By
[[pthm-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-polarization-outcome-law]] the outcome law of
the analyser is
$$p_{+1}=\|P_{\theta}e_{1}\|^{2}=\cos^{2}\theta,\qquad p_{-1}=\sin^{2}\theta,$$
so the **transmitted Born probability** is $\cos^{2}\theta$ in the unit $1$ of
dimensionless probabilities.

**(b) The declared classical transverse-amplitude model.** Declare the
following elementary model, with no claim that it is Maxwell theory: its
**field data** are complex vectors $E\in V$ whose coordinates are dimensionless
amplitude ratios relative to one fixed reference amplitude $E_{\mathrm{ref}}$;
no absolute field strength is assigned. The **analyser at angle $\theta$**
acts on the field data by the orthogonal projection
$$E\longmapsto P_{\theta}E;$$
the model's **declared dimensionless relative intensity** of a field datum is
$$I(E):=\|E\|^{2},$$
and the **transmitted intensity fraction** is $I(P_{\theta}E)/I(E)$ for
$E\ne0$.
This is a declared idealisation of the classical description of a
polariser as projecting the transverse field amplitude (the Jones-vector
reading); it imports no Maxwell equation and makes no detector claim.

[L2] **Born law of the analyser.** For the declared analyser and a pure preparation of unit vector $\psi$, the outcome probability is $\|P_{\theta}\psi\|^{2}$ ([[pthm-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-polarization-outcome-law]] clause (c), [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b)).

- **What is compared.** Only the two declared models on the declared
  two-dimensional space are compared. No claim is made that the elementary
  classical model reproduces the photon counting statistics or the
  non-classical states of the radiation sector; the comparison of counting
  statistics is the subject of
  [[ex-nrqm-photons-single-mode-number-statistics-coherent-and-thermal]] and
  [[texp-nrqm-photons-classical-field-and-quantized-detection-comparison]].
- **Sources and status.** The coincidence of the classical transmitted
  fraction with the quantum transmitted probability is explicitly noted in the
  cited source; the classical model here is an elementary declared idealisation
  constructed for the comparison and is not a derivation from Maxwell theory.

consumer_reviews.snippet:
Adopt the observable and probability postulate P2 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], the
autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], and the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5 and internal-factor postulate P6 read
through [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] for a particle
of mass parameter $m>0$ and spin label $s$
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]), and
assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H_{s}$ be the model's
state space with componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$
([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]), let
$\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}$ be the outcome law of an assigned sharp
observable $A$ in a unit vector $\psi$, let
$H_{0}:=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k}P_{k}^{2}$ with domain
$D(H_{0})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ and flow
$U_{0}(t)=\exp(-itH_{0}/\hbar)$, and for real bounded measurable
$V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ let $H_{V}$ and $U_{V}$ be the operator and flow of
[[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-translation-covariance]], with
$D(H_{V})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ and
$V_{u}(x,t):=V(x-ut)$. For $u\in\mathbb R^{3}$ and $t\in\mathbb R$ define the
**boost operator** $B_{u}(t)$ componentwise by
$$\bigl(B_{u}(t)\psi\bigr)(x):=\exp\Bigl(\frac{i}{\hbar}\Bigl(m\,u\cdot x -\frac{m|u|^{2}}{2}t\Bigr)\Bigr)\psi(x-ut).$$
Then:

(a) for every $u,t$ the operator $B_{u}(t)$ is unitary,
$B_{u}(t)^{-1}=B_{u}(t)^{*}$, and it maps $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$
and $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ onto themselves;

(b) $B_{u}(t)D(Q_{j})=D(Q_{j})$ and $B_{u}(t)D(P_{k})=D(P_{k})$; for
$f\in D(Q_{j})$ and $g\in D(P_{k})$, respectively,
$$Q_{j}B_{u}(t)f=B_{u}(t)(Q_{j}+u_{j}tI)f,\qquad P_{k}B_{u}(t)g=B_{u}(t)(P_{k}+mu_{k}I)g.$$
For a Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and
$a\in\mathbb R$, write $B-a:=\{b-a:b\in B\}$. Consequently, for every
unit $\psi$ and Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R$
$$\mu^{Q_{j}}_{B_{u}(t)\psi}(B)=\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(B-u_{j}t),\qquad \mu^{P_{k}}_{B_{u}(t)\psi}(B)=\mu^{P_{k}}_{\psi}(B-mu_{k});$$

(d) **moving-frame bounded-potential model.** For every real bounded
measurable $V$ and every $u$, the two-parameter family
$$W_{u}(t,s):=B_{u}(t)\,U_{V}(t-s)\,B_{u}(s)^{-1}$$
consists of unitaries preserving $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, and
for every $s\in\mathbb R$ and $\psi_{0}\in W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$
the curve $t\mapsto W_{u}(t,s)\psi_{0}$ takes values in $W^{2,2}$, is
differentiable as an $L^{2}$-valued curve and satisfies
$$i\hbar\frac{d}{dt}\psi(t)=\Bigl(\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k}P_{k}^{2}+M_{V_{u}(\cdot,t)}\Bigr)\psi(t),\qquad \psi(s)=\psi_{0};$$
it is unique among maps $w:\mathbb R\to W^{2,2}$ that are differentiable
into $L^{2}$ and satisfy this equation in $L^{2}$ for every $t$ with
$w(s)=\psi_{0}$;

**Given:** The postulates P2, P4, P5 and P6 read through [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]]; the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice; the state space $H_{s}$, $r=2s+1$; the componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$ and their scalar counterparts; the boost operators $B_{u}(t)$; the free energy $H_{0}$; a bounded real measurable $V$ and the operators $H_{V}$, $U_{V}$, $W_{u}(t,s)$; a unit vector $\psi$; a Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$; vectors $u\in\mathbb R^{3}$, $x\in\mathbb R^{3}$; times $s,t$.

[F2] **Componentwise kinematics, momentum representation and laws.** $Q_j,P_k$ are the componentwise operators with their maximal domains and $P_kf=-i\hbar D_kf$ on its domain ([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (a)). The unitary momentum transform $U^{(s)}$ sends $P_k$ to multiplication by $p_k$ with the corresponding domain equality, and sends $T_a$ to multiplication by $e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}$ ([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]] clauses (b),(d)). The spectral measures and outcome laws are those of [[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]] clauses (a),(c).

[F5] **Flows and uniqueness.** $H_{0}$ and $H_{V}$ are self-adjoint on $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ with strongly continuous unitary flows preserving the domain and satisfying the Schroedinger equation exactly on it ([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]] clause (c), [[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-schrodinger-picture-flow]] clauses (a)-(c), [[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]).

1.1 [Unitarity and domain preservation] Write $B_{u}(t)=M_{e^{i\varphi(\cdot,t)}}T_{ut}$ componentwise, where $T_{ut}$ is the componentwise translation and $\varphi(\cdot,t)$ the smooth real phase of [F1]. By [F3] the translation is unitary and preserves $W^{2,2}$ and the Schwartz class; multiplication by the unimodular smooth function $e^{i\varphi}$ is unitary and preserves both classes because the phase is affine with bounded derivatives. Hence $B_{u}(t)$ is unitary with the stated inverse and preserves both classes, componentwise as in the scalar case of [F1]. This proves (a). [F1, F3, algebra]

2.1 [Law transports] For a componentwise representative $f$, $(E_{Q_j}(B)B_u(t)f)(x)=\mathbf 1_B(x_j)e^{i\varphi(x,t)}f(x-ut)$, whereas $(B_u(t)E_{Q_j}(B-u_jt)f)(x)=e^{i\varphi(x,t)}\mathbf 1_{B-u_jt}(x_j-u_jt)f(x-ut)$. Since the two indicators agree, $E_{Q_j}(B)B_u(t)=B_u(t)E_{Q_j}(B-u_jt)$; taking norms gives $\mu^{Q_j}_{B_u(t)\psi}(B)=\mu^{Q_j}_{\psi}(B-u_jt)$. For momentum, changing variables $y=x-ut$ in the Fourier transform first on smooth compactly supported representatives yields $(U^{(s)}B_u(t)f)(p)=e^{-it u\cdot p/\hbar+i m|u|^2t/(2\hbar)}(U^{(s)}f)(p-mu)$. The equality extends to all $L^2$ by density and unitarity. Therefore the indicator $\mathbf 1_B(p_k)$ on the left equals the transported indicator $\mathbf 1_{B-mu_k}(p_k-mu_k)$ on the right, so $E_{P_k}(B)B_u(t)=B_u(t)E_{P_k}(B-mu_k)$ and $\mu^{P_k}_{B_u(t)\psi}(B)=\mu^{P_k}_{\psi}(B-mu_k)$. These are the two law transports in (b); neither depends on the phase in the position density. [step 1.2, step 1.3, F2, F3, algebra]

3.1 [Free covariance] Put $\tau:=t-s$. Under $U^{(s)}$, each $P_k$ is multiplication by $p_k$ ([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]] clause (b)); hence $H_0=(2m)^{-1}\sum_kP_k^2$ is multiplication by $|p|^2/(2m)$ on the transformed $W^{2,2}$ domain, and its spectral-calculus flow $U_0(\tau)$ is multiplication by $e^{-i\tau|p|^2/(2m\hbar)}$ ([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]] clause (b), [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (b)). By the momentum-transform formula of step 2.1, both sides of the free-covariance identity have the same momentum representative because [step 2.1, F2, F5, algebra]
$$e^{-it u\cdot p/\hbar+i m|u|^2t/(2\hbar)}e^{-i\tau|p-mu|^2/(2m\hbar)}=e^{-i\tau|p|^2/(2m\hbar)}e^{-is u\cdot p/\hbar+i m|u|^2s/(2\hbar)},$$
as follows by expanding $|p-mu|^2$ and using $\tau=t-s$. The equality holds on all of $H_s$ because $U^{(s)}$ is unitary and all displayed multipliers are unimodular. [step 2.1, F2, F5, algebra]

consumer_reviews.snippet:
Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero, action constant $\hbar>0$, and a declared potential $V$ of the
**resolvent-tail class**: real $V=V_{2}+V_{\mathrm b}$ with
$V_{2}\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3})$ and $V_{\mathrm b}\in L^{\infty}(\mathbb R^{3})$
real, and, with the model's reference length $L_*$, energy $E_*=\hbar^2/(2mL_*^2)$, dimensionless coordinate $y=x/L_*$, reduced potential $W_*(y)=V(L_*y)/E_*$ and the
nondimensional free operator $A_{0,*}:=-\Delta_y^{\mathrm{weak}}$ of the model,
$$h_*(r):=\bigl\|M_{W_*}(A_{0,*}-iI)^{-1}\mathbf 1_{\{|y|\ge r\}}\bigr\|,$$
finite for every dimensionless $r\ge0$ and in $L^{1}([0,\infty))$.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(b) $S=\Omega_{+}^{*}\Omega_{-}$ is unitary on $H_{0}$;

(c) the conclusions of (a) and (b) hold in particular for a declared potential
of the explicit **decaying-tail form** $V=V_{\mathrm{loc}}+V_{\mathrm{tail}}$
with real $V_{\mathrm{loc}}\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3})$ compactly supported and
$|V_{\mathrm{tail}}(x)|\le C(1+|x|/L_*)^{-1-\delta}$ almost everywhere for some
constants $C>0$ in joules and dimensionless $\delta>0$; here the integrability hypothesis of the preamble
is not presupposed, because the cited theorem supplies it for this form;

[F1] **Spatial and energy scaling.** The model proves that the unitary
$D_*$ maps $W^{2,2}_x$ onto $W^{2,2}_y$ and conjugates the physical pair to
$E_*A_{0,*}$ and $E_*A_*$, where $A_*=A_{0,*}+M_{W_*}$.
The purely mathematical positive-scaling correspondence
[[lem-nrqm-scattering-model-scaling-correspondence]] applies to these
operators with positive scalar $c=E_*$ (its numerical parameters can be
chosen as $\hbar'=1$, $m'=1/(2E_*)$). It gives spectral dilation, preservation
of spectral types and the time change $\tau=tE_*/\hbar=t/T_*$.
Unitary conjugation transports the PVM and the strong limits, so
$E_H(E_*B)=D_*^*E_{A_*}(B)D_*$ and
$\Omega_\pm=D_*^*\Omega_{\pm,*}D_*$; each physical spectral subspace is
$D_*^*$ of the corresponding subspace for $A_*$.

[F2] **Resolvent-tail short-range completeness in dimensionless coordinates.** Assume Countable Choice. For real $V_{0}=V_{0,2}+V_{0,\mathrm b}$ with $V_{0,2}\in L^{2}$, $V_{0,\mathrm b}\in L^{\infty}$ real and $\|M_{V_{0}}(-\Delta-i)^{-1}\mathbf 1_{\{|x|\ge r\}}\|$ finite for every dimensionless $r\ge0$ and integrable over $r\ge0$, the operator $-\Delta+M_{V_{0}}$ on $H^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ is self-adjoint, both ordinary wave operators exist, $H_{\mathrm{sc}}=\{0\}$, $\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{+}=\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{-}=H_{\mathrm{ac}}=H_{\mathrm c}$, and $S=\Omega_{+}^{*}\Omega_{-}$ is unitary; all conclusions hold for $V_{0}=V_{0,\mathrm{loc}}+V_{0,\mathrm{tail}}$ with compactly supported $L^{2}$ part and $|V_{0,\mathrm{tail}}(x)|\le C(1+|x|)^{-1-\delta}$, $\delta>0$ ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-resolvent-tail-short-range-completeness]] clause display and its final paragraph).

**Proof technique:** direct; the class hypothesis is exactly the nondimensional resolvent-tail hypothesis for the reduced potential, so the cited theorem applies, and the scaling correspondence transfers self-adjointness, the limits, the range equalities and the unitarity.

1.1 Put $W_*(y)=V(L_*y)/E_*=W_{*,2}(y)+W_{*,\mathrm b}(y)$. Lebesgue dilation gives $\|W_{*,2}\|_2=E_*^{-1}L_*^{-3/2}\|V_2\|_2$ and $\|W_{*,\mathrm b}\|_\infty=E_*^{-1}\|V_{\mathrm b}\|_\infty$. Thus these parts are real $L^2$ and bounded functions respectively. In [F2] use the dimensionless variable $y$ in place of its abstract variable $x$, $V_0=W_*$ and $A_{0,*}=-\Delta_y^{\mathrm{weak}}$. The full hypothesis is exactly $h_*(r)<\infty$ for every $r$ with $h_*\in L^1$, so [F2] gives self-adjoint $A_*$ on $H^2_y$, isometric wave operators $\Omega_{\pm,*}$, $H_{\mathrm{sc}}(A_*)=0$, equal ranges $H_{\mathrm{ac}}(A_*)=H_{\mathrm c}(A_*)$ and unitary $S_*$. [F1, F2, given, algebra]

1.2 [Failure of the general Coulomb resolvent-tail condition] For the pure Coulomb reduced potential put $W_{*,C}=-\gamma_*/|y|$, $\gamma_*=\kappa/(E_*L_*)>0$. All radii in this argument are dimensionless. Fix by [F4] a nonzero real $\phi\in C_c^\infty(B_R)$, and for $r>R$ set $\phi_r(y)=\phi(y-2r e_1)$ and $f_r=(A_{0,*}-i)\phi_r$. Both are supported outside the radius-$r$ ball, since $2r-R>r$; derivatives do not enlarge support. The free derivative action and translation isometry give $\|\phi_r\|_2=\|\phi\|_2>0$ and $\|f_r\|_2=\|(A_{0,*}-i)\phi\|_2=:c_f>0$. Positivity and self-adjointness of $A_{0,*}$ ensure its resolvent at $i$ exists, and $(A_{0,*}-i)^{-1}\mathbf1_{\{|y|\ge r\}}f_r=\phi_r$. If the Coulomb resolvent-tail operator is not bounded at some radius it already fails the class; otherwise its operator norm obeys $h_{*,C}(r)\ge\frac{\|M_{W_{*,C}}\phi_r\|_2}{\|f_r\|_2}\ge\frac{\gamma_*\|\phi\|_2}{c_f(2r+R)}.$ The last bound uses $|y|\le2r+R$ on that support. The positive lower bound has divergent integral over $r>R$, so $h_{*,C}\notin L^1([0,\infty))$. Thus pure Coulomb fails the general class as well, proving the general-class exclusion in (d) without any zero-energy hypothesis. [F4, given, algebra]

3.1 By [F3] and step 2.1, $S=D_*^*S_*D_*$, which is unitary since $S_*$ and $D_*$ are unitary. This proves (b). [F1, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

consumer_reviews.snippet:
In the one-particle model of [[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]] with potential $V=0$, the free kinetic operators
$$K_{m}:=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta,\qquad D(K_{m})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C),\qquad m>0,$$
have a massless strong-action limit: there exist a self-adjoint operator $K_{0}\ge0$ on $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ with $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)\subseteq D(K_0)$ such that $K_{m}f\to K_{0}f$ in $L^{2}$ for every $f$ in the Schwartz class $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ as $m\downarrow0$, and the formal free-plane-wave frequencies of this massive family have a finite pointwise limit at every fixed nonzero wave vector. Precisely, for $k\in\mathbb R^{3}\setminus\{0\}$ with $[k]=\ell^{-1}$, define $\omega_m(k):=\hbar|k|^{2}/(2m)$ by the plane-wave solution $e^{i(k\cdot x-\omega_m(k)t)}$ of the free equation; the additional claim is that $\lim_{m\downarrow0}\omega_m(k)$ is finite, where $[\omega_m]=\tau^{-1}$ under [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]].

[L4] Frequencies of the free model: for $k\in\mathbb R^{3}$, $\omega\in\mathbb R$, and $[k]=\ell^{-1}$, the smooth formal plane-wave mode $\psi_{k,\omega}(x,t)=e^{i(k\cdot x-\omega t)}$ satisfies $i\hbar\partial_{t}\psi_{k,\omega}=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta\psi_{k,\omega}$ at every point exactly when $\hbar\omega=\frac{\hbar^{2}|k|^{2}}{2m}$, that is $\omega=\frac{\hbar|k|^{2}}{2m}$, because $\partial_{t}\psi_{k,\omega}=-i\omega\psi_{k,\omega}$ and $\Delta\psi_{k,\omega}=-|k|^{2}\psi_{k,\omega}$ and the exponential does not vanish ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]] clause (iv)); the frequency has dimension $\tau^{-1}$ in the conventions of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. For $k\ne0$ this plane wave is not in $L^2(\mathbb R^3)$, so it is a formal mode rather than a normalized state.
