consumer_reviews.snippet:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, read through the oscillator model of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] with parameters $m>0$, $\omega>0$ and action constant $\hbar>0$, and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\ell=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$, let $(g_n)$, $D$, $A$, $(\psi_n)$ and $H_1$ be the Hermite family, the unitary, the dimensionless diagonal operator, the scaled eigenbasis and the energy operator of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clauses (a) and (b), so that $\psi_n=Dg_n$ and $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ is the model's one-dimensional assigned energy observable of the model definition clause (c). Put
$$N_\psi:=DND^{-1},\qquad a_\psi:=DaD^{-1},\qquad a^\dagger_\psi:=Da^\dagger D^{-1},$$
where $N$ is the number operator of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-closed-ladder-domains]] and $N_\psi$ is the assigned excitation-number observable with unit $1/\mathrm{count}$ of the model definition clause (c); these are the number and ladder operators transported from that lemma, with domains $D(N_\psi)=\{Dx:x\in D(N)\}$, $D(a_\psi)=\{Dx:x\in D(a)\}$ and $D(a^\dagger_\psi)=\{Dx:x\in D(a^\dagger)\}$. Write $E_n:=\hbar\omega(n+\tfrac12)$ and, for the three-dimensional realization of the model definition clause (d), let $(H_3,\mathrm J)$ and $(\psi_N)_{N\in\mathbb N^3}$ be its assigned energy observable and its product eigenbasis. Then:

(c) **Energy outcome law.** For every unit $f\in\mathcal H_1$ the outcome law of the assigned energy observable $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ in the pure preparation of $f$ is purely atomic with
$$\mu^{H_1}_f\bigl(\{E_n\}\bigr)=|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}\quad(n\in\mathbb N),\qquad \mu^{H_1}_f(B)=\sum_{n:\,E_n\in B}|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}$$
for every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$, and $\mu^{H_1}_f(\sigma(H_1))=1$; in particular the law has no mass outside $\{E_n:n\in\mathbb N\}$, and $E_n$ is an atom of the law of $f$ exactly when $\langle f,\psi_n\rangle\ne0$;

(d) **Three-dimensional isotropic realization.** The energy observable $(H_3,\mathrm J)$ of the model definition clause (d) has spectrum $\sigma(H_3)=\{\hbar\omega(M+\tfrac32):M\in\mathbb N\}$; for every $M\in\mathbb N$ the eigenspace $\ker(H_3-\hbar\omega(M+\frac32)I)$ has the orthonormal basis $\{\psi_N:N\in\mathbb N^{3},\ n_1+n_2+n_3=M\}$ and dimension $(M+1)(M+2)/2$; the ground energy is $\tfrac32\hbar\omega$;

**Given:** the adopted postulates P1, P2, P4, P5; the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice; the oscillator model of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]]; the Hermite data, the unitary $D$, the diagonal operator $A$, the eigenbasis $(\psi_n)$ and the energy operator $H_1$ of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]]; the closed ladder and number operators of [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-closed-ladder-domains]] and their transports; a unit vector $f\in\mathcal H_1$; a Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$; a nonnegative integer $n$ and a nonnegative integer $M$.

[F1] **The model's assigned observables.** $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ is the model's assigned energy observable, $(Q,\mathrm m)$ and $(P,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1})$ are its assigned position and momentum observables, and $(N_\psi,1/\mathrm{count})$ is its assigned dimensionless excitation-number observable; the flow of the isolated model is $U(t)=\exp(-itH_1/\hbar)$, so $H_1$ is a self-adjoint operator with a spectral projection-valued measure $E_{H_1}$ and outcome law $\mu^{A}_{f}(B)=\|E_A(B)f\|^{2}$ for the assigned observable $(A,u_A)$ in the pure preparation of a unit vector $f$ ([[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clauses (b), (c); [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b); [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clauses (a), (b)).

[F5] **Atoms and support of a spectral law.** For a self-adjoint operator $A$ with spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$: $E_A(\{\lambda\})$ is the orthogonal projection onto $\ker(A-\lambda I)$, so for a unit vector $f$ the law satisfies $\mu^{A}_f(\{\lambda\})=\|E_A(\{\lambda\})f\|^{2}$; and $\mu^{A}_f(B)=\mu^{A}_f(B\cap\sigma(A))$ with $\mu^{A}_f(\sigma(A))=1$ for every Borel $B$, while the scalar law of a pure preparation is a probability measure and is countably additive ([[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a), (b); [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clauses (a), (b); [[pthm-nrqm-observables-born-outcome-law-properties]] clause (a)).

[F6] **The multidimensional theorem.** For the three-dimensional isotropic realization the energy operator $H_3$ of the model definition clause (d) is self-adjoint with the domain and core displayed in [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-multidimensional-oscillator-completeness]] clause (c), and its spectrum is $\{\hbar\omega(M+\frac32):M\in\mathbb N\}$ with the eigenvalue $\hbar\omega(M+\frac32)$ having multiplicity $\binom{M+2}{2}=(M+1)(M+2)/2$ and eigenspace spanned by the orthonormal family $\{\psi_N:\sum_jn_j=M\}$ ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-multidimensional-oscillator-completeness]] clauses (c), (d)).

[F7] **Transport along isometric bijections.** For complex Hilbert spaces $H,K$, a bijective linear isometry $U:H\to K$ and a self-adjoint $T$ on $H$, the operator $UTU^{-1}$ with domain $U D(T)$ is self-adjoint, has the same spectrum as $T$, and satisfies $\mu^{UTU^{-1}}_{Ux}(B)=\mu^{T}_x(B)$ for every unit $x\in H$ and Borel $B$ ([[lem-nrqm-oscillator-unitary-transport-of-spectral-pvms]] clauses (a), (c), (d)).

1.2 [Transported ladder and number operators] The map $D$ is a bijective linear isometry by [F2], and the operators $N_\psi=DND^{-1}$, $a_\psi=DaD^{-1}$, $a^\dagger_\psi=Da^\dagger D^{-1}$ have the transported domains $D(N_\psi)=D\,D(N)$, $D(a_\psi)=D\,D(a)$, $D(a^\dagger_\psi)=D\,D(a^\dagger)$; because $\psi_n=Dg_n$ and $D$ preserves the inner product, the coefficients satisfy $\langle Dx,\psi_n\rangle=\langle x,g_n\rangle$, so by [F3] $D(N_\psi)=\{f:\sum_nn^{2}|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}<\infty\}$ and the identities of [F3] transport: $D(a_\psi a^\dagger_\psi)=D(a^\dagger_\psi a_\psi)=D(N_\psi)$, on which $a^\dagger_\psi a_\psi=N_\psi$ and $a_\psi a^\dagger_\psi=N_\psi+I$, and $N_\psi\psi_n=n\psi_n$, $a_\psi\psi_n=\sqrt n\,\psi_{n-1}$ ($n\ge1$) with $a_\psi\psi_0=0$, $a^\dagger_\psi\psi_n=\sqrt{n+1}\,\psi_{n+1}$. For the non-self-adjoint pair, closedness and the adjoint relations transport by the direct pairing computation: for $x\in D(a_\psi)$ and $y\in D(a^\dagger_\psi)$, $\langle a_\psi x,y\rangle=\langle aD^{-1}x,D^{-1}y\rangle=\langle D^{-1}x,a^\dagger D^{-1}y\rangle=\langle x,a^\dagger_\psi y\rangle$, so $a_\psi\subseteq(a^\dagger_\psi)^{*}$ and $a^\dagger_\psi\subseteq a_\psi^{*}$; and if $x_k\to x$ with $a_\psi x_k\to y$, then $D^{-1}x_k\to D^{-1}x$ and $aD^{-1}x_k=D^{-1}a_\psi x_k\to D^{-1}y$, so closedness of $a$ gives $D^{-1}x\in D(a)$ and $aD^{-1}x=D^{-1}y$, that is $x\in D(a_\psi)$ and $a_\psi x=y$: $a_\psi$ is closed, and the same argument with $a^\dagger$ makes $a^\dagger_\psi$ closed. By [F8], for $y\in\mathcal H_1$, the functional $x\mapsto\langle a_\psi x,y\rangle=\langle aD^{-1}x,D^{-1}y\rangle$ on $D(a_\psi)$ is bounded in the ambient norm exactly when $D^{-1}y\in D(a^*)=D(a^\dagger)$, because $D$ is a surjective isometry between the domains. Thus $D(a_\psi^*)=D\,D(a^\dagger)$ and $a_\psi^*y=Da^*D^{-1}y=a^\dagger_\psi y$; interchanging $a$ and $a^\dagger$ proves the other adjoint equality. By [F7] applied with $U=D$ and $T=N$, the operator $N_\psi$ is self-adjoint with $\sigma(N_\psi)=\sigma(N)=\mathbb N$ and $\mu^{N_\psi}_{Dx}(B)=\mu^{N}_x(B)$ for every unit $x$ and Borel $B$. [given, F2, F3, F7, F8]

1.3 [The three-dimensional realization] By [F6] the spectrum of $H_3$ is $\{\hbar\omega(M+\frac32)\}=\{E^{(3)}_M:M\in\mathbb N\}$, the eigenspace at $E^{(3)}_M$ has the orthonormal basis $\{\psi_N:n_1+n_2+n_3=M\}$ and dimension $(M+1)(M+2)/2$, and the least eigenvalue is $\frac32\hbar\omega$; this is clause (d), whose self-adjointness, domain and core assertions are those of [F6]. [given, F6]

2.2 [Number-operator identity] By steps 1.1 and 1.2, $D(H_1)=\{f:\sum_nn^{2}|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}<\infty\}=D(N_\psi)$ and both operators act diagonally on the family, with $H_1$ having eigenvalues $E_n=\hbar\omega(n+\frac12)$ and $N_\psi$ having eigenvalues $n$; hence $H_1=\hbar\omega(N_\psi+\frac12I)$ with common domain $D(H_1)=D(N_\psi)$. By step 1.2 and [F4] the eigenspaces of $N_\psi$ are $\ker(N_\psi-nI)=\mathbb C\psi_n$, so its eigenvectors are exactly the nonzero multiples of the $\psi_n$, and its spectrum is $\mathbb N$ by [F7]. For the preparation of the unit eigenvector $\psi_n$, [F5] and the eigenspace identity give $\mu^{N_\psi}_{\psi_n}(\{n\})=\|E_{N_\psi}(\{n\})\psi_n\|^{2}=\|\psi_n\|^{2}=1$; since the scalar law of a pure preparation is a probability measure [F5], the law is the point mass $\delta_n$. Together with the ladder actions of step 1.2 this is clause (b). [step 1.1, step 1.2, F4, F5, F7]

3.1 [Atoms of the energy law] By [F1], $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ is an assigned sharp observable of the model whose outcome law in the pure preparation of a unit vector $f$ is $\mu^{H_1}_f(B)=\|E_{H_1}(B)f\|^{2}$. For every $n$, [F4] and step 2.1 give $\ker(H_1-E_nI)=\mathbb C\psi_n$, so the orthogonal projection $E_{H_1}(\{E_n\})$ is the projection onto $\mathbb C\psi_n$ by the first clause of [F5]; for a unit $f$ this gives $\mu^{H_1}_f(\{E_n\})=\|E_{H_1}(\{E_n\})f\|^{2}=|\langle f,\psi_n\rangle|^{2}$. [step 2.1, F1, F5]

5.1 [Status] Clauses (a), (b) and (c) were obtained from the postulates, the adopted model, the scaling theorem, the closed ladder operators and the general spectral law facts; clause (d) from the multidimensional theorem. No measured spectral line, no numerical value of $m$, $\omega$ or $\hbar$, no apparatus model, no selection rule and no transition rate entered, and the identification of a laboratory resonance with an eigenvalue difference is a tested identification under P7, not a consequence of the argument. This is clause (e). [step 1.3, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 4.1] ∎

consumer_reviews.snippet:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2 and the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, read through the one-dimensional oscillator model of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clauses (a), (b), (c), and the coherent-state family of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-states]]; assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $Q$ and $P$ be the model's position and momentum observables with their declared units ($\mathrm m$ and $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$), let $\ell=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$, let $\Delta_{\rho}A$ be the preparation spread of an assigned sharp observable in the reading of [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]], and write $\langle A\rangle_z:=\langle A\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle$ for the model's coherent preparation of label $z$. Then:

(b) **Position-momentum relation of the model.** Every unit vector $f\in D(Q)\cap D(P)$ satisfies
$$\Delta_{f}Q\,\Delta_{f}P\ge\frac{\hbar}{2},$$
read in the product unit $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{2}\mathrm s^{-1}$; consequently the value $\hbar/2$ attained in (a) is the minimum over the common domain, and it is attained by every coherent preparation;

**Given:** the adopted postulates P1, P2, P5; the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice; the one-dimensional oscillator model with parameters $m,\omega,\hbar>0$ and length $\ell$; the coherent states $\Psi_z$; a unit vector $f\in D(Q)\cap D(P)$; a complex number $z$.

[F2] **Coherent data.** For every $z$: $\Psi_z$ is a unit vector with $a_\psi\Psi_z=z\Psi_z$ and $\Psi_z\in D(N_\psi^{k})$ for every $k$; $\langle\Psi_z,\Psi_w\rangle=e^{-(|z|^{2}+|w|^{2})/2+z\overline w}$; and $\Psi_0=\psi_0$ ([[def-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-states]] clauses (b), (c); [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-state-convergence]] clauses (a), (b), (c), (d), (e)).

[F3] **Exact coherent quantities.** With $Q$ and $P$ the position and momentum operators on $L^{2}(\mathbb R,dx)$ and $a_\psi=DaD^{-1}$, $a^\dagger_\psi=Da^\dagger D^{-1}$ the transported ladder operators,
$$Q\Psi_z=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2}\bigl(a_\psi+a^\dagger_\psi\bigr)\Psi_z,\qquad P\Psi_z=\frac{\hbar}{i\ell\sqrt2}\bigl(a_\psi-a^\dagger_\psi\bigr)\Psi_z,$$
and the quadratic-form means and variances of the coherent vectors are
$$\langle Q\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle=\sqrt2\,\ell\operatorname{Re}z,\qquad\langle P\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle=\frac{\sqrt2\,\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}z,$$
$$\|(Q-\langle Q\rangle_zI)\Psi_z\|^{2}=\frac{\ell^{2}}{2},\qquad\|(P-\langle P\rangle_zI)\Psi_z\|^{2}=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2\ell^{2}};$$
and $\|a_\psi\Psi_z\|^{2}=|z|^{2}$, $\|a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z\|^{2}=|z|^{2}+1$; also the adjoint relation $(a_\psi)^{*}=a^\dagger_\psi$ holds, the transport of $a^{*}=a^\dagger$ along the unitary $D$ ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-evolution-and-variance]] clauses (d), (e); [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-state-convergence]] clause (e); [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-closed-ladder-domains]] clauses (b), (d), (e)).

[F4] **Means, variances and spreads.** For an assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ and a unit vector $f\in D(A)$ the mean and second moment of the outcome law exist, $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_f=\langle Af,f\rangle$, $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_f=\|Af\|^{2}$, and the preparation variance and spread are
$$\operatorname{Var}_{f}(A)=\|(A-\langle Af,f\rangle I)f\|^{2},\qquad \Delta_{f}A=\operatorname{Var}_{f}(A)^{1/2},$$
read in the unit $u_A$ and its square ([[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]] clauses (a), (b); [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]] clauses (b), (c), (d)).

[F5] **Product domain and commutator in one dimension.** For $d=1$, $r=1$ the product domain is $D(QP)\cap D(PQ)=\{f:D_xf,xf,xD_xf\in L^{2}\}$ and $(QP-PQ)\varphi=i\hbar\varphi$ for every $\varphi$ in it ([[lem-nrqm-uncertainty-product-domain-commutator-identity]] clauses (b), (c)).

[F6] **Robertson relation.** For two assigned sharp observables $(A,u_A)$, $(B,u_B)$ and a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)\cap D(B)$: $\Delta_{\psi}A\Delta_{\psi}B\ge|\operatorname{Im}\langle A\psi,B\psi\rangle|$; and if in addition $\psi\in D(AB)\cap D(BA)$, then $\Delta_{\psi}A\Delta_{\psi}B\ge\frac12|\langle[A,B]\psi,\psi\rangle|$ ([[pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-robertson-relation]] clauses (a), (b)).

[F7] **Approximation by product-domain vectors.** For every nonzero $f\in D(Q)\cap D(P)$ there is a sequence of unit vectors $\varphi_k\in D(QP)\cap D(PQ)$ with $\varphi_k\to f/\|f\|$, $Q\varphi_k\to Qf/\|f\|$, $P\varphi_k\to Pf/\|f\|$, and with $\langle Q\varphi_k,\varphi_k\rangle\to\langle Qf,f\rangle/\|f\|^{2}$, $\|Q\varphi_k\|\to\|Qf\|/\|f\|$, and the analogous momentum limits ([[lem-nrqm-uncertainty-approximation-by-product-domain-vectors]]).

[F8] **Inner-product calculus and Cauchy-Schwarz.** The pairing is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second, $\|u\|^{2}=\langle u,u\rangle$, $|\langle u,v\rangle|\le\|u\|\,\|v\|$ with equality if and only if $u,v$ are linearly dependent, and inner products and norms are continuous for norm convergence ([[def-inner-product-space]], [[def-hilbert-space]], [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-for-real-and-complex-inner-product-spaces]]).

1.1 [The model's operators and the coherent formulas] By [F1] the model's $Q$, $P$ are the $d=1$, $r=1$ componentwise operators with the displayed dense domains, and both are assigned sharp observables; by [F2] each $\Psi_z$ is a unit vector with $a_\psi\Psi_z=z\Psi_z$, $\|a_\psi\Psi_z\|^{2}=|z|^{2}$ and $\|a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z\|^{2}=|z|^{2}+1$. By [F3] the vectors $Q\Psi_z=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2}(a_\psi+a^\dagger_\psi)\Psi_z$ and $P\Psi_z=\frac{\hbar}{i\ell\sqrt2}(a_\psi-a^\dagger_\psi)\Psi_z$ lie in $\mathcal H_1$, so $\Psi_z\in D(Q)\cap D(P)$, and the displayed coherent means and central norms hold. [given, F1, F2, F3]

1.2 [Spreads as centered norms] Let $f\in D(Q)\cap D(P)$ be a unit vector. By [F4] applied to the assigned observables $(Q,\mathrm m)$ and $(P,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1})$, the outcome-law means and variances exist and $\Delta_{f}Q^{2}=\|(Q-\langle Qf,f\rangle I)f\|^{2}=\|Qf\|^{2}-\langle Qf,f\rangle^{2}$, and likewise $\Delta_{f}P^{2}=\|Pf\|^{2}-\langle Pf,f\rangle^{2}$. [given, F4]

1.3 [Bound on the product domain] Let $\varphi\in D(QP)\cap D(PQ)$ be a unit vector. By [F5], $(QP-PQ)\varphi=i\hbar\varphi$, so $\langle[Q,P]\varphi,\varphi\rangle=\langle i\hbar\varphi,\varphi\rangle=i\hbar\langle\varphi,\varphi\rangle=i\hbar$ by linearity of the pairing in its first argument. By the Robertson form of [F6] applied to the assigned sharp observables $(Q,\mathrm m)$ and $(P,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1})$, $\Delta_{\varphi}Q\Delta_{\varphi}P\ge\frac12|i\hbar|=\hbar/2$. [given, F5, F6]

1.4 [Approximating a common-domain vector] Let $f\in D(Q)\cap D(P)$ be a unit vector. By [F7] there is a sequence of unit vectors $\varphi_k\in D(QP)\cap D(PQ)$ with $\varphi_k\to f$, $Q\varphi_k\to Qf$, $P\varphi_k\to Pf$, $\langle Q\varphi_k,\varphi_k\rangle\to\langle Qf,f\rangle$, $\|Q\varphi_k\|\to\|Qf\|$ and the analogous momentum limits. [given, F7]

2.1 [Clause (a)] By step 1.1 and step 1.2 applied to the unit vector $\Psi_z\in D(Q)\cap D(P)$, the preparation variances are the central squared norms of [F3]: $\operatorname{Var}_{\Psi_z}(Q)=\|(Q-\langle Q\rangle_zI)\Psi_z\|^{2}=\ell^{2}/2$ and $\operatorname{Var}_{\Psi_z}(P)=\hbar^{2}/(2\ell^{2})$; taking square roots gives $\Delta_{\Psi_z}Q=\ell/\sqrt2$ and $\Delta_{\Psi_z}P=\hbar/(\ell\sqrt2)$, whose product is $\hbar/2$ in the unit $\mathrm m\cdot\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}=\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{2}\mathrm s^{-1}$. [step 1.1, step 1.2, F3]

2.2 [Clause (b), relation] Let $f\in D(Q)\cap D(P)$ be a unit vector and let $(\varphi_k)$ be the approximating sequence of step 1.4. For every $k$, step 1.3 gives $\Delta_{\varphi_k}Q\Delta_{\varphi_k}P\ge\hbar/2$; by step 1.2, $\Delta_{\varphi_k}Q^{2}=\|Q\varphi_k\|^{2}-\langle Q\varphi_k,\varphi_k\rangle^{2}$, and the limits of step 1.4 together with the continuity of the inner product [F8] give $\Delta_{\varphi_k}Q^{2}\to\|Qf\|^{2}-\langle Qf,f\rangle^{2}=\Delta_{f}Q^{2}$, and likewise $\Delta_{\varphi_k}P^{2}\to\Delta_{f}P^{2}$. Taking square roots and passing to the limit in the inequality gives $\Delta_{f}Q\Delta_{f}P\ge\hbar/2$. [step 1.2, step 1.3, step 1.4, F8]

3.1 [Clause (c), saturation] Fix $z$ and put $u:=(a_\psi+a^\dagger_\psi)\Psi_z$, $v:=(a_\psi-a^\dagger_\psi)\Psi_z$, both in $\mathcal H_1$ by step 1.1. Using the conjugate-linearity in the second argument, the coherent data $a_\psi\Psi_z=z\Psi_z$ and the adjoint relation $(a_\psi)^{*}=a^\dagger_\psi$ of [F2] and [F3], so that $\langle a_\psi\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle=z$, $\langle\Psi_z,a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z\rangle=\langle a_\psi\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle=z$ and $\langle a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle=\overline z$, together with $\|\Psi_z\|=1$ and $\|a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z\|^{2}=|z|^{2}+1$, the four pairings are $\langle a_\psi\Psi_z,a_\psi\Psi_z\rangle=|z|^{2}$, $\langle a_\psi\Psi_z,a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z\rangle=z\langle\Psi_z,a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z\rangle=z^{2}$, $\langle a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z,a_\psi\Psi_z\rangle=\overline z\langle a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle=\overline z^{2}$ and $\langle a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z,a^\dagger_\psi\Psi_z\rangle=|z|^{2}+1$, so $\langle u,v\rangle=|z|^{2}-z^{2}+\overline z^{2}-(|z|^{2}+1)=\overline z^{2}-z^{2}-1$; hence, using the first formula of [F3] and $\overline{\hbar/(i\ell\sqrt2)}=i\hbar/(\ell\sqrt2)$, $\langle Q\Psi_z,P\Psi_z\rangle=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2}\cdot\frac{i\hbar}{\ell\sqrt2}\langle u,v\rangle=\frac{i\hbar}{2}\bigl(\overline z^{2}-z^{2}-1\bigr)=2\hbar\operatorname{Re}z\operatorname{Im}z-\frac{i\hbar}{2}$, because $\overline z^{2}-z^{2}=(\overline z-z)(\overline z+z)=-4i\operatorname{Re}z\operatorname{Im}z$. By [F3], $\langle Q\rangle_z\langle P\rangle_z=\sqrt2\ell\operatorname{Re}z\cdot\frac{\sqrt2\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}z=2\hbar\operatorname{Re}z\operatorname{Im}z$, so $\langle x_z,y_z\rangle=\langle Q\Psi_z,P\Psi_z\rangle-\langle Q\rangle_z\langle P\rangle_z=-\frac{i\hbar}{2}$. Therefore $\operatorname{Re}\langle x_z,y_z\rangle=0$ and $|\langle x_z,y_z\rangle|=\hbar/2$, while step 2.1 gives $\|x_z\|\,\|y_z\|=\Delta_{\Psi_z}Q\,\Delta_{\Psi_z}P=\hbar/2$, so equality holds in the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality of [F8] and $x_z,y_z$ are linearly dependent. [step 1.1, step 2.1, F3, F8]

3.2 [Clause (b), minimality] By step 2.2 every unit vector in $D(Q)\cap D(P)$ has spread product at least $\hbar/2$, and by step 2.1 every coherent preparation attains the value $\hbar/2$; hence the minimum of the spread product over the unit vectors of the common domain is $\hbar/2$, attained by each $[\Psi_z]$. [step 2.1, step 2.2]

[[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] for the mode models
declared below, the state and probability postulates P1, P2
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]) in the readings of

[[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]], and the
identical-particle and spin postulate P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]); assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Temperatures are assigned as in
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]], so that
$\beta=1/(k_BT)$ in $\mathrm J^{-1}$. Declare the occupation readouts as assigned sharp observables $(N,1)$ and $(N_-,1)$, with unit particle-count, which is dimensionless. The total particle-number operator $\mathcal N$ in the countable-mode reading has the same unit; every occupation mean and higher number moment below is read in the corresponding dimensionless count unit. Then:

(a) *single bosonic mode*: let $F(\mathbb C)$ be the one-mode Fock space with
number operator $N$ and orthonormal number basis $(e_n)$
([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-mode-number-law]],
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-number-operator-domain]]), let
$\varepsilon>0$ and let the model declare the energy operator $H:=\varepsilon N$
on $F(\mathbb C)$; the model's canonical preparation at temperature $T$ is
$\rho_\beta=e^{-\beta H}/Z$ with $Z=(1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon})^{-1}$, the
number readout $N$ is an assigned sharp observable with finite thermal mean
$$\langle N\rangle_\beta=\frac1{e^{\beta\varepsilon}-1}=\frac1{e^{\varepsilon/(k_BT)}-1},$$
and all moments $\langle N^k\rangle_\beta$, $k\ge1$, are finite;

(e) *scope*: clauses (a)-(d) are conditional statements about the declared
mode models together with the adopted ensemble assignment; they assert no
thermodynamic limit, no continuum of radiation modes, no Bose-Einstein
condensation, no measured occupation number, and no thermalisation of a
sample. All numerical equalities are exact identities of the declared
finite-mode (or product) models at the assigned temperature.

**Given:** the mode models of the statement with their energies, the assigned temperature $T$ and inverse temperature $\beta=1/(k_BT)$, and the adopted canonical preparations.

[F2] **Fermionic and grand-canonical formulas.** For $\beta>0$, $(\varepsilon_j)\subseteq(0,\infty)$ and $\mu\in\mathbb R$, with $q_j=e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_j-\mu)}$: the two-dimensional occupation operator $N_-$ on $\mathbb C^2$ has $Z=1+e^{-\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)}$ and mean occupancy $1/(e^{\beta(\varepsilon_1-\mu)}+1)$; the products $Z_{\mathrm B}=\sup_N\prod_{j\in N}(1-q_j)^{-1}$ and $Z_{\mathrm F}=\sup_N\prod_{j\in N}(1+q_j)$ are finite exactly under the stated summability and positivity conditions; and the single-mode dilute identities and remainder bounds hold, all as statements about diagonal weights ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fermion-and-dilute-grand-canonical-formulas]] clauses (a)-(c)).

2.1 [Readings] In each case the occupation number is an assigned sharp observable by [F4], so the mean of its outcome law in the canonical preparation is the number computed in steps 1.1-1.3; the identification of the computed parameters with a physical temperature and chemical potential is the adopted assumption of the ensemble postulate, and no convergence statement beyond the displayed criteria is asserted. This gives the readings of (a)-(d). [F4, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, algebra]

3.1 [Conclusion and scope] Steps 1.1-1.3 and 2.1 prove (a)-(d). The argument is a finite-mode or product computation at assigned temperature; no thermodynamic limit, continuum of modes, condensation or measured occupation entered, which is (e). [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 2.1] ∎

- **No continuum claim.** The product criterion covers countably many discrete modes; a continuum of radiation modes has divergent free partition function by the cited one-particle non-compactness argument, so a finite-volume or cutoff model would be required before making a continuum thermal claim.
- **The chemical potential.** $\mu$ is an assigned model parameter in joules with its uncertainty; the bosonic condition $\varepsilon_j-\mu>0$ is required for each geometric factor, while the fermionic factors are finite for every real $\mu$.

consumer_reviews.snippet:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]), the radiation extension
postulate
([[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]]),
the radiation sector definition
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]] and
the declared ideal counting model
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-ideal-counting-and-detection-model]]. Assume the
Axioms of Countable Choice, Dependent Choice and Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a unit mode vector $\varphi\in\mathfrak h$ with
coordinate representatives in $\mathrm m^{3/2}$ under $d^{3}k$ by clause (b)
of [[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]];
write $U=U_\varphi$ for the fixed-mode isometry of
[[lem-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-number-isometry]] and let the dimensionless label
$z\in\mathbb C$ and a
**declared effective mode energy** $\varepsilon_{0}>0$ in joules (equivalently a
declared effective frequency $\omega_{0}=\varepsilon_{0}/\hbar>0$ in
$\mathrm s^{-1}$) be given parameters of this example. The example compares the
count statistics of the following three **declared preparations** of the mode
subspace, all read with the declared ideal total-number detector:

**(b) The mode-coherent state.** The pure preparation of the ray of
$U\psi_{z}$, with dimensionless coherent-state label $z$ and
$\psi_{z}=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\sum_{m}\frac{z^{m}}{\sqrt{m!}}e_{m}$.

**Given:** The declared mode data: unit $\varphi\in\mathfrak h$, the isometry $U$, dimensionless label $z\in\mathbb C$, energy $\varepsilon_{0}>0$ joules, inverse-energy parameter $\beta>0$ in $\mathrm J^{-1}$, and the three preparations (a)-(c).

[L1] **Mode transfer and number law.** $Ue_{m}=\varphi^{\otimes m}$ are orthonormal unit vectors with $NUe_{m}=m\,Ue_{m}$, the count law of a preparation of $Ue_{m}$ is $\delta_{m}$, the count law of the mode-coherent preparation is $e^{-|z|^{2}}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!}$ with mean and variance $|z|^{2}$, and $\|\psi_{z}\|=1$ ([[pthm-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-number-and-energy-statistics]] clauses (a),(b), [[lem-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-number-isometry]] clauses (a),(b), [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-mode-number-law]] clause (b)).

[L4] **States.** The rank-one operators $T_{u,u}$ of unit vectors are states, and a trace-norm convergent convex combination of states with weights $(1-q)q^{n}$, $\sum_{n}(1-q)q^{n}=1$, is a state ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]).

[L5] **Free-energy multiplier calculus, products and logarithm.** The free energy is the self-adjoint direct sum of the sector multipliers $\varepsilon_n=\sum_i\varepsilon(k_i)$, with the exact multiplication domains ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]], clauses (a)-(c)). The symmetric transverse sector embeddings and projections are constructed in [[lem-nrqm-photons-transverse-fock-total-momentum]], proof1.1-2.1; scalar multiplier spectral PVMs are inverse-image indicators ([[lem-nrqm-observables-l2-multiplication-spectral-measure]], clauses (b),(c)), and the regular spectral representation of a self-adjoint operator is unique ([[lem-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-cc-arbitrary-hilbert-spectral-calculus]], Statement). Finite product tensor inner products are the Euclidean product integrals ([[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]], Statement). The real logarithm is the inverse of the real exponential, which is strictly increasing with value one at zero ([[def-natural-logarithm]], [[thm-exponential-is-strictly-increasing]], Statement).

1.4 [Geometric moments] Put $p_{n}=(1-q)q^{n}$ with $0<q<1$. By [L3], $\sum_{n\ge1}n\,q^{n}=\sum_{k\ge1}\sum_{n\ge k}q^{n}=\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{q^{k}}{1-q}=\frac{q}{(1-q)^{2}}$, and likewise $\sum_{n\ge2}n(n-1)q^{n}=2\sum_{k\ge2}(k-1)\frac{q^{k}}{1-q}=\frac{2q^{2}}{(1-q)^{3}}$. Hence the mean, second moment and variance of the count law are $$\sum_{n}n\,p_{n}=\frac{q}{1-q}=\frac{1}{e^{\beta\varepsilon_{0}}-1},\qquad \sum_{n}n^{2}p_{n}=\frac{q(1+q)}{(1-q)^{2}},\qquad \operatorname{Var}=\frac{q}{(1-q)^{2}}=\frac{e^{\beta\varepsilon_{0}}}{(e^{\beta\varepsilon_{0}}-1)^{2}},$$ the variance formula from $\sum n^{2}p_{n}=2\sum_{n\ge2}\binom n2q^{n}(1-q)+\sum n p_{n}$ combined with the two sums above; in particular the variance equals $m(m+1)$ for the mean $m=(e^{\beta\varepsilon_{0}}-1)^{-1}$. [L3, algebra]

3.1 [Concluding comparison] The computations show: the $n$-quanta mode state has the sharp count $n$; the mode-coherent state has the Poisson count law with mean and variance $|z|^{2}$; and the declared effective-energy preparation with parameter $\varepsilon_{0}>0$ has the geometric law with mean $1/(e^{\beta\varepsilon_{0}}-1)$ and variance $m(m+1)$. The parameter $\varepsilon_{0}$ is declared; it is not derived from $\varphi$, because no normalisable mode vector has sharp energy. No measurement, sampling model or temperature identification occurs, and the comparison is a comparison of the declared conditional models, which is the announced computation. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 1.4, step 2.1]

- **Independent effective-energy assignment and Gibbs compression.** The
  example independently declares $\varepsilon_0$; a normalisable mode is not
  an eigenmode of the free energy, so the free Hamiltonian does not restrict
  to $\varepsilon_0N'$ on this mode subspace. Nevertheless a compression of
  its bounded Gibbs operator is possible. Put
  $a_\beta:=\langle e^{-\beta\varepsilon}\varphi,\varphi\rangle$.
  Since $0<e^{-\beta\varepsilon(k)}<1$ off the null set $\{k=0\}$ and
  $\|\varphi\|=1$, $0<a_\beta<1$. The sector multiplier representation of
  [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]]
  gives $e^{-\beta T_n}=M_{\prod_i e^{-\beta\varepsilon(k_i)}}$ on the
  symmetric transverse sector. Its pairing on $\varphi^{\otimes n}$ is
  $a_\beta^n$ by the finite-product inner-product integral of [[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]], and different sectors have zero cross
  pairing. Hence $U^*e^{-\beta H_f}U$ is the diagonal operator with entries
  $a_\beta^n$; its trace is $(1-a_\beta)^{-1}$ and its normalization gives
  the geometric weights $(1-a_\beta)a_\beta^n$. At each fixed $\beta$ these
  correspond to the effective scale
  $\varepsilon_{\rm eff}(\beta)=-\beta^{-1}\log a_\beta>0$, with
  the real logarithm of [[def-natural-logarithm]]; positivity follows because the exponential is strictly increasing with $\exp(0)=1$ ([[thm-exponential-is-strictly-increasing]]). The scale is generally
  dependent on $\beta$. This is compression and normalization of a positive
  operator, not a normalized Gibbs state of the full continuum or an
  invariant free-energy mode. The full Gibbs operator remains non-trace-class
  by clause (e) of
  [[pthm-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-number-and-energy-statistics]]; no
  thermalisation or temperature identification follows.
- **Counts are model quanta.** All three laws are laws of the declared ideal
  total-number detector; a laboratory photon-counting comparison would require
  a declared counter response, efficiency and sampling model, and reported
  data. None is supplied or assumed here.

Adopt P1, P2, P4 and P7 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]], work in the
**two-site bond model** of
[[ex-nrqm-many-body-two-site-bond-thermal-ensemble]] with coupling $t>0$,
sites $|1\rangle,|2\rangle$, bond Hamiltonian
$h=-t(T_{|1\rangle,|2\rangle}+T_{|2\rangle,|1\rangle})$ and eigenbasis
$u_-=(|1\rangle+|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$, $u_+=(|1\rangle-|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$ with $hu_\mp=\mp tu_\mp$, and adopt
the canonical equilibrium postulate
[[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] at assigned
temperature $T>0$, $\beta=1/(k_BT)$. Consider the hypothetical declared
preparation $\rho(0):=T_{|1\rangle,|1\rangle}$ (the particle localised at
site $1$) evolving by $\rho(\tau)=U(\tau)\rho(0)U(\tau)^*$ with
$U(\tau)=\exp(-i\tau h/\hbar)$. Then:

(a) $\rho(0)\ne\rho_\beta$, and for every $\tau\in\mathbb R$ one has
$\rho(\tau)\ne\rho_\beta$: the unitary evolution of the model never produces
the canonical preparation from this preparation;

(b) the site-$1$ occupation readout $(P_1,1)$ with $P_1:=T_{|1\rangle,|1\rangle}$, assigned in the dimensionless particle-count unit, has the
exact mean
$$\langle P_1\rangle(\tau)=\cos^2\!\Bigl(\frac{t\tau}{\hbar}\Bigr),$$
and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta P_1)=1/2$; in particular
$\langle P_1\rangle(0)=1\ne1/2$, so at the initial time the readout does not
take its canonical mean;

[F4] **Invariance statement.** In the finite-sector class, if $\rho(0)\ne\rho_\beta$ then $\rho(\tau)\ne\rho_\beta$ for every $\tau$ ([[pthm-nrqm-many-body-unitary-evolution-preserves-entropy]] clause (c)).

1.1 [The evolved preparation and the site readout] With $\psi_0=|1\rangle=(u_-+u_+)/\sqrt2$, [F1] gives $\psi(\tau)=U(\tau)\psi_0=(e^{i\theta}u_-+e^{-i\theta}u_+)/\sqrt2$, where $\theta:=t\tau/\hbar$; by [F2] and $u_-=(|1\rangle+|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$, $u_+=(|1\rangle-|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$ this equals $\cos\theta\,|1\rangle+i\sin\theta\,|2\rangle$, a unit vector. Since $T_{|1\rangle,|1\rangle}=\tfrac12(I+\sigma_z)$ with $\sigma_z=T_{|1\rangle,|1\rangle}-T_{|2\rangle,|2\rangle}$, and $\sigma_z\psi(\tau)=\cos\theta\,|1\rangle-i\sin\theta\,|2\rangle$, the site-occupation mean is $\langle P_1\rangle(\tau)=|\cos\theta|^2=\cos^2\theta=\cos^2(t\tau/\hbar)$, in particular $\langle P_1\rangle(0)=1$. [F1, F2, algebra]

- **What the scenario shows.** The preparation never equals the canonical
  one, yet the site-occupation readout has the same mean $1/2$ as the
  canonical preparation at the times when $\cos^2(t\tau/\hbar)=1/2$; the
  energy readout meanwhile never takes its canonical mean. Readout
  coincidence is therefore not state convergence, and different readouts
  behave differently under the same unitary flow.
- **Hypothetical status.** No apparatus, sampling or detection model is
  specified; the scenario is a conditional statement about the declared
  model, and any comparison with an experiment would require the declared
  preparation, isolation, detection and sampling models of P7.

consumer_reviews.snippet:
**(ii) Pure preparations.** A **pure preparation** of the system is a unit ray $[\psi]=\{z\psi:z\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}\}$ of a vector $\psi\in H$ with $\|\psi\|=1$; that is, two nonzero vectors describe the same pure preparation exactly when they differ by a nonzero complex factor. The zero vector is not a state and no preparation is assigned to it: the normalization $\|\psi\|=1$ is part of the assignment. The ray allows arbitrary nonzero rescaling; between unit representatives the factor has modulus one and is a **global phase**, which has no observable consequence (P2). The rank-one operator $T_{\psi,\psi}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] is the density operator associated with the ray of $\psi$.

**(iv) Composition.** Two independent distinguishable subsystems with state spaces $H_{A}$ and $H_{B}$ are composed by the completed Hilbert tensor product $H_{A}\widehat\otimes H_{B}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]. Product preparations $\psi_{A}\otimes\psi_{B}$ are simple tensors and are the special case in which each subsystem has its own specified preparation. Their finite linear span is dense in $H_{A}\widehat\otimes H_{B}$ by the construction; a pure composite preparation may be any unit ray in this completion, including a norm limit of finite linear combinations of product vectors, and need not factor. General composite preparations are density operators on this space and include the statistical mixtures of clause (iii). A quantity of subsystem $A$ alone is represented on the composite by an operator of the form $A\otimes I_{B}$ and a quantity of $B$ alone by $I_{A}\otimes B$, in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] (bounded case; unbounded local operators are treated where they occur). The existence of the completed tensor product is mathematics; the assignment of that product to a composite physical system is the physical assumption here.

consumer_reviews.snippet:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2 and the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, read through the one-dimensional oscillator model of [[def-nrqm-oscillator-framework-quadratic-potential-model]] clauses (a), (b), (c), and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\psi_0$ be the ground eigenvector of the model's energy operator $H_1$, let $\ell=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$, and let $Q$, $P$ be the model's position and momentum observables. Then:

(a) the class $\psi_0$ has the representative
$$\psi_0(x)=\ell^{-1/2}\pi^{-1/4}e^{-x^{2}/(2\ell^{2})},$$
it is a unit vector, it is the model's coherent state of label $0$, and $H_1\psi_0=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\psi_0$;

(b) the position outcome law of the assigned observable $(Q,\mathrm m)$ in the ground preparation has the density
$$f(x)=\ell^{-1}\pi^{-1/2}e^{-x^{2}/\ell^{2}},$$
with $\int_{\mathbb R}f=1$, mean $0$ and second moment $\ell^{2}/2$; hence $\Delta_{\psi_0}Q=\ell/\sqrt2$;

(c) the momentum outcome law of the assigned observable $(P,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1})$ has the density
$$g(p)=\frac{\ell}{\hbar\sqrt\pi}e^{-\ell^{2}p^{2}/\hbar^{2}},$$
with $\int_{\mathbb R}g=1$, mean $0$ and second moment $\hbar^{2}/(2\ell^{2})$; hence $\Delta_{\psi_0}P=\hbar/(\ell\sqrt2)$;

[F1] **The ground vector from the scaling theorem.** With $g_0(y)=\pi^{-1/4}e^{-y^{2}/2}$ and $D$ the scaling unitary of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]], one has $\psi_0=Dg_0$, $\psi_0(x)=\ell^{-1/2}g_0(x/\ell)=\ell^{-1/2}\pi^{-1/4}e^{-x^{2}/(2\ell^{2})}$, $\|\psi_0\|=1$, and $H_1\psi_0=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\psi_0$; moreover $\psi_0=\Psi_0$ is the coherent state of label $0$ ([[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] clauses (a), (b); [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-hermite-recurrence]] clause (a); [[def-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-states]] clause (c); [[pthm-nrqm-oscillator-energy-spectrum-and-completeness]] clause (a)).

[F3] **Heat kernel and its moments.** For $t>0$ and $n=1$, $\Gamma(x,t)=(4\pi t)^{-1/2}e^{-x^{2}/(4t)}$ satisfies $\int\Gamma(x,t)dx=1$, and all first and second moments are absolutely integrable with $\int x\Gamma(x,t)dx=0$ and $\int x^{2}\Gamma(x,t)dx=2t$ ([[def-heat-kernel]], [[lem-heat-kernel-normalisation-scaling-and-derivatives]] clause (i), [[lem-first-and-second-moments-of-the-heat-kernel]]).

[F4] **The momentum law.** $\mathcal F_2(P\psi)(\xi)=2\pi\hbar\,\xi\,\mathcal F_2\psi(\xi)$ for $\psi\in D(P)$, and $D(P)=\{\psi:\xi\mathcal F_2\psi\in L^{2}\}$; with $g(\xi):=2\pi\hbar\xi$ and $M_g$ the multiplication operator on $L^{2}(\mathbb R,d\xi)$ one has $P=\mathcal F_2^{-1}M_g\mathcal F_2$ with $D(P)=\mathcal F_2^{-1}D(M_g)$, so by the transport lemma the spectral projection-valued measure of $P$ is $E_P(B)=\mathcal F_2^{-1}E_{M_g}(B)\mathcal F_2$ and, for a unit $\psi$, $\mu^{P}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{M_g}(B)\mathcal F_2\psi\|^{2}$; the multiplication lemma applied to $M_g$ gives $E_{M_g}(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{g^{-1}(B)}}$ and $\mu^{P}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{g^{-1}(B)}|\mathcal F_2\psi(\xi)|^{2}\,d\xi$ ([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (b) at $d=1$, $r=1$; [[lem-nrqm-oscillator-unitary-transport-of-spectral-pvms]] clauses (b), (c); [[lem-nrqm-observables-l2-multiplication-spectral-measure]] clauses (b), (c)).

[F6] **Means, variances and spreads.** For an assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ and a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the outcome-law mean and second moment exist and equal $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$, and the preparation spread is the square root of the outcome-law variance $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}d\mu^{A}_{\psi}$; for the coherent preparations of the model the identity $\Delta Q\,\Delta P=\hbar/2$ is known ([[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]] clauses (a), (b); [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]] clauses (b), (c); [[pthm-nrqm-oscillator-coherent-state-fluctuations]] clause (a)).

1.3 [The momentum law] By [F4] and [F5], for every Borel $B$ the momentum law is $\mu^{P}_{\psi_0}(B)=\int_{g^{-1}(B)}|\mathcal F_2\psi_0(\xi)|^{2}d\xi=\int_B(2\pi\hbar)^{-1}|\mathcal F_2\psi_0(p/(2\pi\hbar))|^{2}dp$, using the substitution $p=2\pi\hbar\xi$ in the second step; hence the density is $g(p)=(2\pi\hbar)^{-1}|\mathcal F_2\psi_0(p/(2\pi\hbar))|^{2}$. [given, F4, F5]

2.1 [Clause (a)] By step 1.1 the ground vector has the displayed representative, is a unit vector, equals $\Psi_0$, and satisfies $H_1\psi_0=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}\psi_0$. [step 1.1]

2.2 [Clause (b)] By step 1.2 the position density is $f(x)=\ell^{-1}\pi^{-1/2}e^{-x^{2}/\ell^{2}}$, which equals the heat kernel $\Gamma(x,\ell^{2}/4)$; by [F3] it integrates to $1$, and its mean and second moment are those of $\Gamma(\cdot,\ell^{2}/4)$: $\int x f=0$ and $\int x^{2}f=2\cdot\frac{\ell^{2}}{4}=\frac{\ell^{2}}{2}$. [step 1.2, F3]

2.3 [Clause (c)] By steps 1.3 and 1.4, $g(p)=(2\pi\hbar)^{-1}\cdot2\sqrt\pi\,\ell\,e^{-4\pi^{2}\ell^{2}(p/(2\pi\hbar))^{2}}=(2\pi\hbar)^{-1}2\sqrt\pi\,\ell\,e^{-\ell^{2}p^{2}/\hbar^{2}}=\frac{\ell}{\hbar\sqrt\pi}e^{-\ell^{2}p^{2}/\hbar^{2}}$, which equals the heat kernel $\Gamma(p,\hbar^{2}/(4\ell^{2}))$; by [F3] it integrates to $1$ and has mean $0$ and second moment $2\cdot\frac{\hbar^{2}}{4\ell^{2}}=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2\ell^{2}}$. [step 1.3, step 1.4, F3]

consumer_reviews.snippet:
**(a) Adopted model and state space.** Adopt the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5 for a declared particle of mass parameter
$m>0$, spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ and internal factor
assigned as in the identical-particle and spin postulate P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]). Put $r:=2s+1$ and take
as the model's one-particle state space the complex Hilbert space
$$H_{s}:=L^{2}\bigl(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}\bigr) =\Bigl\{f:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb C^{r}\ \text{measurable}:\ \int_{\mathbb R^{3}}\|f(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx<\infty\Bigr\}\Big/\!\sim,$$
the quotient by equality almost everywhere, with inner product
$\langle f,g\rangle=\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}\sum_{l=1}^{r}f_{l}\overline{g_{l}}\,dx$
linear in the first argument ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]).
Thus an element of $H_{s}$ is a class of functions, not a function, and
pointwise values of a state are not defined; the position density is read from
the class through the observables of clause (b) and the observable and
probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). Its dimension
in the conventions of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (d)1
is $\ell^{-3/2}$ per component. P5 presents the same space as the completed
tensor product $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)\widehat\otimes\mathbb C^{r}$
with the spin factor carrying the representation of P6; the unitary
identification of the two descriptions and the componentwise reading of
componentwise operators are those of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]] and
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]. The orthonormal
basis $(e_{m})_{m=-s,\dots,s}$ of $\mathbb C^{r}$ is the basis fixed by P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] clause (ii)).

**(b) Position and momentum.** The model's $j$-th position and $k$-th momentum
are the componentwise operators $Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (a): for
$f=(f_{l})$, restricted to the classes with $x_{j}f_{l}\in L^{2}$ respectively
with $D_{k}f_{l}\in L^{2}$ for all $l$,
$$(Q_{j}f)_{l}(x):=x_{j}f_{l}(x),\qquad (P_{k}f)_{l}:=-i\hbar\,D_{k}f_{l},$$
with $D_{k}$ the weak derivative and $\hbar$ the action constant of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. These are the scalar operators of
[[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]] applied
componentwise. The model assigns to $(Q_{j},\mathrm m)$ and to
$(P_{k},\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}})$ the status of assigned sharp observables in
the sense of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]
clause (a), with the units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]
clause (d)4; both are densely defined and self-adjoint by
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (a). On the
Schwartz core they satisfy the componentwise canonical commutation relations,
and they commute with the internal-factor operators of clause (c) in the sense
of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-and-internal-factor-commutation]] clauses (a),(c).

**(c) Internal factor.** For $i\in\{1,2,3\}$ let $S_{i}=\hbar J_{i}$ be the
self-adjoint endomorphisms of $\mathbb C^{r}$ of the spin assignment P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] clause (ii),
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]]), and let the model read
them on $H_{s}$ as the matrix actions
$$(S_{i}f)_{l}:=\hbar\sum_{m=1}^{r}(J_{i})_{lm}f_{m}\qquad(l=1,\dots,r),$$
that is, as the amplifications $I\otimes S_{i}$ under the tensor
identification of clause (a) ([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-and-internal-factor-commutation]]
clause (d)). Their declared unit is the unit of action ([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]
clause (d)4). The factor is internal bookkeeping: it is not a spatial
coordinate, not a rotating body and not a relativistic spinor, and the model
assigns no position or worldline to it.

**(d) Momentum-space representative.** With $U^{(s)}$ the unitary of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]] for $r=2s+1$, the
**momentum-space representative** of a preparation vector $\psi\in H_{s}$ is
$\psi_{p}:=U^{(s)}\psi\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3},dp;\mathbb C^{r})$; for a
Schwartz class $\psi$ it is the componentwise Fourier transform
$$(\psi_{p})_{l}(p)=(2\pi\hbar)^{-3/2}\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}e^{-ip\cdot x/\hbar}\psi_{l}(x)\,dx,$$
and its dimension is $(\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}})^{-3/2}$ per component
([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (d)2). By
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]] clause (b), $P_{k}$ acts on the
momentum representative by multiplication by $p_{k}$; this is the model's
momentum reading and no measured momentum distribution is identified with
$|\psi_{p}|^{2}$ by this definition.

**(e) Frame reading.** The model's inertial frames are the global coordinate
charts of P5; frame changes are the Galilean transformations of P5, with
parameters and units as in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. This
definition uses P5's frame class only. The transformation law of state
representatives under a change of inertial frame is a derived statement about
the model's operators and is established by the covariance theorems of this
page for translations and boosts; it is not an additional assumption of this
definition, and no Lorentz transformation law is claimed.

- **Why the class reading matters.** $H_{s}$ consists of almost-everywhere
  classes; the operators $Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are defined on the classes of
  clause (b) and the core identities hold on the Schwartz classes. Phrases such
  as "the value of the wave function at $x$" are shorthand for a chosen
  representative and are not part of the model's state assignment.
- **Units.** The wave function, its momentum representative, the position and

  units fixed by [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; no numerical
  value, and in particular no value of $m$, $s$ or $\hbar$, is asserted beyond
  the exact defining constants of the current SI recorded there.

consumer_reviews.snippet:
**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4,
the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, the identical-particle
and spin postulate P6, and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Fix a mass parameter
$m>0$ and a spin label $s=0$, so that the framework's one-particle model
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] reads its state space as
$H_{0}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ with the pairing linear in the first
argument, its componentwise position family $Q_{1},Q_{2},Q_{3}$, its
componentwise momentum family $P_{1},P_{2},P_{3}$ and the action constant
$\hbar>0$; the spin-zero internal factor carries the trivial representation of
P6. Units are those of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]: position is
read in metres, momentum in $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, energy and potential
energy in joules, and $\hbar$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the cited
mathematical suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(e) Declared generalized stationary solutions.** Let
$-\infty=x_{0}<x_{1}<\dots<x_{n}=\infty$ be a finite partition of
$\mathbb R$, let $E\in\mathbb R$, and let $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ be bounded and classically
$C^{1}$ on $\mathbb R$ with a continuous derivative, and twice continuously
differentiable on each open interval $(x_{j},x_{j+1})$ restricted to which
$V$ is continuous, satisfying
$-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\psi''(x)+V(x)\psi(x)=E\psi(x)$ there. Such a $\psi$ is
a **declared generalized stationary solution** of the model at energy $E$. It
is generally not an element of $H_{\mathrm{lin}}$ (a bounded oscillatory
solution has $|\psi|^{2}$ not integrable), so it is not a preparation of the
model and clause (d) does not apply to it; it is used only through the
declared flux quantities computed from it, and every such use states the
idealization. For dimensional bookkeeping, assign $\psi$ and its amplitudes
the one-dimensional position-wavefunction dimension $\ell^{-1/2}$ of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (d)1 (the SI reference unit
is $\mathrm{m}^{-1/2}$); this convention does not normalize $\psi$ or make it
an element of $H_{\mathrm{lin}}$. The pair's scattering reading assigns to
$\psi$ the
**probability current** $j(x)=\frac{\hbar}{m}\operatorname{Im}\bigl(\overline{\psi(x)}\psi'(x)\bigr)$,
read in $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ by clause (d)5 of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], and reads a ratio of currents at
infinity as a *transmitted or reflected fraction* of the incident current,
conditional on the declared solution and on the asymptotics displayed in each
statement; no such fraction is ascribed to a single particle and no count is
predicted.

consumer_reviews.snippet:
**(e) Reading and scope.** The spread $\Delta_{\rho}A$ is a property of the
pair (preparation, assigned observable): it is the standard deviation of the
outcome law that P2 assigns. It is not an apparatus resolution, not a
measurement error and not a disturbance of the preparation; those are further
objects that require a declared instrument or apparatus model and are not
introduced here. Clause (b) makes no claim that a preparation realizes a
specific laboratory state, that a laboratory procedure measures $A$ with
resolution $u_{A}$, or that the spread is observed in any experiment; the
identification of an apparatus with the pair $(A,u_{A})$ is a tested
identification under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7.
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] fixes the units in which the
displays are read.

consumer_reviews.snippet:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, and the
internal-factor assignment P6 of the framework, read for the spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$, spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\dots\}$ and $r=2s+1$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $Q_{j},P_{j}$ be the model's $j$-th position and
$j$-th momentum operators with their maximal domains, and let
$\Delta_{\psi}Q_{j}$ and $\Delta_{\psi}P_{j}$ be their preparation spreads in
the reading of [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]]. Let
$\psi\in D(Q_{j})\cap D(P_{j})$ be a unit vector and put
$$a:=\langle Q_{j}\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad b:=\langle P_{j}\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad x:=(Q_{j}-a)\psi,\qquad y:=(P_{j}-b)\psi .$$
Then:

(c) for every unit $\psi\in D(Q_{j})\cap D(P_{j})$ the centered pairing has the
exact imaginary part
$$\operatorname{Im}\langle x,y\rangle=-\frac{\hbar}{2};$$
consequently equality $\Delta_{\psi}Q_{j}\Delta_{\psi}P_{j}=\hbar/2$ holds if
and only if $x$ and $y$ are linearly dependent and
$\operatorname{Re}\langle x,y\rangle=0$;

**Given:** The postulates P1, P2, P5 and P6 read through [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]]; the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice; the operators $Q_{j},P_{j}$ of the model with their maximal domains; a unit vector $\psi\in D(Q_{j})\cap D(P_{j})$; the numbers $a,b$ and the centered vectors $x,y$.

[F2] **Moments and spreads.** For a unit vector in $D(Q_{j})$ the mean and variance of the position law exist with $\Delta_{\psi}Q_{j}=\|(Q_{j}-a)\psi\|$ where $a=\langle Q_{j}\psi,\psi\rangle$ is real, and likewise for $P_{j}$ ([[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]] clauses (a) and (b), [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]] clauses (b) and (c)).

[F4] **Approximation.** For every unit $\psi\in D(Q_{j})\cap D(P_{j})$ there is a sequence $(\varphi_{n})$ of unit vectors in $D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})$ with $\varphi_{n}\to\psi$, $Q_{j}\varphi_{n}\to Q_{j}\psi$ and $P_{j}\varphi_{n}\to P_{j}\psi$ in $H_{s}$, and with $\langle Q_{j}\varphi_{n},\varphi_{n}\rangle\to\langle Q_{j}\psi,\psi\rangle$, $\|Q_{j}\varphi_{n}\|\to\|Q_{j}\psi\|$ and the analogous momentum limits ([[lem-nrqm-uncertainty-approximation-by-product-domain-vectors]]).

[F5] **Robertson relation.** For two assigned sharp observables and a unit vector in the intersection of the two operator domains and the two product domains, the spread product is at least half the absolute value of the commutator pairing ([[pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-robertson-relation]] clause (b)).

1.1 [Product-domain case] Let $\varphi$ be a unit vector in $D(Q_{j}P_{j})\cap D(P_{j}Q_{j})$. By [F1] the operators $Q_{j},P_{j}$ are the model's assigned sharp observables with their maximal domains, so the preparation spreads and the Robertson relation of [F5] apply to them. By [F3], $(Q_{j}P_{j}-P_{j}Q_{j})\varphi=i\hbar\varphi$, so $\langle[Q_{j},P_{j}]\varphi,\varphi\rangle=i\hbar\|\varphi\|^{2}=i\hbar$. By [F5] the product of the preparation spreads of the two assigned observables satisfies $\Delta_{\varphi}Q_{j}\Delta_{\varphi}P_{j}\ge\tfrac12|i\hbar|=\hbar/2$. [given, F1, F3, F5, algebra]

2.1 [Approximation] Let $\psi\in D(Q_{j})\cap D(P_{j})$ be a unit vector and let $(\varphi_{n})$ be the approximating sequence of [F4]. For every $n$, $\varphi_{n}$ is a unit product-domain vector, so step 1.1 gives $\Delta_{\varphi_{n}}Q_{j}\Delta_{\varphi_{n}}P_{j}\ge\hbar/2$. By [F2] and [F4], $\Delta_{\varphi_{n}}Q_{j}^{2}=\|Q_{j}\varphi_{n}\|^{2}-\langle Q_{j}\varphi_{n},\varphi_{n}\rangle^{2}\to\|Q_{j}\psi\|^{2}-\langle Q_{j}\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}=\Delta_{\psi}Q_{j}^{2}$, and the analogous identity holds for $P_{j}$ with the momentum limits of [F4]; taking square roots and products gives $\Delta_{\varphi_{n}}Q_{j}\Delta_{\varphi_{n}}P_{j}\to\Delta_{\psi}Q_{j}\Delta_{\psi}P_{j}$. Hence the limit satisfies $\Delta_{\psi}Q_{j}\Delta_{\psi}P_{j}\ge\hbar/2$, which is (a); and on the product domain the same computation together with [F3] is the derivation of (b). [given, step 1.1, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

4.1 [Equality characterization] For a unit $\psi\in D(Q_{j})\cap D(P_{j})$ put $\Delta_{Q}:=\Delta_{\psi}Q_{j}$, $\Delta_{P}:=\Delta_{\psi}P_{j}$. By step 3.1, $\operatorname{Im}\langle x,y\rangle=-\hbar/2$, and by [F6] $$\hbar/2\le\Delta_{Q}\Delta_{P}=\|x\|\,\|y\|\ge|\langle x,y\rangle|\ge|\operatorname{Im}\langle x,y\rangle|=\hbar/2 .$$ Equality $\Delta_{Q}\Delta_{P}=\hbar/2$ holds exactly when both inequalities are equalities, that is (by the equality case of [F6] and the identity $|\langle x,y\rangle|^{2}=(\operatorname{Re}\langle x,y\rangle)^{2}+(\operatorname{Im}\langle x,y\rangle)^{2}$) when $x,y$ are linearly dependent and $\operatorname{Re}\langle x,y\rangle=0$. This completes (c). [step 2.1, step 3.1, F6, algebra]

consumer_reviews.snippet:
**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the framework data of clause (a) of the declared
central-potential model [[def-nrqm-central-framework-central-potential-model]]
with a declared mass parameter $m>0$, spin label $s=0$, the state space
$H_{0}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, the componentwise position and momentum
families and the action constant $\hbar>0$ of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]]; units are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the cited
mathematical suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(d) The declared two-body Coulomb model.** As a further model assumption,
take two **distinguishable** spinless massive particles with declared mass
parameters $m_{1},m_{2}>0$ (unit kg) and opposite declared charges: particle 1
carries charge $-q_{-}$ and particle 2 carries charge $+q_{+}$, where the
charge magnitudes $q_{-},q_{+}>0$ are read in coulombs. Declare the **pair
coupling**
$$\kappa:=\frac{q_{-}q_{+}}{4\pi\varepsilon_{0}},\qquad \varepsilon_{0}:=(\mu_{0}c^{2})^{-1},$$
where $\mu_{0}$ is the declared magnetic constant of the SI conventions and
$c$ the speed of light, both as in clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; the identification
$\kappa=q_{-}q_{+}/(4\pi\varepsilon_{0})$ is a constitutive assumption of the
model, and $\kappa$ is read in $\mathrm{J\,m}$. Its equal-magnitude,
net-neutral submodel is $q_{-}=q_{+}=q>0$, with charges $-q,+q$ and
$\kappa=q^{2}/(4\pi\varepsilon_{0})$; this is the branch used by the later
relative-dipole consumers. The two-particle state space is the Hilbert tensor product of
two copies of the one-particle space of clause (a) as in
[[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], identified with
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{6};\mathbb C)$ through
[[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]]; the spin-zero internal
factor is trivial, and because the two particles are of different species no
symmetrisation is imposed (the case of identical species belongs to the
identical-particle sector of P6 and is not used here). The **assigned energy
operator** is
$$H_{2}:=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m_{1}}\Delta_{x_{1}}-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m_{2}}\Delta_{x_{2}}-\frac{\kappa}{|x_{1}-x_{2}|},\qquad D(H_{2}):=H^{2}(\mathbb R^{6};\mathbb C),$$
which is self-adjoint by clause (c) of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-two-body-reduced-mass]]. Let
$$\Phi(x_{1},x_{2}):=(R,r),\qquad R:=\frac{m_{1}x_{1}+m_{2}x_{2}}{M},\quad r:=x_{1}-x_{2},\quad M:=m_{1}+m_{2},$$
be the centre-of-mass/relative coordinate map of that theorem, with its
unitary $U_{\Phi}$. The model declares the **centre-of-mass/relative reading**
$U_{\Phi}H_{2}U_{\Phi}^{-1}=T_{R}\otimes I+I\otimes C_{\mu}$ of clause (c) of
that theorem, with the **reduced mass**
$$\mu:=\frac{m_{1}m_{2}}{m_{1}+m_{2}}\qquad(\text{unit }\mathrm{kg}),$$
the centre-of-mass kinetic operator $T_{R}:=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2M}\Delta_{R}$
and the **relative operator** $C_{\mu}:=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2\mu}\Delta_{r}-\frac{\kappa}{|r|}$;
the relative operator is exactly the one-centre Coulomb operator of clause
(b) with mass parameter $\mu$. The energy operators $H_{2}$, $T_{R}$ and
$C_{\mu}$ are each read in joules. The model further declares the **fixed-nucleus
reading**: the one-centre model of clauses (b), (c) with mass parameter $m_{1}$
is read as the limiting description in which the second particle is
infinitely heavy, $\mu\to m_{1}$ as $m_{2}\to\infty$ at fixed $m_{1},\kappa$;
this is a declared limiting reading, and no convergence theorem for operators
or states is asserted by it.

**(e) The hydrogen-like identification.** A **hydrogen-like ion** assignment of
the two-body model is the choice $m_{1}=m_{\mathrm e}$ (electron mass
parameter), $m_{2}=m_{\mathrm n}$ (nuclear mass parameter), $q_{-}=e$ (the
elementary charge of clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]) and $q_{+}=Ze$ (nuclear charge
magnitude), so that $\kappa=Ze^{2}/(4\pi\varepsilon_{0})$ for a declared
positive integer $Z$. The **hydrogen assignment** is the specialization
$Z=1$, $m_{2}=m_{\mathrm p}$, for which $q_{-}=q_{+}=e$ and the pair is
net-neutral. These assignments use empirical mass and charge parameters; any
comparison of the model's consequences with a laboratory hydrogen atom is a
tested identification in the sense of clause (iii) of P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]) and carries the
uncertainty of that identification. The model declares no numerical value of
$m_{\mathrm e},m_{\mathrm n},e,\mu_{0}$ or $\hbar$; numerical evaluations, when
made, use their declared or measured values as explicitly qualified empirical
inputs.

consumer_reviews.snippet:
**(c) Local readout of an assigned sharp observable.** Let $(A,u_{A})$ be an
assigned sharp observable of subsystem $A$ with spectral projection valued
measure $E_{A}$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (a),
(b), the spectral measure being regular by
[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]). Define
$$F_{A}(B):=E_{A}(B)\otimes I_{K}\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}) .$$
By [[lem-nrqm-composites-local-pvm-tensor-extension]] clauses (a) and (d),
$F_{A}$ is a regular projection valued measure on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra
of $\mathbb R$ acting on $H\widehat\otimes K$
([[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Its integral
$A^{\mathrm{loc}}:=\int\lambda\,dF_{A}$ with domain
$\{\Psi:\int\lambda^{2}\,dF_{A,\Psi}(\lambda)<\infty\}$ is self-adjoint with
spectral projection valued measure $F_{A}$ by the converse direction of
[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]. The pair
$$(A^{\mathrm{loc}},u_{A})$$
is therefore an assigned sharp observable of the composite
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a)); it
is the **local readout of $(A,u_{A})$ on the declared composite**, and the unit
$u_{A}$ is read as before ([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]). Its
outcome law in a preparation $\rho\in D(H\widehat\otimes K)$ is
$$\mu^{A^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(E_{A}(B)\otimes I_{K})\bigr) .$$
The analogous construction with the roles of $A$ and $B$ exchanged gives the
local readout of an assigned sharp observable of $B$.

Then, using the numerical SI coordinates of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]: $x_j$ and the marginal coordinate $t$ are read in metres, $\xi_j$ in $\mathrm m^{-1}$, $p$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, $m$ in kilograms and $\hbar$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$. consumer_reviews.snippet:
**Setup.** Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero, action constant $\hbar>0$, and declare the **Yukawa potential**
$$V_{g,\mu}(x):=-g\,\frac{e^{-\mu|x|}}{|x|}\qquad(x\ne0),\qquad g>0,\ \mu>0,$$
with the origin convention $V_{g,\mu}(0):=0$, read in joules, with $g$ in
$\mathrm{J\,m}$ and $\mu$ in $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$. Fix the model's reference length $L_*>0$ and write $\mu_*:=\mu L_*>0$, a dimensionless screening parameter.

[F1] Polar integration in dimension three is supplied by [[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]]; the sphere measure has total mass $4\pi$ by [[lem-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-integral-in-angle-coordinates]] clause (b). Both suppliers assume Countable Choice, already declared here.

1.1 Put $V_{\mathrm{loc}}:=V_{g,\mu}\mathbf1_{\{|x|<L_*\}}$ and $V_{\mathrm{tail}}:=V_{g,\mu}\mathbf1_{\{|x|\ge L_*\}}$. The local part is supported in the closed radius-$L_*$ ball, and polar integration gives $\int|V_{\mathrm{loc}}|^2dx=4\pi g^2\int_0^{L_*}e^{-2\mu r}dr \le4\pi g^2L_*<\infty$. Thus it is compactly supported $L^2$, while the tail is bounded by $g/L_*$, in joules. [F1, given, algebra]

2.1 For $s=|x|/L_*\ge1$, $|V_{\mathrm{tail}}(x)|\le(g/L_*)e^{-\mu_*s}$. For any dimensionless $\delta>0$, choose an integer $N>1+\delta$; for $s\ge1$, $(1+s)^{1+\delta}\le(2s)^N$, so [[thm-exponential-beats-every-polynomial]] at $a=\mu_*$ and $m=N$ gives $e^{-\mu_*s}(1+s)^{1+\delta}\to0$. This and continuity on compact intervals give the finite dimensionless constant $C_\delta:=\sup_{s\ge0}e^{-\mu_*s}(1+s)^{1+\delta}$. Hence $|V_{\mathrm{tail}}(x)|\le(g/L_*)C_\delta (1+|x|/L_*)^{-1-\delta}$ on that region; on $|x|<L_*$ the tail is zero, so the bound holds everywhere. [step 1.1, given, algebra]

3.1 By 1.1 and 2.1 the declared Yukawa potential has the decaying-tail form of [[pthm-nrqm-scattering-resolvent-tail-asymptotic-completeness]] clause (c) with any $\delta>0$; hence, by that theorem, the model's interacting operator is self-adjoint on $W^{2,2}$, its wave operators exist and are asymptotically complete with vanishing singular continuous spectrum, and its scattering operator is unitary. [step 2.1, given, algebra]

consumer_reviews.snippet:
**(a) Adopted readings and framework data.** Adopt the state and composition
postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable
and probability postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2), the
autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]
(P4) and the preparation and apparatus postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]] (P7), together with the
Boltzmann-constant and temperature conventions of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]]. Declare one of the
following model readings of the same **adopted Gibbs assignment**:

(ii) a separately declared number-variable mode model, such as a one-mode
bosonic Fock space, a fermionic occupation space, or a declared countable
independent-mode space, with its declared assigned observables and energy
operator $H$. The model declares a self-adjoint Gibbs generator $G$ on that
space: either $G=H$, or a separately supplied self-adjoint realization of the
effective generator $G=H-\mu\mathcal N$, where $\mathcal N$ is the declared
particle-number operator and $\mu\in\mathbb R$ is an assigned chemical
potential in joules. The subtraction is an operator with its supplied domain,
not an assertion that a formal unbounded difference is self-adjoint.

In either reading assume $G$ is bounded below and give its spectral PVM
$E_G$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Let $T>0$ be an assigned temperature in
kelvin and let $\beta:=1/(k_BT)$ in $\mathrm J^{-1}$ with the assigned
Boltzmann constant $k_B$. The Gibbs assignment to either model, and the
chemical-potential identification in (ii), are additional physical
preparation assumptions made here; they are not derived from P1-P4 or from
the fixed-$N$ construction. In (ii) no restriction on the assigned real
$\mu$ is imposed beyond the declared generator and trace existence
conditions; the mode-specific convergence conditions are proved separately.
For reading (ii), $G$ specifies the Gibbs weights. If the assigned autonomous
dynamics is generated by $H$, stationarity of the Gibbs density requires its
separate dynamical or commutation hypotheses; this assignment does not
identify $H-\mu\mathcal N$ with the physical evolution generator.
The physical Helmholtz free-energy vocabulary of the entropy definition
continues to apply only to its stated nonzero finite-sector class and is not
extended to every effective generator by this postulate.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of
the spectral calculus.

**(b) Existence hypothesis and the Gibbs preparation.** The model assumes
that the **partition trace is strictly positive and finite**:
$$0<Z:=\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta G}<\infty,$$
where $\operatorname{Tr}B:=\sum_{f\in\mathcal B}\langle Bf,f\rangle$ for a
bounded positive $B$ and an orthonormal basis $\mathcal B$, with value allowed
to be $+\infty$. Such a basis exists under the declared AC by the maximal
orthonormal-family argument using [[thm-zorn]] and the zero-complement
criterion of [[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]].
This trace is basis independent: for $C:=B^{1/2}$ of
[[thm-positive-square-root]], the defining sum is
$\sum_{f\in\mathcal B}\|Cf\|^2$, whose invariance is
[[thm-hilbert-schmidt-norm-is-basis-independent]]. When the sum is finite,
$C$ is Hilbert-Schmidt ([[def-hilbert-schmidt-operator]]), so $B=C^2$ is
trace class by [[thm-trace-class-iff-product-of-two-hilbert-schmidt-operators]],
and its ordinary trace is this same diagonal sum by
[[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]. Apply this to the bounded positive operator $e^{-\beta G}$, since the
declared Gibbs generator $G$ is bounded below. The model
adopts as the **canonical** or **Gibbs preparation** of the declared model
at temperature $T$ the density operator
$$\rho_\beta:=Z^{-1}e^{-\beta G}.$$
If the sector is zero-dimensional, its partition trace is $Z=0$, no
trace-one density exists, and no canonical density or equilibrium free
energy is assigned. On a nonzero finite-dimensional model space, $Z$ is a
positive finite sum $\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}$ over the eigenvalues of $G$; no energy
sign restriction is needed. There $\rho_\beta$ is the canonical operator of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]], and the
strict positivity and finiteness hypothesis is automatic. In reading (i),
$Z=Z_N$ and this is precisely the finite-sector Gibbs assignment.

Outside the finite-dimensional class the existence hypothesis is a genuine
restriction. For a declared non-interacting fixed-$N$ model with a supplied
countably infinite orthonormal eigenmode basis and real mode energies
$\varepsilon_j$ bounded below, the complete construction and trace criterion
of [[lem-nrqm-many-body-fixed-n-countable-mode-partition-criterion]] give
$Z_N=h_N(q)$ for bosonic statistics or $Z_N=e_N(q)$ for fermionic statistics,
where $q_j=e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}$ and $h_N,e_N$ are the corresponding
nonnegative occupation-series sums. For every fixed $N\ge1$, either trace is
finite exactly when $\sum_jq_j<\infty$. This is a trace on the fixed-$N$
sector and permits negative mode energies.

**(c) The equilibrium assumption and thermal means.** The model **assumes**
that, for a declared sample of the species at the assigned temperature $T$
and in the absence of further preparation information, the preparation
description of the sample is $\rho_\beta$ in the sense of P1. For an assigned
sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ with spectral PVM $E_A$, define its outcome law
$\mu_{\rho_\beta}^A(B):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta E_A(B))$ as in
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b).
If and only if the absolute first moment is finite,
$$\int_{\mathbb R}|a|\,d\mu_{\rho_\beta}^A(a)<\infty,$$
the model defines the **thermal mean** at temperature $T$ by
$$\langle A\rangle_\beta:=\int_{\mathbb R}a\,d\mu_{\rho_\beta}^A(a),$$
read in the assigned unit $u_A$. For bounded $A$ this equals
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta A)=\operatorname{tr}(A\rho_\beta)$. For
unbounded $A$, if the mean exists and the literal product $A\rho_\beta$ is
defined on the whole Hilbert space and is trace class, the mean also equals
$\operatorname{tr}(A\rho_\beta)$ and
$\operatorname{tr}(\overline{\rho_\beta A})$; these conditional product
identities are proved by the density eigenexpansion in
[[lem-nrqm-many-body-spectral-mean-and-defined-trace-product]]. First-moment
existence alone imposes no such product or operator-square-domain condition.
When the absolute first moment is infinite the model asserts no finite
thermal mean. The identification of the parameter $T$ with the thermodynamic temperature of a
sample, and of $\beta$ with its inverse temperature, is part of this
assumption; the stated conservation and equilibrium properties of
$\rho_\beta$ under the flow of P4, and the extremal property of $\rho_\beta$
among preparations, are separate conditional results of this pair.

**(d) Motivation and status.** The assumption is motivated, but not
established, by the maximum-entropy reasoning of the cited sources: among
preparations with a prescribed mean energy, the Gibbs weights maximize the
entropy functional, and the finite-dimensional comparison theorem makes
$\rho_\beta$ the minimizer of the corresponding functional built from $G$.
Its physical Helmholtz free-energy reading applies in the stated finite
fixed-sector class; an effective-generator interpretation in a different
mode model is a separate declared reading. That reasoning is
an argument inside mathematical statistics and thermodynamics; it does not
derive the physical assumption that a sample is described by $\rho_\beta$.
The postulate is an **adopted** statistical-mechanical assumption of the
model, in the sense of the content model's distinction between adopted
assumptions and derived consequences.

**(e) Scope.** The postulate asserts nothing about how a sample reaches the
Gibbs preparation; in particular it asserts no thermalization, no equilibration
time, no ergodicity, no master-equation or Markov approximation, no
thermodynamic limit, no pressure, volume or phase-transition structure, and
no measured temperature or expectation. The requirement $0<Z<\infty$ is part
of the assumption; the model does not define a canonical preparation when
$Z=0$ or the partition trace diverges. Any comparison with a laboratory sample requires the
declared preparation, isolation, detection and sampling models of P7, and
agreement of a thermal prediction with data is evidence about the combined
model and apparatus assumptions, not a proof of the framework or of this
postulate.

- **The finite-sector case.** For a nonzero finite-dimensional sector the existence
  hypothesis is a positive finite sum and hence automatic (and likewise for
  any separately declared nonzero finite-dimensional mode space); the only content of clause
  (b) there is the assignment of the Gibbs weights to the declared energies.
- **Relation to P4.** The postulate adds a preparation assumption to the
  dynamics; by itself P4 describes the unitary evolution of whatever
  preparation is declared, and does not single out $\rho_\beta$. The precise
  sense in which unitary evolution cannot produce $\rho_\beta$ from a
  different preparation is a separate theorem of this pair.
