consumer_reviews.snippet:
Adopt the framework postulates P1, P2, P4 and P5 and the readings of the
declared two-body Coulomb model
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clauses (a), (b),
(d) and (e) with declared masses $m_{1},m_{2}>0$, opposite charge magnitudes
$q_{-},q_{+}>0$, and coupling
$\kappa=q_{-}q_{+}/(4\pi\varepsilon_{0})$ (the equal-magnitude branch
$q_{-}=q_{+}=q$ has $\kappa=q^{2}/(4\pi\varepsilon_{0})$), reduced mass
$\mu=m_{1}m_{2}/(m_{1}+m_{2})$, the centre-of-mass/relative coordinate map
$\Phi$, its unitary $U_{\Phi}$, the total operator $H_{2}$ on
$H^{2}(\mathbb R^{6};\mathbb C)$, the centre-of-mass kinetic operator $T_{R}$
and the relative operator $C_{\mu}$, together with the one-centre results
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-energy-observable-and-flow]] and
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-spectrum-and-degeneracy]] applied with mass
parameter $\mu$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]],
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(d) let $P_{R,j}:=-i\hbar\partial_{R_j}$ on the factor domain
$$D(P_{R,j})=\{\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3}_{R};\mathbb C):\partial_{R_j}\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3}_{R};\mathbb C)\text{ as a weak derivative}\},$$
and define the lifted total-momentum component on the composite state space by
$$\widetilde P_{R,j}:=U_{\Phi}^{-1}(P_{R,j}\otimes I)U_{\Phi},\qquad D(\widetilde P_{R,j})=U_{\Phi}^{-1}\{F\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3}_{R}\times\mathbb R^{3}_{r};\mathbb C):\partial_{R_j}F\in L^{2}\text{ as a weak derivative}\};$$
it is self-adjoint on this maximal weak-derivative domain, has momentum unit
$\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, and has no nonzero eigenvectors in
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{6};\mathbb C)$. A state of definite total momentum would
be a simultaneous eigenvector of the three lifted components, so the model
has no such normalisable state. Since $H_{2}$ has no
eigenvalues, for every $\varphi\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3}_{R};\mathbb C)$ and
nonzero relative bound vector $u$ with $C_{\mu}u=\mathcal E_{n}u$, any
nonzero tensor product $\varphi\otimes u$ in the transformed $(R,r)$ tensor
space, equivalently $U_{\Phi}^{-1}(\varphi\otimes u)$ in the composite
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{6})$ state space, is not an eigenvector; the
stationary-state criterion therefore excludes its pure preparation as a
stationary state;

**Given:** The declared two-body Coulomb model with $m_{1},m_{2},\hbar>0$, opposite charge magnitudes $q_{-},q_{+}>0$, coupling $\kappa=q_{-}q_{+}/(4\pi\varepsilon_{0})$, reduced mass $\mu=m_{1}m_{2}/(m_{1}+m_{2})$, the coordinate map $\Phi$, the unitary $U_{\Phi}$, the operators $T_{R}$, $C_{\mu}$ and $H_{2}$; the one-centre results with mass parameter $\mu$; the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice.

[F2] **Unscaled relative Coulomb spectral representation.** For $\gamma>0$, the mathematical operator $C_{\gamma}:=-\Delta-\gamma/|\cdot|$ on $H^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ is unitarily equivalent to the direct sum, over spherical channels $(l,m)$, of its negative bound-state copies with values $-\gamma^{2}/(4n^{2})$ for $n\ge l+1$ and a continuum copy $L^{2}((0,\infty),d\lambda)$ on which it is multiplication by $\lambda$ on the maximal domain $\{h:\lambda h\in L^{2}\}$; the negative family is complete and $0$ is not an eigenvalue ([[thm-nrqm-coulomb-onto-radial-continuum-transform]] clause (d), [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-negative-subspace-completeness-and-degeneracy]]).

[F4] **Dilation and center Fourier multiplier.** For $c>0$, the map $D_ch(E):=c^{-1/2}h(E/c)$ is unitary from $L^{2}((0,\infty),d\lambda)$ to the correspondingly scaled $L^{2}((0,\infty),dE)$; explicitly $D_c^{-1}g(\lambda)=c^{1/2}g(c\lambda)$. The one-dimensional change-of-variables formula gives its norm identity, and direct substitution gives $D_cM_fD_c^{-1}=M_{f(E/c)}$ for bounded Borel $f$, where $M_f$ denotes the maximal multiplication operator (bounded here) by $f$. On $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3}_{R})$ the $2\pi$-normalized Fourier transform sends $T_R$ to multiplication by $\tau_R(\xi):=2\pi^{2}\hbar^{2}|\xi|^{2}/M$ and $P_{R,j}$ to multiplication by $2\pi\hbar\xi_j$. Their maximal multiplier domains are $\{g:\tau_Rg\in L^2\}$ and $\{g:\xi_jg\in L^2\}$ respectively; the corresponding real multiplication operators are self-adjoint on these maximal domains. Tensoring the transform with the identity gives the unitary partial Fourier transform on the composite $L^2$ space and the maximal weak-derivative domain for $P_{R,j}\otimes I$. Spheres in $\mathbb R^{3}_{\xi}$ are Lebesgue-null by the polar-coordinate formula; Tonelli applies to the $\xi$ and $E$ product measure ([[thm-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-lebesgue-measurable-functions]], [[thm-plancherel]], [[lem-weak-derivatives-are-polynomial-fourier-multipliers]], [[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]], [[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]], [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]]).

[F5] **Two-body decomposition.** $\Phi$ is a linear isomorphism with $|\det\Phi|=1$, $U_{\Phi}$ is unitary, and $U_{\Phi}H_{2}U_{\Phi}^{-1}=T_{R}\otimes I+I\otimes C_{\mu}$ under the identification $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{6})\cong L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3}_{R})\widehat\otimes L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3}_{r})$; $H_{2}$ is self-adjoint on $H^{2}(\mathbb R^{6};\mathbb C)$ and $C_{\mu}=-(\hbar^{2}/2\mu)\Delta-\kappa/|\cdot|$ is the one-centre Coulomb operator with mass parameter $\mu$ ([[thm-nrqm-coulomb-two-body-reduced-mass]] clauses (a)-(c), [[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]]).

[F6] **One-centre results with mass $\mu$.** The one-centre Coulomb model with parameters $(\hbar,\mu,\kappa)$ has bound energies $\mathcal E_{n}=-\frac{\mu\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}$, $n\ge1$, the eigenspace at $\mathcal E_{n}$ having dimension $n^{2}$ and consisting of the transported Laguerre solutions, with the radial and position readings of the one-centre items ([[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-spectrum-and-degeneracy]] clauses (a), (b), [[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-state-radial-distributions]] clauses (a), (c)).

**Proof technique:** direct; transfer the exact unscaled relative PVM by the positive-scaling lemma and continuum dilation, derive the product-channel spectrum, and lift the centre-of-mass momentum through the coordinate unitary.

1.2 [Scaled relative PVM and continuum dilation] Put $\gamma:=2\mu\kappa/\hbar^2>0$ and $c_\mu:=\hbar^2/(2\mu)>0$, so $C_\mu=c_\mu C_\gamma$. By [F2], a unitary spectral representation of $C_\gamma$ has bound channels with values $-\gamma^2/(4n^2)$ and continuum channels $L^2((0,\infty),d\lambda)$ with maximal multiplier $M_\lambda$. The PVM of the scaled operator is transferred by [F3], so on each continuum channel its projection for a Borel set $B$ is multiplication by $\mathbf 1_{c_\mu^{-1}B}(\lambda)$. The unitary dilation of [F4], $$(D_{c_\mu}h)(E):=c_\mu^{-1/2}h(E/c_\mu),$$ satisfies $D_{c_\mu}M_fD_{c_\mu}^{-1}=M_{f(E/c_\mu)}$ for bounded Borel $f$; direct substitution on the maximal multiplier domain gives $D_{c_\mu}(c_\mu M_\lambda)D_{c_\mu}^{-1}=M_E$, with domain $\{g:E g\in L^2(dE)\}$. It sends the transferred projection $M_{\mathbf 1_{c_\mu^{-1}B}(\lambda)}$ to $M_{\mathbf 1_B(E)}$. Each bound value scales to $c_\mu(-\gamma^2/(4n^2))=\mathcal E_n$. Hence the exact spectral representation of $C_\mu$ consists of these bound channels and continuum copies with multiplier $E$, with no zero eigenchannel. This explicitly transfers both the continuum representation and its PVM. [F2, F3, F4, algebra]

2.1 [Product-channel representation and lower spectral bound] Apply the relative unitary of step 1.2 and the partial $2\pi$-normalized Fourier transform in $R$ to the tensor decomposition of [F5]. The transformed $H_2$ is multiplication on each bound channel $(n,l,m)$ by $\tau_R(\xi)+\mathcal E_n$ and on each continuum channel by $\tau_R(\xi)+E$, where $\tau_R(\xi):=2\pi^2\hbar^2|\xi|^2/M\ge0$ by [F4]. Since $\mathcal E_n\ge\mathcal E_1=-\mu\kappa^2/(2\hbar^2)$ and continuum energies satisfy $E>0$, every channel multiplier is at least $\mathcal E_1$; thus $H_2\ge\mathcal E_1 I$. [step 1.1, step 1.2, F4, F5, algebra]

5.1 [Lifted total momentum on the composite state space] In the partial Fourier representation of [F4], $P_{R,j}$ is the real multiplier $2\pi\hbar\xi_j$ on its maximal domain. Therefore $P_{R,j}\otimes I$ is self-adjoint on the maximal weak-derivative domain in the product space, and conjugation by $U_\Phi$ gives exactly $\widetilde P_{R,j}$ and $D(\widetilde P_{R,j})$ stated in (d). If $\widetilde P_{R,j}\Psi=p\Psi$, then for $F=U_\Phi\Psi$ its partial Fourier transform satisfies $$(2\pi\hbar\xi_j-p)\widehat F(\xi,r)=0\quad\text{for almost every }(\xi,r).$$ It is supported on the hyperplane $\xi_j=p/(2\pi\hbar)$, which is null in $\mathbb R^3_\xi$; Tonelli over the remaining momentum and relative variables gives $\widehat F=0$, hence $\Psi=0$. The multiplier has momentum dimension $[\hbar][\xi_j]=\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$. This proves the total-momentum assertion of (d). Since step 4.1 excludes every eigenvector of $H_2$, the stationary-state criterion [F7] also excludes a stationary preparation from any nonzero centre-of-mass/relative-bound product. [F4, F5, F7, step 4.1, algebra]

$t'=t$, $x'=x+a$ of P5 (a change of spatial origin; the parameter $a$ has the

**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4
and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), with the short-range
scattering model of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]]: mass $m>0$, spin zero,
state space $H_{0}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, a declared short-range
potential $V$, the free and interacting assigned energy observables
$H^{\mathrm{free}}$ and $H$, its reading of the flow by
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], and the units of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) Incident plane-wave reading and declared density scale.** As an
additional model assumption of the pair, adopt the **stationary elastic beam
model**. Fix a **wave number** $k>0$ in $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$, a **direction**
$d\in S^2$, and an **incident number-density scale** $n_{\mathrm{inc}}>0$ in
$\mathrm{m^{-3}}$. This scale is an explicitly declared model normalization;
no numerical sample density or measured beam value is supplied. Retain the
unit-amplitude, dimensionless incident shape
$$u_{\mathrm{inc}}(x):=e^{ikd\cdot x},$$
with energy reading $E:=\hbar^2k^2/(2m)$ in joules. The **physical incident
beam field** is $\Phi_{\mathrm{inc}}:=\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}\,u_{\mathrm{inc}}$,
with unit $\mathrm{m^{-3/2}}$ and constant model number density
$|\Phi_{\mathrm{inc}}|^2=n_{\mathrm{inc}}$. For a dimensionless unit-amplitude
shape $\psi$, write $\mathbf j^{\mathrm{unit}}[\psi]:=(\hbar/m)\operatorname{Im}(\overline\psi\nabla\psi)$ for the mathematical current of
[[lem-nrqm-scattering-three-dimensional-current-and-flux]]. Its incident
value is $(\hbar k/m)d$, with velocity unit $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. The model's
**physical number-current density** is the current of
$\Phi=\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}\psi$,
$$\mathbf j[\Phi]:=\frac{\hbar}{m}\operatorname{Im}(\overline\Phi\nabla\Phi)=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\mathbf j^{\mathrm{unit}}[\psi].$$
Thus the **incident current density** and **incident flux density** through a
plane normal to $d$ are
$$\mathbf j_{\mathrm{inc}}=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\frac{\hbar k}{m}d,\qquad J_{\mathrm{inc}}:=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\frac{\hbar k}{m}>0,$$
both in $\mathrm{m^{-2}s^{-1}}$ as in
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (d)5. The mathematical
plane-wave current of the cited lemma remains the unit-shape computation;
the density factor supplies the declared physical beam normalization.

consumer_reviews.snippet:
**Setup.** Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero, action constant $\hbar>0$ and the **uniform ball potential**
$$V(x):=\begin{cases}V_{0},&|x|<R,\\ 0,&|x|\ge R,\end{cases}\qquad V_{0}\in\mathbb R,\ R>0,$$
read in joules and metres; adopt the stationary beam model at wave number
$k>0$ and direction $d$, and let $W=(2m/\hbar^{2})V$, $q=\|K_{k}\|$, $f_{k}$
and the Born amplitude $f_{B}$ be as in
[[pthm-nrqm-scattering-controlled-born-approximation]]. Write
$\theta$ for the scattering angle, $\cos\theta=\Omega\cdot d$, and
$\mathbf q_{\mathrm{tr}}:=k(d-\Omega)$ for the wave-vector transfer and $q_{\mathrm{tr}}:=|\mathbf q_{\mathrm{tr}}|=2k\sin(\theta/2)$ for its magnitude.

2.1 Therefore $f_{B}(\Omega)=-\frac{2mV_{0}}{\hbar^{2}}\cdot\frac{\sin(q_{\mathrm{tr}}R)-q_{\mathrm{tr}}R\cos(q_{\mathrm{tr}}R)}{q_{\mathrm{tr}}^{3}}$ for $q_{\mathrm{tr}}>0$, with the forward value $f_{B}(\theta=0)=-\frac{2mV_{0}}{\hbar^{2}}\frac{R^{3}}{3}$; the amplitude has the dimension of length, since $2mV_{0}/\hbar^{2}$ is in $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$ and the bracket in $\mathrm{m^{3}}$. Adopt the state and composition postulate P1 and the observable and
probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]), the radiation extension
postulate
([[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]]) and
the radiation sector definition
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]], in
the state vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] and
the observable vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]. Assume Countable
Choice, Dependent Choice and Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), including the hypotheses
inherited from the radiation postulate and the cited operator and spectral
items.
Let $f\in\mathfrak h$ be a unit one-photon wave-packet vector. Under the
$d^{3}k$ normalization of clause (b) of
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]], its
coordinate representatives $f(k)$ have units $\mathrm m^{3/2}$. Put
$\varepsilon(k)=\hbar c|k|$, and let
$\rho_{f}$ be the one-photon preparation of the ray of $\iota_{1}(f)$. Then:

(d) *no sharp frequency, energy or momentum*: for every unit vector
$f\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$, the variances of the frequency and energy
laws of (b) are strictly positive, and for every unit vector in
$D(M_{\hbar k_j}^{\mathfrak h})$ the momentum-component variance of (c) is
strictly positive; consequently the mode assignment "photon energy $E=\hbar\omega$,
$\omega=c|k|$" is a spectral assignment of the model and never an exact value
of a normalisable one-photon state;

**Given:** the postulates P1, P2 and the adopted radiation model with transverse space $\mathfrak h$, sectors $\mathfrak H_{n}^{+}$, number operator $N$, free-field energy $H_f$ with $\varepsilon(k)=\hbar c|k|$, one-photon momentum readouts $M_{\hbar k_{j}}^{\mathfrak h}$, and a unit $f\in\mathfrak h$.

[F3] **Spectral atoms.** For a self-adjoint operator $A$ with spectral measure $E_A$, $E_A(\{\lambda\})$ is the orthogonal projection onto the eigenspace $\ker(A-\lambda)$; for a unit eigenvector $u$ at $\lambda$ and a pure state $\rho=T_{u,u}$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})=1$ ([[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a),(b)).

[F6] **Restricted multipliers.** For $m\in\{\hbar c|k|,\hbar k_{j}\}$ the operator $M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}$ is self-adjoint on $\mathfrak h$ with spectral measure $E_{m}(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{m^{-1}(B)}}|_{\mathfrak h}$, the law of a unit $g\in\mathfrak h$ is the push-forward of $\|g\|^{2}\,d^{3}k$ under $k\mapsto m(k)$, and $M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}$ has no eigenvalues; for unit $g\in D(M_{m}^{\mathfrak h})$ the variance is strictly positive ([[lem-nrqm-photons-transverse-restricted-momentum-and-energy-multipliers]] clauses (a)-(d)).

[F7] **Means and variances for pure states.** For a self-adjoint $A$ and a unit $u\in D(A)$ the mean of the outcome law in the pure state $T_{u,u}$ is $\langle Au,u\rangle$; the variance is $\|Au\|^{2}-\langle Au,u\rangle^{2}$ when $u\in D(A)$ ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (e)).

1.2 [Frequency and energy laws] By [F5] the spectral measure of $H_f$ is $E(B)=\bigoplus_{n}E_{T_{n}}(B)$, and on the one-photon sector $\iota_{1}\mathfrak H_{1}^{+}$ it acts as $\iota_{1}E_{T_{1}}(B)\iota_{1}^{-1}$; since $T_{1}=\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}$ by [F4], the restriction is the spectral measure $E_{\varepsilon}(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{\varepsilon^{-1}(B)}}|_{\mathfrak h}$ of [F6]. Therefore $\mu^{H_f}_{\rho_{f}}(B)=\langle E(B)\iota_{1}f,\iota_{1}f\rangle=\langle E_{\varepsilon}(B)f,f\rangle=\int_{\varepsilon^{-1}(B)}\|f(k)\|^{2}\,d^{3}k.$ The assigned frequency law is the push-forward under $k\mapsto c|k|$ by clause (e) of [[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]]. These are the laws in (b), and they exist for every unit $f\in\mathfrak h$. [F4, F5, F6, algebra]

4.1 [Strict positivity of the variances] By [F6] the multiplier $M_{\hbar c|k|}^{\mathfrak h}$ has no eigenvalues and every unit $f\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$ has strictly positive finite energy variance; together with step 1.2 this gives the energy variance claim. The frequency law is the positive constant rescaling $\omega=E/\hbar$, so on the same domain its variance is $\hbar^{-2}$ times the energy variance and is strictly positive. The same clause of [F6] applied to $m=\hbar k_j$ gives strictly positive finite momentum-component variance whenever $f\in D(M_{\hbar k_j}^{\mathfrak h})$. Hence no unit vector of $\mathfrak h$ has a sharp value of frequency, energy or any momentum component, and the assignments of the radiation postulate are spectral assignments. This proves (d). [F6, step 1.2, step 3.1, algebra]

consumer_reviews.snippet:
Adopt the declared long-range Coulomb model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-coulomb-dollard-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin zero,
action constant $\hbar>0$, coupling $\kappa>0$, the assigned energy operator
$H_{\kappa}$ on $H^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, the free operator
$H^{\mathrm{free}}$, the inverse-length coupling
$\gamma=2m\kappa/\hbar^{2}$, a declared reference length $\ell_\star>0$ in metres and reference time $t_{\star}=2m\ell_\star^2/\hbar$, the
Dollard-modified comparison $U_{D}(t)$ and the modified wave operators
$\Omega_{D\pm}$ and $S_{D}$ of that definition. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(c) the modified scattering operator $S_{D}=\Omega_{D+}^{*}\Omega_{D-}$ is
unitary on $H_{0}$ and commutes with the free flow;

[F1] **Dollard integrable remainder.** Assume Countable Choice. For $\gamma>0$, with $H_{0}=-\Delta$, $H_{\gamma}=-\Delta-\gamma/|\cdot|$ on $H^{2}$ and the Dollard-modified evolution $U_{D}^{\mathrm{nd}}(\tau)=e^{-i\tau H_{0}}e^{i\operatorname{sign}(\tau)a(P)\log|\tau|}$, $a(p)=\gamma/(2|p|)$, the family is unitary and the remainder $\gamma/|\cdot|-\gamma/(2|\tau||P|)$ is integrable along $U_{D}^{\mathrm{nd}}$: there are $T_{\psi},C_{\psi}$ with $\|\bigl[\gamma/|\cdot|-\gamma/(2|\tau||P|)\bigr]U_{D}^{\mathrm{nd}}(\tau)\psi\|_{2}\le C_{\psi}(1+\log|\tau|)/|\tau|^{2}$ for $|\tau|\ge T_{\psi}$, for vectors in the dense momentum-test class ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-dollard-integrable-remainder]] clauses (a), (b)).

[F2] **Dollard channel completeness.** With the hypotheses of [F1], the modified wave operators $\Omega_{D\pm}=s\text{-}\lim_{\tau\to\pm\infty}e^{i\tau H_{\gamma}}U_{D}^{\mathrm{nd}}(\tau)$ exist on all of $L^{2}$, satisfy $\Omega_{D\pm}e^{-isH_{0}}=e^{-isH_{\gamma}}\Omega_{D\pm}$, act in each angular channel as multiplication by a bounded Borel function of the energy with $|b_{l,\pm}(E)|=1$ for a.e. $E>0$, and $\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{D\pm}=H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H_{\gamma})=H_{\mathrm c}(H_{\gamma})$; $S_{D}=\Omega_{D+}^{*}\Omega_{D-}$ is unitary ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-dollard-channel-completeness]] clauses (a), (b), (c)).

**Proof technique:** direct; represent the physical data numerically in SI, compare with the supplied mathematical Dollard evolution through a fixed incoming or outgoing energy phase, and transfer the full limits, intertwining, completeness and scattering unitarity.

1.1 [Numerical SI comparison with dimensionless arguments] Write the fixed SI units as $L_0=1\,\mathrm m$, $T_0=1\,\mathrm s$, $M_0=1\,\mathrm{kg}$ and $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$. Let $m_0=m/M_0$, $h_0=\hbar/(E_0T_0)$, $k_0=\kappa/(E_0L_0)$, $L=\ell_\star/L_0>0$ and $t_0=t/T_0$ be their numerical values, and put $\gamma_0=\gamma L_0=2m_0k_0/h_0^2$, $c_0=h_0^2/(2m_0)$ and $\tau=h_0t_0/(2m_0)$. These are pure real numbers, with $\tau\to\pm\infty$ as $t\to\pm\infty$. Represent the wavefunctions in the numerical SI coordinate $q=x/L_0$, with the normalized $L^2$ coordinate map $\mathcal J_0f(q)=L_0^{3/2}f(L_0q)$, the Jacobian normalization understood in the chosen length unit. Substitution in the integral proves this map unitary; weak derivative substitution gives its exact $H^2$ domain transport. The numerical energy representatives are therefore $\mathsf H_\kappa=E_0^{-1}\mathcal J_0H_\kappa\mathcal J_0^{-1}=c_0C_{\gamma_0}$ and $\mathsf H_f=E_0^{-1}\mathcal J_0H^{\mathrm{free}}\mathcal J_0^{-1}=c_0A_0$, where $A_0=-\Delta_q$ and $C_{\gamma_0}=-\Delta_q-\gamma_0/|q|$. Thus $\mathcal J_0e^{-itH_\kappa/\hbar}\mathcal J_0^{-1}=e^{-i\tau C_{\gamma_0}}$ and similarly for the free operator. The numerical reference time is $t_{\star,0}=2m_0L^2/h_0$, so $\frac{|t|}{t_\star}=\frac{|t_0|}{t_{\star,0}}=\frac{|\tau|}{L^2},\qquad \log\frac{|t|}{t_\star}=\log|\tau|-2\log L.$ Every logarithm has a dimensionless argument; no time having units of length squared is placed inside the source logarithm. [F3, F4, given, algebra]

2.1 [Exact fixed energy phases] For a positive numerical energy $e=c_0\lambda$, the phase coefficient of the physical definition is $m_0k_0/(h_0\sqrt{2m_0e})=\gamma_0/(2\sqrt\lambda)$. By [F1], $a(P)=\gamma_0/(2|P|)$ for the numerical source $A_0=|P|^2$. For $\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}$ define the fixed bounded unitary $B_{\sigma,L}=b_{\sigma,L}(A_0),\qquad b_{\sigma,L}(\lambda)=\exp\Bigl(-2i\sigma\frac{\gamma_0}{2\sqrt\lambda}\log L\Bigr)\quad(\lambda>0),\qquad b_{\sigma,L}(0)=1.$ The functions are bounded unimodular Borel functions despite their oscillation near zero, so their calculus is defined on all $L^2$ and they commute with $e^{-irA_0}$ for every $r$. Spectral correspondence [F3] and step 1.1 give, for $|\tau|\ge1$ and $\sigma=\operatorname{sign}t$, $\mathcal J_0U_D(t)\mathcal J_0^{-1}=e^{-i\tau A_0}e^{i\sigma a(P)\log|\tau|}B_{\sigma,L}=U_D^{\mathrm{nd}}(\tau)B_{\sigma,L}.$ The bounded functional calculus also transports under $\mathcal J_0$: conjugating the PVM gives a regular PVM representing the numerical operator, so spectral uniqueness identifies it and simple-function approximation gives the claimed calculus transport. If desired, the annular smooth momentum class in [F1] is preserved by each $B_{\sigma,L}$ because its multiplier is smooth on every compact annulus; hence the source remainder estimate remains integrable on that class after this fixed phase. The comparison for finite $|\tau|<1$ need not equal the source's short-time extension and is irrelevant to the two asymptotic limits. [step 1.1, F1, F3, F4, algebra]

3.1 [Strong limits, isometry and intertwining] Apply [F2] at the positive numerical coupling $\gamma_0$. Let $W_\pm$ be its two full-space Dollard wave operators. Step 2.1 makes the physical comparison product, conjugated by $\mathcal J_0$, equal $e^{i\tau C_{\gamma_0}}U_D^{\mathrm{nd}}(\tau)B_{\pm,L}$ on the corresponding exterior half-line. The fixed bounded right factor and the positive scalar time change let the strong limits pass on every vector, giving $\Omega_{D\pm}=\mathcal J_0^{-1}W_\pm B_{\pm,L}\mathcal J_0.$ Both $W_\pm$ are isometries by [F2] and both $B_{\pm,L}$ are unitaries, so these operators are isometries. For physical $s\in\mathbb R$, put $r=h_0(s/T_0)/(2m_0)$. The numerical free/Coulomb flows are $e^{-irA_0}$ and $e^{-irC_{\gamma_0}}$ by step 1.1. Since $B_{\pm,L}$ commute with the free flow and $W_\pm e^{-irA_0}=e^{-irC_{\gamma_0}}W_\pm$, conjugating gives the exact intertwining of (a). No new source existence or momentum-domain assumption was introduced. [step 1.1, step 2.1, F2, F3, algebra]

4.1 [Full completeness under the reference convention] Because $B_{\pm,L}$ are onto, step 3.1 gives $\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{D\pm}=\mathcal J_0^{-1}\operatorname{ran}W_\pm$. By [F2], this is $\mathcal J_0^{-1}H_{\mathrm{ac}}(C_{\gamma_0})=\mathcal J_0^{-1}H_{\mathrm c}(C_{\gamma_0})$. Positive energy scaling by $c_0$ preserves these spectral subspaces [F3], and the unitary numerical coordinate representation transports the spectral measures and their subspaces as in step 2.1. The resulting physical subspaces are exactly $H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H_\kappa)=H_{\mathrm c}(H_\kappa)$. This proves (b) for every declared reference length, preserving the source's whole continuous subspace and all angular channels. [step 2.1, step 3.1, F2, F3, algebra]

5.1 [Scattering phases, unitarity and free-flow commutation] Put $S^{\mathrm{nd}}=W_+^*W_-$. The formula in step 3.1 gives $S_D=\mathcal J_0^{-1}B_{+,L}^*S^{\mathrm{nd}}B_{-,L}\mathcal J_0.$ All factors are unitary by [F2] and step 2.1, so $S_D$ is unitary. The commutation with the free flow follows directly from the two intertwinings: taking the adjoint of the plus identity at time $-r$ gives $e^{-irA_0}W_+^*=W_+^*e^{-irC_{\gamma_0}}$, hence $S^{\mathrm{nd}}e^{-irA_0}=W_+^*e^{-irC_{\gamma_0}}W_-=e^{-irA_0}S^{\mathrm{nd}}$. The fixed $B_{\pm,L}$ commute with that same flow, so their scattering product does too, and conjugating proves (c). Equivalently the common range projection from step 4.1 gives both $S_D^*S_D=I$ and $S_DS_D^*=I$. For any other reference time $t_\star'$, let $Q_\sigma=q_\sigma(H^{\mathrm{free}})$ with $q_\sigma(E)=\exp(-i\sigma\alpha(E)\log(t_\star'/t_\star))$, $\alpha(E)=m\kappa/(\hbar\sqrt{2mE})$ for $E>0$ and $q_\sigma(0)=1$. The defining phases give exactly $\Omega_{D\pm}'=\Omega_{D\pm}Q_\pm$ and $S_D'=Q_+^*S_DQ_-$. These incoming/outgoing factors are different sign conventions, not a claim that the scattering operator itself is unchanged. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

6.1 [Scope and assembly] Steps 3.1–5.1 establish all the original modified-limit, isometry, intertwining, full completeness and scattering-unitarity conclusions with their corrected dimensional convention. No step supplies the ordinary unmodified Coulomb wave limits, so (d) retains exactly that distinction. The reference length adds only a comparison convention and its fixed channel phases; it adds no hypothesis on a state or on the Coulomb interaction, no amplitude formula and no measured cross section. [F4, given, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1] ∎

- **Phases and observables.** The modified comparison is not unique: changing
  the reference time $t_{\star}$ changes asymptotic channel phases. The
  completeness equalities of (b) and the unitarity of (c) are invariant
  under that change, which is why the definition declares the reference time
  as a convention.
- **What would be needed for an amplitude.** An explicit Coulomb scattering
  amplitude, and with it any Rutherford-type cross section, would require the
  angular asymptotic analysis of the Coulomb continuum solutions and a
  further normalization statement; neither is contained in the completeness
  theorem, and the pair does not assert one.

The statement is conditional on the declared model and the cited mathematics.
It asserts no completeness of the ranges, no unitarity of $S$, no cross
section and no measured quantity; completeness is the content of the two
following theorems of this page.

[F2] **Concrete Cook existence.** Assume Countable Choice. For real $V_{0}\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3})$, with $H_{0}=-\Delta$ on $W^{2,2}$ and $H=H_{0}+M_{V_{0}}$ self-adjoint on the same domain, the Cook integrals $\int_{0}^{\infty}\|V_{0}e^{-itH_{0}}\psi\|_{2}dt$ and its negative-time analogue converge for every Schwartz $\psi$, the wave operators $\Omega_{\pm}=\operatorname*{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH}e^{-itH_{0}}$ exist as bounded linear isometries with $\Omega_{\pm}e^{-isH_{0}}=e^{-isH}\Omega_{\pm}$ and $H\Omega_{\pm}\psi=\Omega_{\pm}H_{0}\psi$ for $\psi\in D(H_{0})$, and $H_{0}$ has purely absolutely continuous spectrum with $L^{2}=H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H_{0})$, the scalar spectral measure of $\psi$ having the displayed density with respect to Lebesgue measure and zero mass at $0$ ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-concrete-three-dimensional-cook-existence]] clauses (a), (b), (c)).

**Proof technique:** direct; use physical-coordinate $W=W_x$ and $A_0=A_{0,x}$, whose numerical representatives in the fixed metre convention are the abstract source operators; the auxiliary parameter $\tau=\hbar t/(2m)$ has square-metre units; identify the model's operators with the energy-divided operators of the cited mathematics through the scaling lemma, transfer the Cook estimates by the linear change of variables $\tau=\hbar t/(2m)$, and transfer the spectral statements by the projection valued measure correspondence.

1.2 For $\psi\in\mathcal S$ put $\tau(t)=\hbar t/(2m)$. By [F1], $Ve^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}\psi=cW e^{-i\tau(t)A_{0}}\psi$, and by [F2] the function $\tau\mapsto\|We^{-i\tau A_{0}}\psi\|_{2}$ is integrable on $[0,\infty)$; the substitution $t\mapsto\tau(t)$ in the Lebesgue integral of a continuous integrand, [[cor-one-dimensional-change-of-variables-with-absolute-derivative]], gives $\int_{0}^{\infty}\|We^{-i\tau(t)A_{0}}\psi\|_{2}dt=\frac{2m}{\hbar}\int_{0}^{\infty}\|We^{-i\tau A_{0}}\psi\|_{2}d\tau<\infty$, hence the first Cook integral of (a); the negative half-line is identical. [F1, F2, algebra]

- **What is not claimed.** Ranges, asymptotic completeness and unitarity of
  $S$ are deliberately absent; they are the content of
  [[pthm-nrqm-scattering-compact-support-asymptotic-completeness]] and
  [[pthm-nrqm-scattering-resolvent-tail-asymptotic-completeness]]. The Cook
  estimates are stated for Schwartz vectors exactly as in the cited
  mathematics; density then gives the strong limits on all of $H_{0}$.
- **Units.** The displayed Cook integrals carry the dimensions of the
  integrand times time; no numerical value of $m$, $\hbar$ or $V$ is asserted.

(e) *Units, reading and scope.* In the SI conventions of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] the position wave function has
unit $\mathrm m^{-3/2}$, the density $n$ has unit
$\mathrm m^{-3}$ and the current $j$ has unit $\mathrm m^{-2}\mathrm s^{-1}$;
the display of (a) is the local balance of the model's squared-amplitude density
in its smooth regime, and (b) reads the rate of change of its integral over a
region as minus the outward current flux across its boundary. When $\psi$ is a
normalized full-space state, these are the position probability density and
probability flux, respectively. The
statement does not assert that the flow of an arbitrary $L^{2}$ initial vector
has a representative obeying the regularity hypotheses of (a)-(c), does not
identify a recorded screen rate or any detection law with the surface flux (the
detection model of this page is the declared effect and bin model), and records
no empirical result.

[F7] **Units.** The position wave function has unit $\mathrm m^{-3/2}$, so $n$ has unit $\mathrm m^{-3}$; $\hbar/m$ has unit $\mathrm m^2\mathrm s^{-1}$, and hence $j$ has unit $\mathrm m^{-2}\mathrm s^{-1}$ ([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]).

polarisation pair is adopted or claimed; the extension does not assert Galilean
covariance of the radiation sector, and it does not identify the massless
Lorentz representations of the photon with the representations of the spatial
rotation group used in P6.

consumer_reviews.snippet:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]), the observable and
probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]),
the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4
([[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]) and the identical-particle and
spin postulate P6 ([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]) in
the readings of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]]
and [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and assume
the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Work in the
finite-mode realization of the declared fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]]: one-particle space
$K$ of finite dimension $d\ge1$ with declared modes $(f_1,\dots,f_d)$,
particle number $N\ge1$, sector space
$\mathfrak H_N^\sigma=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(N)}$, one-particle
self-adjoint operator $h\in\mathcal B(K)$, and **non-interacting** interaction
$W=0$, so that $H_{\mathrm{lab}}=\sum_{i=1}^Nh^{(i)}$ and
$H_N^\sigma=H_{\mathrm{lab}}|_{\mathfrak H_N^\sigma}$ in the notation of that
definition. Let $e_1,\dots,e_d$ be an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors of
$h$ with real eigenvalues $\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_d$ and let
$\varepsilon_{(1)}\le\cdots\le\varepsilon_{(d)}$ be the nondecreasing
rearrangement of the list. Then:

(a) *the labelled operator is diagonal*: $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ is bounded and
self-adjoint with $\|H_{\mathrm{lab}}\|\le N\|h\|$, it commutes with every
permutation unitary $U_\pi$, and for every multi-index
$i=(i_1,\dots,i_N)\in\{1,\dots,d\}^N$,
$$H_{\mathrm{lab}}\,(e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_N})=\Bigl(\sum_{k=1}^N\varepsilon_{i_k}\Bigr)e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_N};$$

(c) *partition sum and ground energy*: write
$$\mathcal C_N^\sigma:=\{\lambda\in W(N,d):\lambda_j\le1\ \text{for every }j\ \text{if }\sigma=-\},\qquad M_N^\sigma:=|\mathcal C_N^\sigma|=\dim\mathfrak H_N^\sigma.$$
The configuration counts are $M_N^- =\binom dN$ and
$M_N^+ =\binom{N+d-1}{N}$. For every $\beta>0$,
$$Z_N(\beta):=\operatorname{tr}e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}=\sum_{\lambda\in\mathcal C_N^\sigma}e^{-\beta\lambda_\lambda}$$
is finite. If $\sigma=-$ and $N>d$, then $\mathcal C_N^-=\varnothing$,
$Z_N(\beta)=0$, and there is no ground eigenvalue or trace-one density
operator on the zero sector; in particular no normalized Gibbs density can
be formed there. Otherwise $M_N^\sigma>0$ and $0<Z_N(\beta)<\infty$.
In this nonzero-sector case, let
$$E_0:=\min_{\lambda\in\mathcal C_N^\sigma}\lambda_\lambda,\qquad E_{\max}:=\max_{\lambda\in\mathcal C_N^\sigma}\lambda_\lambda.$$
Then the actual Boltzmann bounds are
$$M_N^\sigma e^{-\beta E_{\max}}\le Z_N(\beta)\le M_N^\sigma e^{-\beta E_0}.$$
No nonnegativity hypothesis on the $\varepsilon_j$ is imposed. For
$\sigma=-$ and $N\le d$,
$$E_0=\sum_{k=1}^N\varepsilon_{(k)},\qquad E_{\max}=\sum_{k=d-N+1}^d\varepsilon_{(k)},$$
and for $\sigma=+$,
$$E_0=N\varepsilon_{(1)},\qquad E_{\max}=N\varepsilon_{(d)}.$$
For every unit vector $\psi\in\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ in either nonzero sector,
$\langle H_N^\sigma\psi,\psi\rangle\ge E_0$, with equality exactly on the
eigenspace of $E_0$;

[F1] **Finite spectral theorem.** A self-adjoint endomorphism $h$ of the finite-dimensional complex inner product space $K$ is normal, so $K$ has an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors of $h$ with real eigenvalues ([[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]], [[def-hilbert-space]]).

[F4] **Configuration counts.** The map $J\mapsto\mathbf 1_J$ is a bijection from $N$-element subsets onto $\{\lambda\in\{0,1\}^d:\sum_j\lambda_j=N\}$, the sector dimensions are $\binom dN$ and $\binom{N+d-1}{N}$, and for $N>d$ the antisymmetric sector is $\{0\}$ ([[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-finite-mode-occupation-counts]] clauses (a), (b), (c), [[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]] clause (b)).

4.1 [Extreme energies and ground eigenspace] Work on a nonzero sector. For $\sigma=-$, each configuration selects $N$ distinct eigenvalues, so its energy is at least the sum of the $N$ smallest and at most the sum of the $N$ largest; these bounds are attained by the corresponding subsets. Thus $E_0=\sum_{k=1}^N\varepsilon_{(k)}$ and $E_{\max}=\sum_{k=d-N+1}^d\varepsilon_{(k)}$. A minimizing subset contains every mode with energy strictly below $\varepsilon_{(N)}$, contains no mode with energy strictly above $\varepsilon_{(N)}$, and fills its remaining places with modes at that boundary energy; this includes all choices allowed by degeneracy. For $\sigma=+$, the identity $\sum_j\lambda_j=N$ gives $N\varepsilon_{(1)}\le\sum_j\lambda_j\varepsilon_j\le N\varepsilon_{(d)}$; the two bounds are attained by putting all particles in a minimum-energy or maximum-energy mode respectively. Equality at the lower bound holds exactly when every occupied mode has energy $\varepsilon_{(1)}$. Finally expand a unit vector in the orthonormal sector basis of step 3.1: $\psi=\sum_\lambda c_\lambda b_\lambda$, $\sum_\lambda|c_\lambda|^2=1$. Then $\langle H_N^\sigma\psi,\psi\rangle-E_0=\sum_\lambda|c_\lambda|^2(\lambda_\lambda-E_0)\ge0$, with equality exactly when all coefficients at energies greater than $E_0$ vanish, that is, exactly on the ground eigenspace. Together with step 3.1 this proves (c). [F3, F4, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 [Conclusion and scope] Steps 1.1 and 2.1 prove (a) and (b), steps 3.1 and 4.1 prove (c) and step 3.2 proves (d). The argument used the finite-mode idealization, the declared non-interacting $h$ and the finite-dimensional spectral and tensor calculus; no interaction, spatial realization, infinite mode family, thermal state, equilibration or laboratory identification entered, which is (e). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 3.2] ∎

**(a) Assigned energy observable.** Adopt the autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] (P4) for a declared isolated system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned energy observable** of the system is an assigned sharp observable $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ in the sense of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a), whose declared unit $u_H$ is an energy unit in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] (joules in the SI conventions fixed there). Thus $H_{\mathrm{op}}:D(H_{\mathrm{op}})\subset H\to H$ is densely defined and self-adjoint ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]), with spectral projection-valued measure $E_H$ on the Borel sets of $\mathbb R$ under the choice hypotheses of [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]] ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]), and its outcome law in a preparation is the law of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). The assignment of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ is part of the model specification, as in clause (i) of P4; this definition asserts nothing about which laboratory quantity of a concrete system realizes it.

**(b) The unitary flow.** The **time evolution** or **flow** of the isolated system is the family
$$U(t):=\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tH_{\mathrm{op}}\Bigr):=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\,dE_H(\lambda)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P4 in the spectral calculus of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ ([[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]); here $\hbar>0$ is the reduced Planck constant with its value and unit fixed by [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], so that $tH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$ is dimensionless. Equivalently, $U(t)=e^{itT}$ for the self-adjoint generator $T:=-H_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$ with $D(T)=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$; the two readings agree by the uniqueness of the generator in Stone's theorem, and by [[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]] ([[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-flow-calculus]] clause (a)) the family $U$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group: $U(0)=I$, $U(t+s)=U(t)U(s)$, $U(t)^{*}=U(t)^{-1}=U(-t)$ ([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]).

(a) for each $i$ the lifted coordinate rotation family
$t\mapsto U_{s}(A_{i}(t))=e^{-itJ_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}/\hbar}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-su2-lift-of-the-rotation-action]] clause (c) is a
strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group of symmetries of the declared
dynamics: $U_{s}(A_{i}(t))\,U(u)=U(u)\,U_{s}(A_{i}(t))$ for all $t,u$ and
$U_{s}(A_{i}(t))D(H_{V})=D(H_{V})$;

(b) each $J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is a conserved assigned sharp observable of
the model with energy $H_{V}$: for every preparation $\rho$, every Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$,
$$\mu^{J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}}_{\rho(0)}(B),\qquad \rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*},$$
and for a unit vector $\psi\in D(L_{i})=D(J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}})$ the mean and
the second moment of the law of $J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ in the pure
preparation $[\psi(t)]$ are finite and independent of $t$, with time-zero
values $\langle J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}\psi,\psi\rangle$ and
$\|J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}\psi\|^{2}$;

**Given:** The postulates P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 in the stated readings; the
three choice principles; the model parameters $m>0$, $s$, $r=2s+1$; the
rotationally invariant real bounded measurable potential $V$; the energy
operator $H_{V}$ and its flow $U$; the angular momentum operators $L_{i}$,
$S_{i}$, $J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}$; a preparation $\rho$; a Borel set $B$;
times $t,u$; a unit vector $\psi$.

[F1] **The bounded-potential operator.** $H_{V}$ is self-adjoint on
$D(H_{V})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ as the componentwise sum of
the free operator and the bounded multiplier $M_{V}$, its domain is invariant
under the flow $U(t)=e^{-itH_{V}/\hbar}$, which is a strongly continuous
one-parameter unitary group, and $P_{k},M_{V}$ act componentwise
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clauses (b),(c) applied to each component,
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]],
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (b)).

[F2] **Rotation invariance of the model.** For every $R\in SO(3)$ one has
$U(R)H_{V}U(R)^{-1}=H_{V_{R}}$ with $V_{R}(x)=V(R^{-1}x)$; since $V_{R}=V$
almost everywhere by hypothesis, every $U(R)$ is a symmetry of $H_{V}$ in the
sense of [[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]]
clause (b), the map $R\mapsto U(R)$ is a strongly continuous unitary symmetry
group, and each $L_{i}$ is conserved with time-independent law and moments in
the sense of that page
([[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-rotational-and-parity-invariance]] clauses (a),(b)).

[F3] **Lifted coordinate group.** For every $i$,
$t\mapsto U_{s}(A_{i}(t))=U(R_{i}(t))M_{s}(A_{i}(t))=e^{-itJ_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}/\hbar}$
is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group with
$J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}=L_{i}+S_{i}$ self-adjoint on $D(L_{i})$
([[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-su2-lift-of-the-rotation-action]] clauses
(b),(c)).

[F5] **Conservation from a symmetry group.** Let $(A,u_{A})$ be an assigned
sharp observable with $W(s):=e^{-isA/\hbar}$ for a self-adjoint $A$. If
$W(s)U(t)=U(t)W(s)$ for all $s,t$, then the outcome law of $(A,u_{A})$ is
time-independent in every preparation, and if $\psi\in D(A)$ is a unit vector
the mean and second moment of the law in $[\psi(t)]$ are finite and
independent of $t$ with time-zero values $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and
$\|A\psi\|^{2}$
([[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-generator-conservation]] clauses (a),(b),
[[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]],
[[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]],
[[def-trace-class-operator]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]).

1.1 [Internal factors commute with the dynamics] Let $M$ be the fibrewise matrix action of a fixed matrix; by [F4] $M$ commutes with $P_{k}$ and with $M_{V}$ and preserves $W^{2,2}$, hence $MD(H_{V})\subseteq D(H_{V})$, $M(H_{V}\psi)=H_{V}(M\psi)$ for $\psi\in D(H_{V})$, and $MU(t)=U(t)M$ for every $t$: write $M=M_1+iM_2$ with $M_1=(M+M^*)/2$, $M_2=(M-M^*)/(2i)$ self-adjoint fibrewise matrix actions, apply the second part of [F4] to each, and add; in particular this applies to $M=M_{s}(A_{i}(t))$, to $M=S_{i}$ and to every bounded matrix action. [F1, F4, algebra]

2.1 [Lifted coordinate groups are symmetries] Fix $i$ and $t$; by [F3], $U_{s}(A_{i}(t))=U(R_{i}(t))M_{s}(A_{i}(t))$; by step 1.2 the first factor commutes with $U(u)$ and preserves $D(H_{V})$, and by step 1.1 the second factor does the same, so the product commutes with $U(u)$ for every $u$ and preserves $D(H_{V})$; combined with the group property and strong continuity of [F3], the family $t\mapsto U_{s}(A_{i}(t))$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group of symmetries, which is (a). 3.1 [Total angular momentum conservation] By step 2.1 and [F3], the group $W(s):=e^{-isJ_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}/\hbar}=U_{s}(A_{i}(s))$ satisfies $W(s)U(t)=U(t)W(s)$ for all $s,t$ and preserves $D(H_{V})$; applying [F5] to the assigned sharp observable $(J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}},\mathrm{J\,s})$ of [[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]] clause (d) gives the time-independence of its outcome law in every preparation and, for a unit $\psi\in D(L_{i})=D(J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}})$, the conservation of the mean and second moment with the stated time-zero values, which is (b). consumer_reviews.snippet:
**Positive operators and effects on the assigned Hilbert space.** For a bounded operator $F:H\to H$, write $F\ge0$ when $F=F^*$ and $\langle Fx,x\rangle\ge0$ for every $x\in H$. Write $0\le F\le I$ when $F$ and $I-F$ are positive; equivalently $0\le\langle Fx,x\rangle\le\|x\|^2$ for every $x\in H$. Thus an **effect** on $H$ is a bounded operator satisfying these conditions. These definitions apply whether or not $H$ is finite-dimensional; in finite dimensions they agree with [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]].

**(i) Sharp observables.** An **ideal sharp real-valued quantity** (observable) of a system with state space $H$ is a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), meaning $D(A)=D(A^*)$ and $A\psi=A^*\psi$ on this common domain, together with a declared unit in which its real spectral coordinate is read; the unit is part of the assignment, and no numerical value of the coordinate is asserted by the assignment. Symmetry of $A$ on a small domain is not sufficient for self-adjointness, and the domain is a declared part of the observable.

- **Adopted, not derived.** The representation of sharp quantities by self-adjoint operators and the Born rule of clause (ii) are assumptions. They are motivated by the successes of the framework but are not deduced from experiment.
- **No detector theorem.** Clause (iii) explicitly distinguishes an ideal point outcome from a finite-resolution record: the model's binomial or binned probabilities are the operational objects, and a vanishing ideal density at a point does not make a finite bin of positive length impossible.
- **Sharpness and units.** A declared observable carries a unit; sums and comparisons of outcome coordinates are meaningful only for observables with the same unit. Quantities of the model whose operator status is not declared are numbers or parameters, not observables.

Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be the state space of a declared isolated system of the framework ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]), let $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ be its assigned energy observable with spectral projection-valued measure $E_H$ and flow $U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)$ ([[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]), and let $u_{1},\dots,u_{N}$ be a finite orthonormal family of eigenvectors of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ with real eigenvalues $\lambda_{1},\dots,\lambda_{N}$: $H_{\mathrm{op}}u_{n}=\lambda_{n}u_{n}$ for $n=1,\dots,N$. Fix coefficients $c_{n}\in\mathbb C$ and the nonzero vector
$$\psi_{0}=\sum_{n=1}^{N}c_{n}u_{n},\qquad S:=\{n:c_{n}\ne0\}.$$
For a nonzero vector $\phi$, write $\mu^{A}_{[\phi]}$ for the outcome law of the pure preparation $[\phi]$, computed on the unit representative $\phi/\|\phi\|$ as in [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b) and [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]].
Then, with $\psi(t)=U(t)\psi_{0}$:

[F2] **Outcome law for a pure preparation.** $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}=\langle E_{A}(B)\psi,\psi\rangle$ for a unit vector, and the number depends only on the ray $[\psi]$; the inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b), [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]], [[def-inner-product-space]]).

2.1 [Trigonometric-polynomial law] Assume first $\|\psi_{0}\|=1$. By [F2] and step 1.1, using conjugate-linearity in the second argument, $\mu^{A}_{[\psi(t)]}(B)=\langle E_{A}(B)\sum_{n\in S}c_{n}e^{-i\lambda_{n}t/\hbar}u_{n},\sum_{m\in S}c_{m}e^{-i\lambda_{m}t/\hbar}u_{m}\rangle=\sum_{m,n\in S}c_{n}\overline{c_{m}}e^{-i(\lambda_{n}-\lambda_{m})t/\hbar}\langle E_{A}(B)u_{n},u_{m}\rangle$. For general nonzero $\psi_{0}$, the unit representative $\psi(t)/\|\psi_{0}\|$ has coefficients $c_{n}/\|\psi_{0}\|$ by step 1.1; substituting these into the unit-vector calculation divides the displayed sum by $\|\psi_{0}\|^{2}$, as asserted. consumer_reviews.snippet:
1. an orthonormal pair $(u_{+},u_{-})$ of $V$, read as the pair of orthogonal
   **fringe bin directions** of a declared two-bin detector, with projections
   $Q_{\pm}x:=\langle x,u_{\pm}\rangle u_{\pm}$;
2. a **declared amplitude datum** $a\in V\setminus\{0\}$ whose complex
   coordinates are dimensionless ratios relative to one fixed reference
   amplitude $A_{\mathrm{ref}}$; $a$ need not have unit norm;
3. the **declared classical field model**, whose state datum is the normalized
   amplitude coordinate $a$, whose dimensionless relative bin intensities are
   $I_{\pm}(a):=\|Q_{\pm}a\|^{2}$, and whose
   normalised two-bin law is $I_{\pm}(a)/(I_{+}(a)+I_{-}(a))$;
4. the **quantised model reading** of the same datum: the pure preparation of
   the ray $[a]$ of the polarisation space, measured by the declared ideal
   sharp measurement with outcome projections $(Q_{+},Q_{-})$ declared directly in the sense of
   [[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]
   clause (a), with the Born law of P2. This arbitrary-bin sharp measurement
   need not belong to the real-angle analyser family of the original frame.

[F1] **Projections and resolution.** For every orthonormal pair $(u_{+},u_{-})$ of the two-dimensional space $V$, the maps $Q_{\pm}$ are orthogonal projections with ranges $\mathbb Cu_{\pm}$, $Q_{+}Q_{-}=0$ and $Q_{+}+Q_{-}=I$ ([[lem-nrqm-photons-analyzer-projections-and-overlaps]] clauses (a),(d), applied with $(e_{1},e_{2}):=(u_{+},u_{-})$).

[F3] **Born law.** For the declared ideal sharp measurement with outcome projections $(Q_{+},Q_{-})$ and the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi$, the outcome probabilities are $\|Q_{\pm}\psi\|^{2}$; for a nonzero datum $a$ the unit vector is $\psi=a/\|a\|$ and the probabilities are $\|Q_{\pm}a\|^{2}/\|a\|^{2}$ ([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]] clauses (a),(b), [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b), [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]).

[F4] **Inner product.** The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second; consequently $\|Q_{\pm}a\|^{2}=|\langle u_{\pm},a\rangle|^{2}$, and for $a=a_{1}+a_{2}$,
$$|\langle u_{\pm},a\rangle|^{2}=|\langle u_{\pm},a_{1}\rangle|^{2}+|\langle u_{\pm},a_{2}\rangle|^{2}+2\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\langle u_{\pm},a_{1}\rangle\overline{\langle u_{\pm},a_{2}\rangle}\bigr)$$
([[lem-nrqm-photons-analyzer-projections-and-overlaps]] Fact [F1], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]).

Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero and a **compact-support-class** potential $V$ supported in $B_{R}$; by
[[pthm-nrqm-scattering-compact-support-asymptotic-completeness]] the model's
wave operators exist and
$$S=\Omega_{+}^{*}\Omega_{-}$$
is unitary on $H_{0}$ and commutes with the free flow. Write $\sigma$ for
surface measure on $S^{2}$ and $\mathfrak h=L^{2}(S^{2},d\sigma)$, and for
every $d\in S^{2}$ let $f_{k}(\cdot,d)$ be the model's stationary amplitude
of [[pthm-nrqm-scattering-stationary-wave-amplitude-and-flux]] at incident
direction $d$, with the operator $\mathcal A_{k}$ on $\mathfrak h$ defined by
$$(\mathcal A_{k}a)(\Omega):=\int_{S^{2}}f_{k}(\Omega,d)\,a(d)\,d\sigma(d).$$
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) the free flow is diagonalized by the free trace transform of the cited
mathematics, a unitary $F_{0}:H_{0}\to L^{2}((0,\infty),dE;\mathfrak h)$ with
$(F_{0}g)(E,\omega)=E^{1/4}2^{-1/2}\widehat g(\sqrt E\,\omega)$ in the
energy-divided variables of the scaling correspondence, where this auxiliary $E=k^2$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$ and the physical energy is $(\hbar^2/2m)E$, and the model's
scattering operator is carried into multiplication,
$$F_{0}\,S\,F_{0}^{*}=M_{S(E)};$$

(b) for almost every $E=k^{2}>0$ the on-shell operator is
$$S(E)=I+\frac{ik}{2\pi}\mathcal A_{k},$$
a unitary operator on $\mathfrak h$, and the model's stationary amplitude
$f_{k}(\Omega,d)$ is the kernel of $\mathcal A_{k}$;

[F1] **Stationary and dynamical sector identification.** Assume Countable Choice. For real bounded compactly supported $V_{0}$, with $H_{0}=-\Delta$, $H=H_{0}+M_{V_{0}}$ and $S=\Omega_{+}^{*}\Omega_{-}$ its complete scattering operator, the free trace transform $F_{0}g(E,\omega)=E^{1/4}2^{-1/2}\widehat g(\sqrt E\omega)$ is unitary onto $L^{2}((0,\infty),dE;\mathfrak h)$, $F_{0}SF_{0}^{*}=M_{S(E)}$ with $S(E)=I+\frac{ik}{2\pi}\mathcal A_{k}$ unitary, $\mathcal A_{k}$ built from the stationary amplitude, $S[V_{R}](E)=U_{R}S[V](E)U_{R}^{-1}$, and for radial $V_{0}$ the fiber is diagonal with $S_{l}(E)=\overline{W_{l}}/W_{l}$, $|S_{l}|=1$ ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-stationary-dynamical-sector-identification]] clauses (a), (b), (c), (d)).

[F2] **The model's amplitude and $S$.** The model's amplitude $f_{k}(\cdot,d)$ is the stationary theorem's amplitude for the reduced potential $W=(2m/\hbar^{2})V$, and the model's $S=\Omega_{+}^{*}\Omega_{-}$ is the unitary operator of the compact-support completeness theorem ([[pthm-nrqm-scattering-stationary-wave-amplitude-and-flux]] clause (b), [[pthm-nrqm-scattering-compact-support-asymptotic-completeness]] clause (c)).

**Proof technique:** direct; represent physical-coordinate $W=W_x$, $k$ and $E=k^2$ numerically in the fixed metre convention; the model's operators and amplitude are the cited energy-divided ones through the scaling correspondence, so the energy-divided identification theorem applies and supplies all four clauses.

3.1 By [F1] the free trace transform $F_{0}$ diagonalizes the free flow and $F_{0}SF_{0}^{*}=M_{S(E)}$ with $S(E)=I+\frac{ik}{2\pi}\mathcal A_{k}$; since the model's $S$ and $\mathcal A_{k}$ are the same operators as in [F1] by steps 1.1 and 2.1, the displays of (a) and (b) follow, including unitarity of the on-shell operator. - The parameter condition is a genuine restriction: under an affine reparametrization $s\mapsto\alpha s+\beta$ of a trajectory, the new parameter again equals the frame time only when $\alpha=1$ and $\beta=0$; free reparametrizations are not part of the model.
- No causal or velocity restriction is imposed on classical trajectories by this definition; the framework is non-relativistic and sets no speed bound. Constraints imposed by a particular apparatus model are stated where that model is introduced.
- **Dimensions of the derivatives.** The parameter $s=t(\gamma(s))$ has dimension $\tau$ and each coordinate $x_i$ has dimension $\ell$ under [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Therefore each coordinate velocity component $w_i=dx_i/ds$ has dimension $\ell\tau^{-1}$, and each coordinate acceleration component $a_i=d^2x_i/ds^2$ has dimension $\ell\tau^{-2}$. These are the dimensions of the frame-coordinate derivatives; they add no force law or speed bound.

$q_j:=e^{-\beta E_j}/Z_N$ with $Z_N:=\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}$,

$F(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)-k_BT\,s(\rho)$ and
$F_{\mathrm{eq}}:=-k_BT\log Z_N$ be the free-energy functional and
equilibrium free energy of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]] clauses (e).
Then:

(e) *scope*: the statement is conditional on the adopted ensemble postulate
and on the declared finite-dimensional model; it asserts no equilibration of
any preparation towards $\rho_\beta$, no rate of approach, no thermodynamic
limit, no pressure or volume variable, and, for a laboratory sample, it
inherits the tested identification of the preparation and temperature
assignment of P7.

**Given:** the declared finite-dimensional sector model with energy operator $H_N^\sigma$, eigen-decomposition and parameters $\beta$, $T$, $k_B$; the canonical preparation $\rho_\beta$ and the functional $F$ of the statement.

[F1] **Supplied finite Gibbs data.** For the finite-dimensional self-adjoint $H_N^\sigma$ with eigenvalues $E_1,\dots,E_D$ and orthonormal eigenbasis $(v_1,\dots,v_D)$, and $\beta>0$: $Z_N=\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}\in(0,\infty)$, $\rho_\beta\in\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$, $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H_N^\sigma)=Z_N^{-1}\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}E_j$, $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H_N^\sigma)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho_\beta)=-\beta^{-1}\log Z_N$, and for every density operator $\rho$ on $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ one has $\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho)\ge-\beta^{-1}\log Z_N$ with $s(\rho)\le\log D$ and equality $s(\rho)=\log D$ exactly for $\rho=D^{-1}\mathrm{id}$ ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]] clauses (a), (b), (c)).

[F2] **Spectral decomposition of a preparation.** A density operator $\rho$ on the finite-dimensional space $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ has the form $\rho=\sum_{i=1}^Dw_iT_{u_i,u_i}$ with $w_i\ge0$, $\sum_iw_i=1$ and $(u_i)$ an orthonormal eigenbasis, by [[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]] and [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] applied as in [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]] clause (a); with $p_{ij}:=|\langle u_i,v_j\rangle|^2$ one has $\sum_jp_{ij}=1$ and $\sum_ip_{ij}=1$, because $(u_i)$ and $(v_j)$ are orthonormal bases.

1.1 [The canonical preparation and its data] By [F1], $Z_N=\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}$ is a finite sum with $0<Z_N<\infty$; since $D\ge1$ each term is positive, so $q_j=e^{-\beta E_j}/Z_N>0$ with $\sum_jq_j=1$. By [F1] the operator $\rho_\beta=\sum_jq_jT_{v_j,v_j}$ is a density operator on $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$, hence a declared sector preparation of the model, and the two displayed identities are the clauses of [F1] together with the entropy definition. This proves (a). [F1, algebra]

2.1 [The free-energy difference for every mixed preparation] Let $\rho=\sum_iw_iT_{u_i,u_i}$ be as in [F2] and put $p_{ij}=|\langle u_i,v_j\rangle|^2$, $r_i=\sum_jp_{ij}q_j$. Each $r_i>0$ and $\sum_ir_i=\sum_jq_j\sum_ip_{ij}=1$. Use the entropy convention $\eta(w)=w\log w$ for $w>0$ and $\eta(0)=0$ (the notation $0\log0=0$ does not define $\log0$). The trace pairing and the entropy definition give $\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)=\sum_{i,j}w_ip_{ij}E_j$ and $s(\rho)=-\sum_i\eta(w_i)$. Since $\beta E_j=-\log q_j-\log Z_N$, $\Delta:=\beta(F(\rho)-F_{\mathrm{eq}})=\sum_i\bigl(\eta(w_i)-w_i\sum_jp_{ij}\log q_j\bigr)$. Define $a_i:=\log r_i-\sum_jp_{ij}\log q_j=\sum_jp_{ij}h(q_j,r_i)$, the last equality using $\sum_jp_{ij}=1$ and $\sum_jp_{ij}(q_j-r_i)=0$. Step 1.2 gives $a_i\ge0$, with equality exactly when $q_j=r_i$ for every $j$ with $p_{ij}>0$. By the quotient law for positive $w_i$ and by the explicit zero convention otherwise, $\Delta=\sum_i b(w_i,r_i)+\sum_iw_i a_i=\sum_i d(w_i,r_i)+\sum_iw_i a_i$, because $\sum_i(w_i-r_i)=0$. All summands are nonnegative, so $F(\rho)\ge F_{\mathrm{eq}}$, proving (b) for every density operator, including those with zero eigenvalues. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.2, algebra]

4.1 [Conclusion and scope] Step 1.1 proves (a), step 2.1 proves (b), step 3.1 proves (c), and step 1.3 proves (d). The argument is an optimisation inside the declared finite-dimensional sector at the adopted ensemble parameters; no equilibration, rate, thermodynamic limit or measured thermal quantity entered, which is (e). [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 1.3, step 3.1] ∎

consumer_reviews.snippet:
Adopt P1, P2 and P4 for the declared two-body Coulomb model of
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clause (d), in the
relative-coordinate factor $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ with the dipole
operator $D_{j}=-qQ_{j}$ and the compressed finite-level coupling of
[[post-nrqm-approximations-static-finite-level-dipole-coupling]]. Use
the Coulomb mass parameter $m=\mu:=m_{1}m_{2}/(m_{1}+m_{2})$ and
$a_{\mu}:=\hbar^{2}/(\mu\kappa)>0$. Choose as
the finite-level subspace the **declared two-dimensional subspace**
$$W:=\operatorname{span}\{\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\}\subseteq L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C),$$
where $\psi_{1}$ and $\psi_{2}$ are normalized bound states of the model with
angular labels $(n,l,m)=(1,0,0)$ and $(2,1,0)$ supplied by
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-bound-spectrum-and-degeneracy]], so that
$H_{\kappa}\psi_{1}=E_{1}\psi_{1}$, $H_{\kappa}\psi_{2}=E_{2}\psi_{2}$ with
$$E_{1}=-\frac{m\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}},\qquad E_{2}=-\frac{m\kappa^{2}}{8\hbar^{2}},\qquad \Delta:=E_{2}-E_{1}=\frac{3m\kappa^{2}}{8\hbar^{2}}>0 .$$
Choose the external field along the third axis of the declared frame,
$\mathbf E_{\rm ext}=(0,0,\mathcal E)$ with $\mathcal E>0$ in
$\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$, and use the dimensionless coupling
$$\lambda:=\frac{\mathcal E}{1\ \mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}},\qquad V:=-(1\ \mathrm{V\,m^{-1}})\,D^{W}_{3},$$
so that the Stark model of the postulate reads
$$H_{S}(\mathcal E)=H_{0}+\lambda V,\qquad H_{0}:=\Pi_{W}H_{\kappa}\big|_{W}=\begin{pmatrix}E_{1}&0\\0&E_{2}\end{pmatrix}$$
in the declared orthonormal basis. Then:

(a) the compression of the dipole matrix has the form
$$D^{W}_{1}=D^{W}_{2}=0,\qquad D^{W}_{3}=D_{\rm rel}\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad D_{\rm rel}:=|\langle\psi_{2},D_{3}\psi_{1}\rangle|>0,$$
with unit $\mathrm{C\,m}$, where the phase of $\psi_{2}$ is chosen to make
the off-diagonal entry positive. The local computation below gives
$D_{\rm rel}=128\sqrt2\,q a_{\mu}/243>0$ from the declared model parameters;
this is an exact model identity, with no measured value of any parameter.
The diagonal entries vanish by angular degree selection, and only $Q_{0}$
can contribute between the chosen $m=0$ states; nonvanishing is proved by
explicit radial and angular integration;

(b) $v=\|V\|=D_{\rm rel}(1\ \mathrm{V\,m^{-1}})$ in joules and the family
$H_{S}$ has the exact eigenvalues
$$F_{\pm}(\mathcal E)=\frac{E_{1}+E_{2}}{2} \pm\sqrt{\Bigl(\frac{\Delta}{2}\Bigr)^{2}+\bigl(D_{\rm rel}\mathcal E\bigr)^{2}},$$
the lower branch $F_{-}$ being the model's followed label for
dimensionless couplings $0\le\lambda<R:=\Delta/(8v)$, equivalently
$0\le\mathcal E<\Delta/(8D_{\rm rel})$, with $\Delta$ playing the role of the gap $g$;

(c) the page's perturbation theorem applies with nondegenerate label
$E_{1}$ (gap $\Delta$), and gives the vanishing first-order shift
$$E'(0)=0$$
and the exact second-order coefficient
$$E''(0)=-\frac{2D_{\rm rel}^{2}(1\ \mathrm{V\,m^{-1}})^{2}}{\Delta},$$
equivalently the quadratic Stark shift
$$F_{-}(\mathcal E)=E_{1}-\frac{D_{\rm rel}^{2}\mathcal E^{2}}{\Delta} +O(\mathcal E^{4});$$

**Proof technique:** direct; evaluate the compressed dipole matrix by the
angular selection rule and the explicit nonzero radial/angular integral,
diagonalize the resulting Hermitian two-by-two
family exactly, read off the page's coefficients, and compare the exact
closed form with the second-order truncation at the test coupling.

1.2 [The two-state family] In the orthonormal basis $(\psi_{1},\psi_{2})$ one has $\Pi_{W}H_{\kappa}|_{W}=\operatorname{diag}(E_{1},E_{2})$ by [L1] and orthogonality of distinct eigenstates; with $v:=D_{\rm rel}(1\ \mathrm{V\, m^{-1}})$ in joules one has $V=-v\sigma_{1}$ and $$H_{S}=\begin{pmatrix}E_{1}&-v\lambda\\-v\lambda&E_{2}\end{pmatrix}.$$ Since $\sigma_{1}$ is Hermitian with $\|\sigma_{1}\|=1$, $V$ is bounded self-adjoint with norm $v$; the exact eigenvalues of a matrix $\begin{pmatrix}a&w\\w&b\end{pmatrix}$ with real $w$ are $\frac{a+b}{2}\pm\sqrt{(\frac{a-b}{2})^{2}+w^{2}}$, verified by the same direct eigenvector computation as in the two-level example of this page with $g:=\Delta$, $w:=-v\lambda$; substituting $a=E_{1},b=E_{2}$ gives clause (b). [L1, given, algebra]

2.1 [Coefficients] The label $E=E_{1}$ is simple with gap $\Delta$ (the second level is $E_{2}=E_{1}+\Delta$ and there are no further levels in the two-dimensional model); the perturbation $V$ is bounded self-adjoint with norm $v$; hence [L3] applies for $|\lambda|v<\Delta/8$. Since $V$ has vanishing diagonal, $E'(0)=\langle V\psi_{1},\psi_{1}\rangle=0$. The reduced inverse on $Q_{0}W=\mathbb C\psi_{2}$ is $S=\Delta^{-1}|\psi_{2}\rangle\langle\psi_{2}|$, so $SV\psi_{1}=-(v/\Delta)\psi_{2}$ and $VSV\psi_{1}=(v^{2}/\Delta)\psi_{1}$, giving $E''(0)=-2v^{2}/\Delta$; substituting $v=D_{\rm rel}(1\ \mathrm{V\,m^{-1}})$ and expanding the closed form of clause (b) by [L4] gives the displayed quadratic Stark shift. This is clause (c). [L3, L4, step 1.2, algebra]

consumer_reviews.snippet:
(a) for every label and every Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$ the position
outcome law in the unit preparation $[\Psi_{nlm}]$ is
$$\mu^{G}_{\Psi_{nlm}}(B)=\|\psi_{nlm}\|^{-2}\int_{0}^{\infty}|u_{nl}(r)|^{2}\Bigl(\int_{S^{2}}\mathbf 1_{B}(r\Omega)\,|Y_{lm}(\Omega)|^{2}\,d\sigma(\Omega)\Bigr)dr;$$
in particular, for a **radial** set $B=\{x:a<|x|<b\}$ with
$0\le a<b\le+\infty$ one has
$$\mu^{G}_{\Psi_{nlm}}(B)=\frac{1}{\|u_{nl}\|_{2}^{2}}\int_{a}^{b}|u_{nl}(r)|^{2}\,dr,$$
so the **radial density** $p_{nl}(r):=|u_{nl}(r)|^{2}/\|u_{nl}\|_{2}^{2}$ is a
probability density on $(0,\infty)$: $p_{nl}\ge0$ and
$\int_{0}^{\infty}p_{nl}(r)\,dr=1$;

**Given:** The declared one-centre Coulomb model with $\hbar,m,\kappa>0$, $a_{\kappa}=\hbar^{2}/(m\kappa)$, $\gamma=2m\kappa/\hbar^{2}$ and bound vectors $\psi_{nlm}$, $\Psi_{nlm}$; the polar unitary and spherical harmonics of the angular-radial theory; the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice.

[F3] **Ground-state data and dimensionless ball bound.** Write $a_{0}:=2/\gamma$. The normalized ground eigenvector supplied by [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-ground-radial-probability-and-units]] has a representative $\phi_{100}(x)=(\gamma^{3}/8\pi)^{1/2}e^{-r/a_{0}}$, lies in $D(C_{\gamma})$, and satisfies $C_{\gamma}\phi_{100}=-\frac{\gamma^{2}}{4}\phi_{100}$. Its radial density $p(r)=\frac{\gamma^{3}}{2}r^{2}e^{-2r/a_{0}}=4r^{2}a_{0}^{-3}e^{-2r/a_{0}}$ is a probability density with mean $3a_{0}/2$ and unique mode $a_{0}$; its spatial density is strictly decreasing in $r$ and maximal at the origin. With $t:=2\varepsilon/a_{0}$, the ball probability is exactly $1-e^{-t}(1+t+t^{2}/2)$, and the proof of clause (d) of the cited item gives $\left|\int_{|x|<\varepsilon}|\phi_{100}|^{2}dx-\frac{t^{3}}6\right|\le t^{4}/8$. Also $a_{0}=\hbar^{2}/(m\kappa)=a_{\kappa}$ under $\gamma=2m\kappa/\hbar^{2}$ ([[thm-nrqm-coulomb-ground-radial-probability-and-units]] proof 3.2 and clauses (a)-(e), [[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clause (b)).

[F4] **Polar disintegration.** For $\psi(x)=u(r)Y_{lm}(\Omega)/r$ with $u$ square integrable and $Y_{lm}$ normalised in $L^{2}(S^{2},\sigma)$, and for every Borel $B$, one has $\int_{B}|\psi(x)|^{2}dx=\int_{0}^{\infty}|u(r)|^{2}\bigl(\int_{S^{2}}\mathbf 1_{B}(r\Omega)|Y_{lm}(\Omega)|^{2}d\sigma(\Omega)\bigr)dr$; this is the polar-coordinates formula for the Lebesgue integral with the surface measure $\sigma$ and Tonelli's theorem, together with $\int_{S^{2}}|Y_{lm}|^{2}d\sigma=1$ ([[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]], [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]], [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]], [[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-onb]]).

[F5] **Position law.** In a unit vector $\psi$ the model's Born position law is $\mu^{G}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{B}|\psi|^{2}dx$ for every Borel $B$ ([[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]] clause (b), [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]).

1.1 [General radial law] Fix a label. By [F1], $\psi_{nlm}(x)=u_{nl}(r)Y_{lm}(\Omega)/r$ and $u_{nl}$ is a regular solution of [F2]; the unit preparation is $[\Psi_{nlm}]$ with $\Psi_{nlm}=\psi_{nlm}/\|\psi_{nlm}\|$. By [F5] its position law is $\mu^{G}_{\Psi_{nlm}}(B)=\int_{B}|\Psi_{nlm}|^{2}dx$, and since the normalisation constant is a scalar, [F4] applied to $\Psi_{nlm}$ gives the displayed formula for every Borel $B$. For a radial set $B=\{a<|x|<b\}$ the indicator $\mathbf 1_{B}(r\Omega)$ does not depend on $\Omega$ and equals $\mathbf 1_{(a,b)}(r)$, so the inner integral is $\int_{S^{2}}|Y_{lm}|^{2}d\sigma=1$ by [F4] and $\mu^{G}_{\Psi_{nlm}}(B)=\|u_{nl}\|_{2}^{-2}\int_{a}^{b}|u_{nl}(r)|^{2}dr$; the density $p_{nl}$ is nonnegative and integrates to one over $(0,\infty)$ by choosing $a=0$, $b=\infty$. This proves (a). [given, F1, F2, F4, F5, algebra]

2.1 [Ground state] Take $n=1$, $l=m=0$. By [F2] with $j=0$ one has $L_{0}^{(1)}=1$ and the regular reduced solution is $u_{10}(r)=c_{10}r e^{-kr}$, where $k=\gamma/2=1/a_{\kappa}$ and $c_{10}\ne0$. With $Y_{00}=1/\sqrt{4\pi}$ from [F4], the corresponding representative is $\psi_{100}(x)=c_{10}e^{-r/a_{\kappa}}/\sqrt{4\pi}$. Polar integration gives $\|\psi_{100}\|=\|u_{10}\|_{2}=|c_{10}|a_{\kappa}^{3/2}/2$, so the normalized representative is $\Psi_{100}(x)=\zeta_{100}(\pi a_{\kappa}^{3})^{-1/2}e^{-r/a_{\kappa}}$ with $\zeta_{100}:=c_{10}/|c_{10}|$ and $|\zeta_{100}|=1$. It follows that $p_{10}(r)=|u_{10}(r)|^{2}/\|u_{10}\|_{2}^{2}=4r^{2}a_{\kappa}^{-3}e^{-2r/a_{\kappa}}$ and $|\Psi_{100}|^{2}=|\phi_{100}|^{2}$ for the normalized ground representative $\phi_{100}$ of [F3]. Thus [F3] supplies the mean, unique mode, strict decrease of the spatial density and exact ball probability. Put $t:=2\varepsilon/a_{\kappa}$; [F3] gives $$\left|\mu^{G}_{\Psi_{100}}(\{|x|<\varepsilon\})-\frac16\Bigl(\frac{2\varepsilon}{a_{\kappa}}\Bigr)^3\right|\le\frac{t^4}{8}=2\Bigl(\frac{\varepsilon}{a_{\kappa}}\Bigr)^4,$$ which proves the dimensionless remainder in (b). Positivity for every $\varepsilon>0$ and convergence to zero as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ follow because the exact probability formula in [F3] is strictly positive for $t>0$ and tends to $0$ as $t\downarrow0$. This proves (b). [step 1.1, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

consumer_reviews.snippet:
Adopt the framework's composition and state readings for a declared composite
of two distinguishable subsystems
([[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]],
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-reduced-preparations]]), the kinematics and
massive-particle model of P5 for a particle subsystem of spin label
$s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ with mass parameter $m>0$ and space
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, $r=2s+1$
([[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]), and
the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]), as required by the cited position-outcome law. In
the model below the particle
subsystem is $A$ and the marker subsystem is $B$. The following vocabulary is
used by this page.
 
**(a) Position readout of the particle factor.** The model's componentwise
position family has joint spectral projection valued measure $G$ on the Borel
sets of $\mathbb R^{3}$, with
$$G(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{B}},\qquad \mu^{G}_{\psi}(B)=\|G(B)\psi\|^{2}=\int_{B}\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx$$
for $\psi\in H_{s}$ of unit norm and Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$, read in
the metre unit of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]
([[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]] clause (b),
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b)). A
**declared detection bin** is a Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$; the
**local position-bin effect** of the declared composite is the bounded effect
$G(B)\otimes I_{K}$ of [[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]]
clause (d), and the **detection weight** of a preparation $\rho'$ of the
composite is
$$p_{\rho'}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho'\,(G(B)\otimes I_{K})\bigr)\in[0,1],$$
the reading of clause (iv) of P2 for that local effect.
 
**(b) Declared marked two-component model.** A **declared marked
two-component model** of the arrangement consists of: two unit vectors
$\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\in H_{s}$, the **path components** relative to the declared
pair of alternative path conditions; and two unit vectors $e_{1},e_{2}\in K$,
the **marker states** correlated with the alternatives. The assignment of
$\psi_{1},\psi_{2},e_{1},e_{2}$ and of the alternatives is declared apparatus
data in the sense of P7; it is not computed from the framework, and no element
of this definition asserts that a particle described by the model "took" one
of the two alternatives. A declared marked model is **overlap-normalized**
when $\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle=0$, and **trivially marked** when
$|\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle|=1$.
 
**(c) Phase family and marked preparations.** For $\varphi\in\mathbb R$ put
$$\Psi(\varphi):=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\Bigl(\kappa(\psi_{1}\otimes e_{1})+e^{i\varphi}\kappa(\psi_{2}\otimes e_{2})\Bigr)\in H_{s}\widehat\otimes K,$$
where $\kappa$ is the embedding of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]].
Define the **admissible phase set** $I:=\{\varphi\in\mathbb R:\Psi(\varphi)\ne0\}$. It is nonempty: $\Psi(0)+\Psi(\pi)=\sqrt2\,\kappa(\psi_1\otimes e_1)\ne0$, so those two vectors cannot both vanish, using $e^{i\pi}=-1$ from [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]. The **marked preparation at an admissible phase $\varphi\in I$** is the state assigned to the nonzero vector $\Psi(\varphi)$,
$$\rho(\varphi):=\widehat\rho\bigl(\Psi(\varphi)\bigr)=\frac{T_{\Psi(\varphi),\Psi(\varphi)}}{\|\Psi(\varphi)\|^{2}}\in D(H_{s}\widehat\otimes K)$$
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] clause (c)); the phase
$\varphi$ is read in radians (dimensionless). The **marker-carried which-path
preparation** is the statistical mixture
$$\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}:=\tfrac12\,T_{\psi_{1}\otimes e_{1},\,\psi_{1}\otimes e_{1}}+\tfrac12\,T_{\psi_{2}\otimes e_{2},\,\psi_{2}\otimes e_{2}},$$
a preparation of the declared composite by clause (iii) of P1.
 
**(d) Detection weights of the family.** For a declared detection bin $B$ and admissible phase $\varphi\in I$ put
$$p(\varphi)(B):=p_{\rho(\varphi)}(B)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(\varphi)(G(B)\otimes I_{K})\bigr),\qquad p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B):=p_{\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}}(B)=\tfrac12\bigl(\langle G(B)\psi_{1},\psi_{1}\rangle+\langle G(B)\psi_{2},\psi_{2}\rangle\bigr).$$
The numbers $p(\varphi)(B)$ and $p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)$ lie in $[0,1]$; they are
probabilities of the declared model, not measured frequencies.
 
**(e) Fringe visibility.** The **fringe visibility of the declared phase
family at the bin $B$** is
$$V(B):=\frac{\sup_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)-\inf_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)}{\sup_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)+\inf_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)}\qquad\text{whenever }\sup_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)+\inf_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)>0,$$
and is left undefined otherwise; all extrema, including the denominator, are taken over the nonempty admissible phase set $I$ of clause (c). The number $V(B)$ is a property of the declared model
and the declared bin, read as the modulation contrast of the family of
probabilities; it is not a measured visibility and carries no statement about
an apparatus.
 
**(f) Status.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the model vocabulary. The path components,
marker states and the identification of a concrete apparatus with the declared
model are declared and tested inputs in the sense of clauses (i)-(iii) of P7;
no dynamics, no interaction, no environment, no detector response, no counts
and no empirical result is asserted. In particular the model does not claim
that the marker is measured or read out, that the alternatives are physically
realized, or that the loss of contrast described by $V$ is caused by any
particular process; the quantitative statement about $V$ is the content of a
separate theorem of this page.
