Adopt the declared WKB regime model of
[[def-nrqm-approximations-framework-wkb-regime-model]] and let its data
$V,m,\hbar,\ell,E_\star,E,W,\lambda,h$ be as in that model, with
hypothesis (W1) on a closed interval $[a,b]\subset\mathbb R$: $W$ is $C^{2}$
on a neighbourhood of $[a,b]$ and $\lambda-W(\xi)\ge\delta>0$ for some
$\delta>0$ and all $\xi\in[a,b]$. Put
$$p(\xi):=\sqrt{\lambda-W(\xi)}>0,\qquad \theta(\xi):=\int_{a}^{\xi}p(s)\,ds,\qquad q(\xi):=\frac{3p'(\xi)^{2}}{4p(\xi)^{2}}-\frac{p''(\xi)}{2p(\xi)},$$
and
$$w_{\pm}(\xi):=p(\xi)^{-1/2}e^{\pm i\theta(\xi)/h},\qquad M(\xi):=\begin{pmatrix}w_{+}(\xi)&w_{-}(\xi)\\ w_{+}'(\xi)&w_{-}'(\xi)\end{pmatrix}.$$
Let $u\in C^{2}([a,b];\mathbb C)$ be an exact solution of the dimensionless
model equation $u''=(W-\lambda)u/h^{2}$ on $[a,b]$, and let
$$c(\xi)=M(\xi)^{-1}\begin{pmatrix}u(\xi)\\ u'(\xi)\end{pmatrix}$$
be its coefficient curve. Then, with $\|\cdot\|_{1}$ the $\ell^{1}$ norm on
$\mathbb C^{2}$ and all quantities read in the model's units:

(d) the estimate is exact at each fixed $h$; it degenerates as
$p(\xi)\to0$ and therefore excludes turning points by hypothesis (W1). It
asserts nothing about connecting asymptotics across a turning point, about
barrier transmission or reflection, about packets or detectors, and it makes
no claim that the right-hand side is small unless the dimensionless quantity
$h\int_{a}^{b}|q|/p$ is actually small. The estimate is an error bound of
Gronwall type, not an asymptotic expansion, and the physical reading of the
interval $[a,b]$ is $[x_{a},x_{b}]=\ell[a,b]$ in the line model with potential
$V(\ell\xi)=E_\star W(\xi)$ and energy $E_\star\lambda$.

[F2] **Integral and norm facts.** A continuously differentiable finite-dimensional vector curve satisfies $c(x)-c(a)=\int_a^x c'(s)\,ds$, and the induced matrix norm satisfies $\|Bc\|_1\le\|B\|_1\|c\|_1$; these are the fundamental theorem of calculus and the definition of the induced $\ell^1$ norm ([[lem-fundamental-theorem-of-calculus-for-banach-valued-continuous-curves]], [[def-bochner-integrable-function]]).

1.1 [Both coefficient relations and their matrix equation] By [F1], $M\in C^{1}$ is invertible and $(u,u')^{\mathsf T}\in C^{1}$, so $c=M^{-1}(u,u')^{\mathsf T}$ is $C^{1}$ and satisfies $Mc=(u,u')^{\mathsf T}$. Differentiating the first component of this identity and comparing it with the second gives $w_{+}c_{+}'+w_{-}c_{-}'=0$. Differentiating the second component, using $u''=-(p^{2}/h^{2})u$ and $w_{\pm}''+(p^{2}/h^{2})w_{\pm}=q w_{\pm}$, gives $w_{+}'c_{+}'+w_{-}'c_{-}'=-q u$. Thus $Mc'=(0,-qu)^{\mathsf T}$ and, since the Wronskian $W_0=-2i/h$, $c'=-q u M^{-1}(0,1)^{\mathsf T}=\frac{q}{W_0}\begin{pmatrix}w_{+}w_{-}&w_{-}^{2}\\-w_{+}^{2}&-w_{+}w_{-}\end{pmatrix}c=:Bc.$ Each entry of $B$ has modulus $h|q|/(2p)$ because $|w_{+}|=|w_{-}|=p^{-1/2}$ and $|W_0|=2/h$; the induced $\ell^{1}$ matrix norm is the largest column sum, hence $\|B\|_{1}=h|q|/p$. [F1, F3, given, algebra]

5.1 [Scope and degeneracy] The hypotheses used are (W1) and $W\in C^{2}$ on a neighbourhood of $[a,b]$: in particular $\lambda-W\ge\delta>0$, so $p\ge\sqrt\delta$ and no turning point occurs on the interval. The displayed estimate is exact at each fixed $h$; its error is small only when the displayed factor $\exp(h\int_a^x|q|/p)-1$ is small, which is an additional condition on the model data. The line-model units and physical interval $[\ell a,\ell b]$ are those of [[def-nrqm-approximations-framework-wkb-regime-model]] and [[lem-nrqm-approximations-scaled-line-model-correspondence]]. This proves clause (d), without asserting a connection across a turning point or a measured quantity. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, F3, given] ∎

- **What "controlled approximation" means here.** The theorem does not say that the WKB wave is close to the exact solution; it gives the exact Gronwall factor by which the WKB coefficient can change, so smallness is a checkable hypothesis on $h$ and on the dimensionless ratio $|q|/p$.
- **Turning points are outside the statement.** Hypothesis (W1) is exactly the exclusion of turning points; the connection problem across a simple turning point is a separate theorem of this page.

Adopt P1, P2, P4 and P7 in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]], and work in the
finite-mode realization of the declared fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]] with:
one-particle space $K=\mathbb C^2$, declared sites $|1\rangle,|2\rangle$ an
orthonormal basis of $K$, particle number $N=1$, single site-occupation
sector, and the declared one-particle operator (the **bond Hamiltonian**)
$$h:=-t\bigl(T_{|1\rangle,|2\rangle}+T_{|2\rangle,|1\rangle}\bigr),\qquad t>0\ \text{in joules}.$$
Adopt the canonical equilibrium postulate
[[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] at assigned
temperature $T>0$ and inverse temperature $\beta=1/(k_BT)$, and read
$\varepsilon:=2t$ as the tunnelling splitting. Then:

(c) the exact means, entropy and free energy are
$$\langle h\rangle_\beta=\frac{2t}{e^{2\beta t}+1}-t=-t\tanh(\beta t),\qquad s(\rho_\beta)=\log\bigl(1+e^{-2\beta t}\bigr)+\frac{2\beta te^{-2\beta t}}{1+e^{-2\beta t}},\qquad F=-\frac1\beta\log\bigl(1+e^{-2\beta t}\bigr)-t,$$
and for every $\beta>0$ one has $-t<\langle h\rangle_\beta<0$ and
$0\le s(\rho_\beta)<\log2$;

(d) *scope*: the computation is an exact statement about the declared
two-dimensional bond model at the assigned temperature; it identifies no
physical double-well or molecular system, asserts no measured splitting and
no transition, and the temperature assignment is the tested identification of
P7.

[L1] **The supplied two-level formulas.** For a two-dimensional space with
orthonormal basis $(u_0,u_1)$ and $H=\varepsilon T_{u_1,u_1}$, $\varepsilon>0$,
$\beta>0$: $Z=1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}$, $\rho_\beta$ is the corresponding
mixture, $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)=\varepsilon/(e^{\beta\varepsilon}+1)$
with values in $(0,\varepsilon/2)$, and
$s(\rho_\beta)=\log(1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon})+\beta\varepsilon/(e^{\beta\varepsilon}+1)<\log2$,
with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho_\beta)=-\beta^{-1}\log Z$
([[lem-nrqm-many-body-two-level-thermal-formulas]] clauses (a)-(c)).

[L2] **The declared model.** The finite-mode realization of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]] with $K=\mathbb C^2$,
$N=1$, one-particle operator $h$ and $W=0$ is a declared non-interacting
model; its sector is $K$ itself and the canonical preparation is the Gibbs
operator of the adopted ensemble postulate; the free-energy functional is
$F(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho h)-k_BT s(\rho)$ by
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]] clause (e).

**Given:** the declared bond model with coupling $t>0$, temperature $T>0$, $\beta=1/(k_BT)$, the vectors $u_\mp$, and [L1], [L2].

1.1 [Diagonalisation] In the basis $(|1\rangle,|2\rangle)$ the operator $h$ has the matrix $\begin{pmatrix}0&-t\\-t&0\end{pmatrix}$; the vectors $u_-=(|1\rangle+|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$, $u_+=(|1\rangle-|2\rangle)/\sqrt2$ are orthogonal unit vectors and $h u_\mp=\mp t\,u_\mp$ by direct evaluation, so $\{u_-,u_+\}$ is an orthonormal eigenbasis with eigenvalues $-t$ and $t$ by [[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]]. Hence $h+t\,\mathrm{id}$ has the eigenvalues $0$ on $u_-$ and $2t$ on $u_+$, and it satisfies the hypothesis of [L1] with $\varepsilon=2t$, $u_0=u_-$, $u_1=u_+$. This proves (a). [L1, algebra]

2.1 [Canonical data] Applying [L1] with $\varepsilon=2t$ gives $Z=1+e^{-2\beta t}$ and $\rho_\beta=Z^{-1}(T_{u_-,u_-}+e^{-2\beta t}T_{u_+,u_+})$ for $h+t\,\mathrm{id}$; since $h=(h+t\,\mathrm{id})-t\,\mathrm{id}$ and both operators are functions of the same eigenbasis, the Gibbs operator of $h$ is the same $\rho_\beta$, because the normalized Gibbs weights are unchanged by the shift: $e^{-\beta h}=e^{\beta t}e^{-\beta(h+tI)}$, so its partition trace is $Z_h=e^{\beta t}Z$ and division gives the same density. The mean of $h+t\,\mathrm{id}$ is $2t/(e^{2\beta t}+1)\in(0,t)$, so $\langle h\rangle_\beta=2t/(e^{2\beta t}+1)-t=-t\tanh(\beta t)$, which lies in $(-t,0)$ because $e^{2\beta t}>1$ for $\beta t>0$; the entropy formula is that of [L1] at $\varepsilon=2t$ and satisfies $0\le s<\log2$ by [L1], and $F=-\beta^{-1}\log(1+e^{-2\beta t})-t$ is the free energy of $h$ by [L2] and [L1]. This proves (b) and (c) apart from the scope clause. [L1, L2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 [Scope] The computation used only the declared two-dimensional model, its exact diagonalisation and the supplied two-level formulas; no physical double well, measured splitting, transition or thermodynamic limit entered, which is (d). [L1, L2, step 2.1] ∎

- **The shift by $t\,\mathrm{id}$.** Adding a constant to the Hamiltonian
  multiplies $Z$ by an exponential and leaves the canonical preparation and
  the entropy unchanged while shifting the free energy by the same constant;
  the example uses this to instantiate the supplied two-level formulas, whose
  levels are $0$ and $\varepsilon$.
- **Low- and high-temperature values.** The formulas give $s\to0$ and
  $\langle h\rangle_\beta\to-t$ as the exponential factor is suppressed, and
  $s\to\log2$, $\langle h\rangle_\beta\to0$ as it approaches one; the
  example states the exact formulas and the bounds, not a limit theorem.

(a) for every label, $\Psi_{nlm}\in D(H_{\kappa})$, $\|\Psi_{nlm}\|=1$,
$H_{\kappa}\Psi_{nlm}=E_{n}\Psi_{nlm}$, and vectors with distinct labels are
orthogonal; the vectors $\Psi_{nlm}$ of fixed $n$ span a subspace of dimension
$\sum_{l=0}^{n-1}(2l+1)=n^{2}$;

(d) the family is not complete in $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$: the
nonnegative spectral subspace $E_{H_{\kappa}}([0,+\infty))L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$
is nonzero, indeed infinite dimensional, and every unit vector $\psi$ in it has
$\mu^{H_{\kappa}}_{\psi}(B)=0$ for every Borel $B\subseteq(-\infty,0)$, i.e.
strictly negative energy outcomes have probability zero in such a preparation;
consequently the bound states of the model do not exhaust its state space and
the model possesses continuum states which are not bound states;

(e) *Energy-law reading.* For every unit vector $\psi$ the restriction of the
energy outcome law to the negative half-line is the discrete law
$\sum_{n\ge1}w_{n}\delta_{E_{n}}$ with weights
$w_{n}:=\|E_{H_{\kappa}}(\{E_{n}\})\psi\|^{2}\ge0$ and
$\sum_{n\ge1}w_{n}=\|E_{H_{\kappa}}((-\infty,0))\psi\|^{2}\le1$; for
$\psi=\Psi_{nlm}$ the whole law is the point mass $\delta_{E_{n}}$;

[F2] **Exhausted negative spectrum of the unscaled operator.** The negative eigenvalues of $C_{\gamma}$ are exactly $-\gamma^{2}/(4n^{2})$, $n\ge1$, and each eigenfunction at a negative eigenvalue lies in the closed span of the transported regular solutions; the negative eigenvalues of each radial operator $A_{l}$ are exactly $-\gamma^{2}/(4n^{2})$ with $n\ge l+1$, each with one-dimensional eigenspace spanned by its regular solution; and for real $k>0$ the value $k^{2}$ is not an eigenvalue of $A_{l}$, while $0$ is not an eigenvalue of $A_{l}$ either ([[thm-nrqm-coulomb-laguerre-bound-energy-exhaustion]] clauses (b), (c), (d), [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-jost-volterra-solution]] clause (d), [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-continuum-spectral-density]] clause (d)).

[F3] **Bound states and negative spectral subspace of the unscaled operator.** Each $\psi_{nlm}$ lies in $D(C_{\gamma})$ with $C_{\gamma}\psi_{nlm}=-\frac{\gamma^{2}}{4n^{2}}\psi_{nlm}$; vectors with distinct labels are pairwise orthogonal and the eigenspace at $-\gamma^{2}/(4n^{2})$ is exactly their span, of dimension $n^{2}$; after normalisation the family $(\psi_{nlm}/\|\psi_{nlm}\|)$ is a complete orthonormal family of $E_{C_{\gamma}}((-\infty,0))L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$; and the nonnegative spectral subspace $E_{C_{\gamma}}([0,+\infty))L^{2}$ is nonzero, indeed infinite dimensional, so the family is not complete in $L^{2}$ ([[thm-nrqm-coulomb-negative-subspace-completeness-and-degeneracy]] clauses (a), (b), (c), [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-essential-spectrum]] (c)).

[F4] **Block identity.** Let $U$ be the polar unitary of the angular-radial reduction with coefficient vector $U\psi=(u_{lm})$. For $\psi\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ one has $\psi\in D(C_{\gamma})$ if and only if $u_{lm}\in D(A_{l})$ for every $(l,m)$ and $\sum_{l,m}(\|u_{lm}\|^{2}+\|A_{l}u_{lm}\|^{2})<\infty$; then $U(C_{\gamma}\psi)=(A_{l}u_{lm})_{l,m}$, equivalently $UC_{\gamma}U^{*}=\bigoplus_{(l,m)}A_{l}$ on $K$ ([[thm-nrqm-coulomb-transported-radial-endpoint-realization]] clauses (a), (d), [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-angular-radial-unitary-reduction]] clauses (a), (b)).

[F6] **Outcome law and atoms.** For every preparation $\rho$ and Borel $B$ the energy outcome law is $\mu^{H_{\kappa}}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{H_{\kappa}}(B))$, for a unit vector it is $\|E_{H_{\kappa}}(B)\psi\|^{2}$, and $\mu^{H_{\kappa}}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=0$ unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue, in which case the value is the total weight of the eigenspace ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (b), (c), [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]], [[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]] clause (b) for the position reading).

1.1 [Eigenpairs and degeneracy] By [F3] clause (a), $\psi_{nlm}\in D(C_{\gamma})$ and $C_{\gamma}\psi_{nlm}=-\frac{\gamma^{2}}{4n^{2}}\psi_{nlm}$; by [F5] the eigenpair correspondence gives $\psi_{nlm}\in D(H_{\kappa})$ and $H_{\kappa}\psi_{nlm}=c_{0}\bigl(-\frac{\gamma^{2}}{4n^{2}}\bigr)\psi_{nlm}$. With $c_{0}=\hbar^{2}/2m$ and $\gamma=2m\kappa/\hbar^{2}$ one computes $c_{0}\frac{\gamma^{2}}{4}=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\cdot\frac{4m^{2}\kappa^{2}}{4\hbar^{4}}=\frac{m\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}}$, so $H_{\kappa}\psi_{nlm}=E_{n}\psi_{nlm}$ with $E_{n}=-\frac{m\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}$; the identity $E_{n}=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2ma_{\kappa}^{2}n^{2}}$ follows from $a_{\kappa}=\hbar^{2}/(m\kappa)$. Normalising preserves the eigenpair relation and orthogonality is inherited from [F3] clause (b); the eigenspace of $C_{\gamma}$ at $-\gamma^{2}/(4n^{2})$ is exactly the span of the $\psi_{nlm}$ with the stated labels, of dimension $n^{2}$, and by [F5] the eigenspaces of $H_{\kappa}$ at $E_{n}$ are the same, so the $\Psi_{nlm}$ of fixed $n$ span exactly that eigenspace. This proves (a) and the eigenspace claim of (b). [given, F3, F5, algebra, F1]

2.1 [No nonnegative eigenvalue] Suppose $H_{\kappa}\psi=\lambda\psi$ with $\psi\ne0$ and $\lambda\ge0$; by [F5] this is equivalent to $C_{\gamma}\psi=(\lambda/c_{0})\psi$ with $\lambda/c_{0}\ge0$, and $\psi\in D(C_{\gamma})$. Write $U\psi=(u_{lm})$; by the block identity [F4] one has $U\psi\in D(\bigoplus_{(l,m)}A_{l})$ and $(A_{l}u_{lm})_{l,m}=U C_{\gamma}U^{*}U\psi=(\lambda/c_{0})U\psi$, so $A_{l}u_{lm}=(\lambda/c_{0})u_{lm}$ for every $(l,m)$. Since $U$ is unitary and $\psi\ne0$, some component $u_{l_{0}m_{0}}$ is nonzero, and $\lambda/c_{0}\ge0$ is an eigenvalue of $A_{l_{0}}$, contradicting [F2] (no eigenvalue $k^{2}>0$, and no eigenvalue $0$). Hence every eigenvalue of $H_{\kappa}$ is negative; by [F2] clauses (b) and (d) together with [F5] the negative eigenvalues of $H_{\kappa}$ are exactly the numbers $c_{0}\,(-\frac{\gamma^{2}}{4n^{2}})=-\frac{\gamma^{2}c_{0}}{4n^{2}}$, $n\ge1$, with the eigenspaces of step 1.1. This completes (b). [step 1.1, F2, F4, F5]

2.2 [Non-exhaustion and the continuum] By [F3] clause (c) the nonnegative spectral subspace of $C_{\gamma}$ is nonzero, indeed infinite dimensional; by [F5] at $B=[0,+\infty)$, $E_{H_{\kappa}}([0,+\infty))=E_{C_{\gamma}}([0,+\infty))$, so the nonnegative spectral subspace of $H_{\kappa}$ is nonzero and infinite dimensional, and by step 1.2 the closed span of the bound states, namely the negative spectral subspace, is a proper subspace of $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$; this is the non-completeness in (d). For a unit vector $\psi$ in the nonnegative subspace the outcome law obeys $\mu^{H_{\kappa}}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{H_{\kappa}}(B)\psi\|^{2}$ by [F6], and for Borel $B\subseteq(-\infty,0)$ the multiplicativity in [F5] with $B\cap[0,+\infty)=\varnothing$ gives $E_{H_{\kappa}}(B)\psi=E_{H_{\kappa}}(B)E_{H_{\kappa}}([0,+\infty))\psi=E_{H_{\kappa}}(\varnothing)\psi=0$, so strictly negative energy outcomes have probability zero. [step 1.2, F3, F5, F6, algebra]

3.1 [Energy-law reading] For a unit $\psi$, [F6] gives the sigma-additive law $\mu^{H_{\kappa}}_{\psi}$ with $\mu^{H_{\kappa}}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{H_{\kappa}}(B)\psi\|^{2}$; its restriction to $(-\infty,0)$ is carried by the eigenvalues $E_{n}$ by step 1.1 and step 2.1, and [F6]'s atom rule gives $\mu^{H_{\kappa}}_{\psi}(\{E_{n}\})=\|E_{H_{\kappa}}(\{E_{n}\})\psi\|^{2}=w_{n}$, so additivity gives $\sum_{n}w_{n}=\mu^{H_{\kappa}}_{\psi}((-\infty,0))=\|E_{H_{\kappa}}((-\infty,0))\psi\|^{2}\le1$. For $\psi=\Psi_{nlm}$ step 1.1 gives $\mu^{H_{\kappa}}_{\psi}=\delta_{E_{n}}$. This is (e). [step 1.1, step 2.1, F6]

- **The degeneracy is a property of this model.** The independence of $E_{n}$
  from $l$ within the range $0\le l\le n-1$ and the resulting $n^{2}$-fold
  degeneracy are properties of the Coulomb spectral problem computed here; the
  page asserts no symmetry explanation of the degeneracy, and the later
  angular-momentum and approximation pages are the destinations for any such
  structural account.
- **Size of the degeneracy.** The count $\sum_{l=0}^{n-1}(2l+1)=n^{2}$ uses
  only the multiplicity $2l+1$ of each fixed-$l$ eigenspace, which is inherited
  from the $(2l+1)$-dimensional span of spherical harmonics in the cited
  mathematics; no additional multiplicity from the angular momentum coupling
  is claimed on this page.

spin-$s$ particle model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] and only within the

([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]).

- **Why a bounded profile.** The domain statement is that of the free
  operator on $W^{2,2}$; it does not cover linearly growing fields, point
  dipoles or fields whose components leave $L^{\infty}$, each of which would
  require a separate form-domain or resolvent analysis.

  value is asserted and, in particular, no exact value of any $g$-factor is
  assumed.

consumer_reviews.snippet:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5 and the
internal-factor assignment of the spin postulate P6, read for the massive
spin-$s$ model of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with
mass parameter $m>0$, spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ and
$r=2s+1$, together with the angular momentum readings of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]), and assume
the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, let $\mu^{A}_{\psi}$ be the
outcome law of an assigned sharp observable $A$ in the pure preparation of a
unit vector $\psi$, and for a unit vector $n=(n_{1},n_{2},n_{3})\in\mathbb
R^{3}$ put $S_{n}:=\sum_{i}n_{i}S_{i}$, the matrix action of the self-adjoint
matrix $\hbar\,n\cdot J$ on the internal factor. For every unit $n$, read
$(S_{n},\mathrm{J\,s})$ as an assigned sharp observable under P2. Put
$S^{2}:=S_{x}^{2}+S_{y}^{2}+S_{z}^{2}$ and, for its outcome-law claim in
(b), read $(S^{2},(\mathrm{J\,s})^{2})$ as an assigned sharp observable
under P2. Then:

(a) for every unit $n$ the operator $S_{n}$ is a bounded self-adjoint
operator on $H_{s}$ with spectrum
$\sigma(S_{n})=\hbar\{-s,-s+1,\dots,s\}$, and for each
$m\in\{-s,\dots,s\}$ the eigenspace $\ker(S_{n}-\hbar m)$ is the range of the
fibrewise orthogonal projection $P_{n,m}$ onto the eigenline of the matrix
$n\cdot J$ with eigenvalue $m$; consequently, for every unit $\psi\in H_{s}$,
$$\mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}(\{\hbar m\})=\|P_{n,m}\psi\|^{2}=\langle P_{n,m}\psi,\psi\rangle\qquad(m=-s,\dots,s),$$
and the law is concentrated on the finite set $\hbar\{-s,\dots,s\}$;

(c) for $s=\tfrac12$, every unit $n$ and every unit $\psi\in H_{1/2}$ one has
$$P_{n,\pm}=\tfrac12\bigl(I\pm n\cdot\sigma\bigr),\qquad \mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}\Bigl(\Bigl\{\pm\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\Bigr\}\Bigr) =\frac{1}{2}\Bigl(1\pm\langle(n\cdot\sigma)\psi,\psi\rangle\Bigr),$$
where $n\cdot\sigma$ is applied fibrewise; in particular,
$\mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}(\{\hbar/2\})+\mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}(\{-\hbar/2\})=1$ and
each number lies in $[0,1]$;

(d) **Scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P5 and
P6, the sharp-observable assignments stated above and the cited
finite-dimensional mathematics; they concern the internal
factor of the model. They assert no dynamics, no magnetic coupling, no
measurement or apparatus model, no joint measurement of two spin components,
no value of $\hbar$ and no empirical spin value. In particular the statements
do not identify the operators $S_{n}$ with any laboratory spin measurement,
and they contain no comparison with data.

**Given:** The postulates P1, P2, P5 and P6 in the stated readings; the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice; the spin-s model with parameters $m>0$, $s$ and $r=2s+1$; the internal matrices $J_{i}$ and the spin operators $S_{i}=\hbar J_{i}$; a unit vector $n\in\mathbb R^{3}$; the assigned pairs $(S_{n},\mathrm{J\,s})$ and $(S^{2},(\mathrm{J\,s})^{2})$ of the Statement; the operators $S_{n}$ and $S^{2}$; a unit vector $\psi\in H_{s}$; a preparation $\rho$; indices $i,j,k$ and eigenvalues $\lambda$ of a self-adjoint operator.

[F2] **Finite angular momentum classification.** If a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner product space $V$ carries self-adjoint endomorphisms $A_{1},A_{2},A_{3}$ with $[A_{1},A_{2}]=iA_{3}$ and its cyclic companions, then $V$ is an orthogonal direct sum of blocks on each of which the triple is unitarily equivalent to a spin-$j$ model with $A^{2}=j(j+1)I$ ([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-block-decomposition]] clauses (b),(c), [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]]).

[F3] **Model operators as matrix actions.** The model's $S_{n}$ is the fibrewise matrix action $(S_{n}f)(x)=\hbar(n\cdot J)f(x)$ on $H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ of a self-adjoint matrix, hence bounded self-adjoint with $\|S_{n}\|\le\hbar\|n\cdot J\|$ ([[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] clause (c), [[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]] clause (c), [[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]).

[F4] **Eigenvalues and their spectral weights.** If $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of a self-adjoint operator $A$ with spectral projection-valued measure $E_{A}$, then $E_{A}(\{\lambda\})$ is the orthogonal projection onto $\ker(A-\lambda)$; for the pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=\|E_{A}(\{\lambda\})\psi\|^{2}$ ([[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a),(b), [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b)).

[F5] **Observable assignments and outcome laws.** The model's coordinate angular momentum operators $L_i$ and $S_i$ are the assigned sharp observables of [[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]] clauses (b),(c) with unit $\mathrm{J\,s}$. The directional and squared-spin observable assignments used here are stated in the theorem's Statement. The outcome law of each assigned sharp observable is that of P2 in the reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b), and the pure preparations are those of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]).

1.1 [Directional component is a single spin-$s$ block] Fix a unit $n$ and choose an oriented orthonormal frame $(e^{(1)},e^{(2)},e^{(3)})$ of $\mathbb R^{3}$ with $e^{(1)}=n$; put $A_{i}:=\sum_{l}e^{(i)}_{l}J_{l}$ for $i=1,2,3$; expanding the commutator with [F1] gives $[A_{i},A_{j}]=\sum_{l,m}e^{(i)}_{l}e^{(j)}_{m}[J_{l},J_{m}]=i\sum_{k}\bigl(\sum_{l,m}\varepsilon_{lmk}e^{(i)}_{l}e^{(j)}_{m}\bigr)J_{k}=i\sum_{k}(e^{(i)}\times e^{(j)})_{k}J_{k}$, which equals $i\sum_{k}\varepsilon_{ijk}A_k$, including zero for $i=j$ and the negative sign for reversed indices, and $\sum_{i}A_{i}^{2}=\sum_{k}J_{k}^{2}=s(s+1)I$ by the orthonormality of the frame; by [F2] applied to the triple $(A_{1},A_{2},A_{3})$ there is a decomposition into blocks with parameters $j_{\nu}$ satisfying $j_{\nu}(j_{\nu}+1)=s(s+1)$ on each block, so $j_{\nu}=s$ and every block has dimension $2s+1=\dim V_{s}$; hence there is exactly one block and $A_{1}=n\cdot J$ has the simple eigenvalues $s,s-1,\dots,-s$, which is the spectrum statement of (a) at the matrix level. [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 [Fibrewise spectral measure and law of $S_{n}$] By step 1.1 the matrix $n\cdot J$ has the simple eigenvalues $m=-s,\dots,s$; let $P_{n,m}$ be the fibrewise action on $H_{s}$ of the orthogonal projection of $\mathbb C^{r}$ onto the eigenline of $n\cdot J$ with eigenvalue $m$; each $P_{n,m}$ is an orthogonal projection on $H_{s}$, $P_{n,m}P_{n,m'}=0$ for $m\ne m'$, $\sum_{m}P_{n,m}=I$ fibrewise, and $S_{n}=\sum_{m}\hbar mP_{n,m}$ as bounded operators; consequently $\ker(S_{n}-\hbar m)=\operatorname{ran}P_{n,m}$ because a class $f$ satisfies $\hbar(n\cdot J)f(x)=\hbar mf(x)$ for almost every $x$ exactly when $f(x)$ lies in the $m$-eigenline almost everywhere; by [F4] applied to the self-adjoint $S_{n}$ of [F3], $E_{S_{n}}(\{\hbar m\})=P_{n,m}$ and $\mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}(\{\hbar m\})=\|P_{n,m}\psi\|^{2}=\langle P_{n,m}\psi,\psi\rangle$ for every unit $\psi$; since $\sum_{m}P_{n,m}=I$, the law is concentrated on $\hbar\{-s,\dots,s\}$, which is (a). [step 1.1, F3, F4, F5, algebra]

3.2 [Spin-half probabilities] Let $s=\tfrac12$ and let $n$ be unit; by [F1], $(n\cdot\sigma)^{2}=\sum_{i,j}n_{i}n_{j}\sigma_{i}\sigma_{j}=\sum_{i,j}n_{i}n_{j}\delta_{ij}I=I$, so $n\cdot\sigma$ is a self-adjoint involution with eigenvalues $\pm1$, and $P_{\pm}:=\tfrac12(I\pm n\cdot\sigma)$ are orthogonal projections with $P_{+}+P_{-}=I$ and $(n\cdot\sigma)P_{\pm}=\pm P_{\pm}$; hence $P_{\pm}$ are the eigenline projections of $n\cdot J=\tfrac12n\cdot\sigma$ for the eigenvalues $\pm\tfrac12$, and step 2.1 gives $\mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}(\{\pm\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\})=\|P_{\pm}\psi\|^{2}=\langle P_{\pm}\psi,\psi\rangle=\tfrac12(1\pm\langle(n\cdot\sigma)\psi,\psi\rangle)$, which lies in $[0,1]$ because $P_{\pm}$ are projections and sums to $1$; this is (c). [step 2.1, F1, F3, F4, algebra]

- **Simplicity of the directional eigenvalues.** The simplicity of the eigenvalues of $n\cdot J$ is a statement about the internal matrices; the corresponding eigenspaces of $S_{n}$ on $H_{s}$ are infinite-dimensional (spatial functions times one internal vector), and clause (a) records the Born weight of the fibrewise projection, not a finite-dimensional multiplicity.
- **No joint law.** Nothing in this theorem asserts a joint outcome law of two different components $S_{n}$ and $S_{n'}$ with $n$ not parallel to $n'$; the incompatibility of the components is a separate result of the uncertainty page, and the present item uses no joint measurement model.

consumer_reviews.snippet:
The conservation laws proved here are model consequences: they hold for the
declared massive model with the displayed potential class and follow from the
invariance hypotheses as identities about that model. They are not reports of
measurements and do not establish that any laboratory preparation is exactly
described by the model. In particular, the mass parameter $m>0$, the charge
parameter $q$, the spin label $s$ and the potentials $(\mathbf A_{\rm ext},\Phi_{\rm ext})$
are declared model data in the units of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; the statement that a concrete
species, field configuration or apparatus realizes them is a tested
identification with uncertainty, external to these items. A selection rule or
a conservation law deduced here becomes an empirical prediction only after a
preparation map, a detection model, a sampling model and an uncertainty
budget are supplied, none of which this page provides. The agreement of such
an identified model with data is evidence about the combined model and
apparatus assumptions; it is not a proof of the postulates.

Adopt the postulates P1, P2, P4, P5 and the declared line model
[[def-nrqm-potentials-one-dimensional-line-model]], with $m>0$, $\hbar>0$ and
energy, potential and position read in the units of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix $a>0$, $U>E>0$ and the incident reference
amplitude $A_{\mathrm{in}}:=1\,\mathrm{m}^{-1/2}$, and let
$$V(x):=\begin{cases}U,&0<x<a,\\ 0&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}$$
let $k:=\sqrt{2mE}/\hbar$, $\kappa:=\sqrt{2m(U-E)}/\hbar$, and consider the
declared generalized stationary solutions of the model at energy $E$ (clause
(e) of the model) that are bounded, classically $C^{1}$ on $\mathbb R$ and
$C^{2}$ on each of $(-\infty,0),(0,a),(a,\infty)$. Then:

[F3] **The model's generalized-solution reading.** A declared generalized stationary solution has real energy, is bounded and classically $C^{1}$ with continuous derivative, is $C^{2}$ on each interval where $V$ is continuous, and satisfies the stationary equation there. Its amplitude has dimension $\ell^{-1/2}$, so its current is read in $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$; it is generally not in $L^{2}$ and is used only through the declared current and current ratios ([[def-nrqm-potentials-one-dimensional-line-model]] clause (e), [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clauses (d)1 and (d)5).

consumer_reviews.snippet:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4, the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5 and the internal-factor assignment of the
spin postulate P6, read for the massive spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$ and spin label $s$, together with the effective magnetic-moment coupling
adopted in [[post-nrqm-angular-momentum-magnetic-moment-coupling]] and the
angular momentum readings of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]], and
assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Fix a real constant
$B_{z}\in\mathbb R$ and use the uniform static field profile
$\mathbf B(x):=(0,0,B_{z})$, so that the Zeeman energy operator of the
postulate is
$$H_{Z}=H_{0}-\gamma_{s}B_{z}S_{3},\qquad H_{0}=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2},\qquad D(H_{Z})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}),$$
with flow $U_{Z}(t)=e^{-itH_{Z}/\hbar}$, and put $\omega:=\gamma_{s}B_{z}$
with unit $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$. For a unit vector $\psi\in H_{s}$ put
$\psi(t):=U_{Z}(t)\psi$ and $\langle S_{i}\rangle(t):=\langle
S_{i}\psi(t),\psi(t)\rangle$. Then:

(b) the component along the field is conserved: $S_{3}U_{Z}(t)=U_{Z}(t)S_{3}$
and $\langle S_{3}\rangle(t)=\langle S_{3}\rangle(0)$ for every unit $\psi$
and every $t$; more generally the outcome law of $S_{3}$ is time-independent
in every preparation;

**Given:** The postulates P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 and the magnetic-moment
postulate in the stated readings; the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of
Countable Choice; the model parameters $m>0$, $s$, $r=2s+1$ and
$\gamma_{s}\in\mathbb R$; the field constant $B_{z}\in\mathbb R$; the
operators $H_{0}$, $H_{Z}$, $S_{i}$, $S^{2}$; a unit vector $\psi$; real
$t,\theta$.

[F2] **Magnetic-moment postulate.** With $\gamma_{s}\in\mathbb R$ and a real
bounded measurable profile $\mathbf B$, the Zeeman operator
$H_{Z}=H_{0}-\gamma_{s}\sum_{i}S_{i}B_{i}(Q)$ with domain $D(H_{0})$ is a
bounded self-adjoint perturbation of $H_{0}$, of unit joule, and
$t\mapsto e^{-itH_{Z}/\hbar}$ is its strongly continuous unitary group in the
reading of P4
([[post-nrqm-angular-momentum-magnetic-moment-coupling]] clauses (i),(ii),
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]).

[F5] **Conserved law from commutation.** If a bounded self-adjoint $S$
satisfies $SK\subseteq KS$ for a self-adjoint $K$, then
$Se^{-itK/\hbar}=e^{-itK/\hbar}S$ for all $t$
([[thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-conserved-spectral-probability-laws]]
clause (a')); and if an assigned sharp observable $A$ satisfies
$e^{-isA/\hbar}U(t)=U(t)e^{-isA/\hbar}$ for all $s,t$, then its outcome law is
time-independent in every preparation, with conserved mean and second moment
on $D(A)$
([[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-generator-conservation]] clauses (a),(b),
[[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]],
[[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]],

2.1 [Transverse means] By step 1.1, $U_{Z}(t)^{*}=e^{-it\gamma_{s}B_{z}S_{3}/\hbar}e^{itH_{0}/\hbar}$, so using the commutation of $S_{1},S_{2}$ with $H_{0}$ from [F1], $U_{Z}(t)^{*}S_{1}U_{Z}(t)=e^{-i\omega tS_{3}/\hbar}S_{1}e^{i\omega tS_{3}/\hbar}=\cos(\omega t)S_{1}+\sin(\omega t)S_{2}$ and $U_{Z}(t)^{*}S_{2}U_{Z}(t)=\cos(\omega t)S_{2}-\sin(\omega t)S_{1}$ by step 1.2 with $\theta=-\omega t$; taking expectations in the unit vector $\psi$ gives the two displayed mean identities, and the pair transformation is the rotation by $-\omega t$; this is (a) and the conjugation identities of (c). [step 1.1, step 1.2, F1, algebra]

2.2 [Conservation of the field component] By [F4] the bounded self-adjoint $S_{3}$ commutes with $H_{0}$ and with itself, hence $S_{3}H_{Z}\subseteq H_{Z}S_{3}$ on $D(H_{Z})$; [F5] gives $S_{3}U_{Z}(t)=U_{Z}(t)S_{3}$ for every $t$, so $\langle S_{3}\rangle(t)=\langle S_{3}\rangle(0)$ for every unit $\psi$, and applying the second part of [F5] to the assigned sharp observable $(S_{3},\mathrm{J\,s})$ of [[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]] clause (c) gives the time-independence of the law of $S_{3}$ in every preparation; moreover $S^{2}$ is a scalar operator by [F4] and commutes with $U_{Z}(t)$. This is (b) and the Casimir statement of (c). [step 1.1, F4, F5, algebra]

consumer_reviews.snippet:
**(a) Adopted framework assumptions.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 and the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, in the readings of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] and [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]], [[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]). Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix real model parameters $m>0$ (mass parameter, unit $\mathrm{kg}$), $\omega>0$ (angular frequency, unit $\mathrm s^{-1}$) and the action constant $\hbar>0$ (unit $\mathrm J\,\mathrm s$) of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (d)4, and put
$$\ell:=\sqrt{\frac{\hbar}{m\omega}}>0\qquad\text{(unit }\mathrm m\text{),}$$
the model's length scale.

**(e) Physical reading and scope.** Clause (c) defines the model quantities that the page calls the energy and excitation number; it is a **model assumption** that the energy of the declared isolated particle is the assigned observable $(H_1,\mathrm J)$ and that $(N_\psi,1/\mathrm{count})$ is its excitation-number observable. The additive constant of the potential energy is removed at the minimum: for a one-dimensional potential-energy function $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^2$, with values in joules for position $x$ in metres, suppose $V$ has a non-degenerate local minimum at $0$, meaning $V'(0)=0$ and $V''(0)>0$. Taylor's theorem gives $V(x)-V(0)=\frac{1}{2}V''(0)x^{2}+o(x^{2})$ as $x\to0$; the oscillator model approximates this shifted potential-energy function by its quadratic term and sets $m\omega^{2}=V''(0)$. The oscillator's quantum ground energy in this convention is $\hbar\omega/2$. With only the stated $C^2$ regularity, the remainder is $o(x^2)$; no quantitative finite-amplitude error bound is asserted on this page (Binney §3.1, cited in the references). No measured value, no laboratory identification and no derivation of $m$ or $\omega$ from any microscopic or environmental theory is asserted. The model contains no damping, no external driving, no time-dependent parameters, no coupling to electromagnetic fields or radiation, no spin-dependent force, no anharmonic term, no relativistic correction and no boundary or many-body effect; those are separate model assumptions belonging to their own items. The parameters $m$ and $\omega$ are model parameters of dimensions $\mu$ and $\tau^{-1}$ in the conventions of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], and all displayed quantities are read in the units fixed there.

consumer_reviews.snippet:
**(ii) Spin.** For a declared **spin label** $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ the model assigns the internal factor $V_s=\mathbb C^{2s+1}$ with the standard inner product and basis $(e_m)_{m=-s,-s+1,\ldots,s}$. Here $SU(2)=\{W\in M_2(\mathbb C):W^*W=I_2,\det W=1\}$ with its matrix topology. For $s>0$ put $n=2s\ge1$ and let $F_s:\mathcal S_n\to V_s$ be the unitary identification $F_sv_k=e_{s-k}$ of [[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-symmetric-power-su2-representation]]. The assigned strongly continuous unitary representation is $D_s(W)=F_sU_n(W)F_s^{-1}$. For $s=0$ put $D_0(W)=I_{\mathbb C}$ for every $W$, the trivial one-dimensional representation with zero generators. The spin operators are $S_i=\hbar J_i$ with the self-adjoint endomorphisms of [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]], satisfying
$$[S_i,S_j]=i\hbar\sum_k\epsilon_{ijk}S_k,\qquad S^2=S_x^2+S_y^2+S_z^2=\hbar^2s(s+1)I.$$
For $A_i(t)=\cos(t/2)I_2-i\sin(t/2)\sigma_i$, the curve $D_s(A_i(t))$ has infinitesimal generator $-iJ_i$, including $s=0$. This specifies the internal $SU(2)$ action. If a spatial Hilbert factor $H_{\mathrm{sp}}$ is separately assigned a strongly continuous unitary $SU(2)$ representation $R_{\mathrm{sp}}$, the combined action is explicitly $W\mapsto R_{\mathrm{sp}}(W)\otimes D_s(W)$ on $H_{\mathrm{sp}}\widehat\otimes V_s$: its representation law follows from bounded tensor composition, and continuity follows on elementary tensors and then by density and the unitary norm bound. The existence and physical interpretation of that spatial action require the separate assignment. The spin label and representation are species model assignments; the internal factor is not a rotating body or a spatial coordinate.

- **Sector and statistics.** The model does not derive from a sector that a species is bosonic or fermionic in nature; it declares the sector. Consequences such as the exclusion of coincident fermionic occupied states are conditional on the adopted antisymmetric sector.
- **Finite spin only.** The internal factor is finite-dimensional, with the representation displayed above. Infinite-dimensional internal structures and relativistic spinor bundles are separate model assumptions.
- **Spin and orbital angular momentum are distinct.** The operators $S_{i}$ of this postulate act on the internal factor; orbital generators act on the spatial factor, and the two are combined only through stated tensor constructions.

This page develops the radiation extension of the framework: the
fixed-mode polarisation model, the quantised transverse radiation sector and
the number, energy and momentum readings of its preparations. The extension is
an explicitly adopted model assumption,
[[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]]: a
declared propagation mode carries a two-dimensional transverse polarisation
space; the free radiation is the bosonic Fock space of the transverse
one-particle space
$\mathfrak h=\{f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{3}):k\cdot f(k)=0\ \text{a.e.}\}$;
and in a declared inertial chart the mode label $k$ is assigned the frequency
$\omega=c|k|$, the photon energy $E=\hbar\omega$ and the photon momentum
$p=\hbar k$, with $c$ and $\hbar$ carrying the SI values of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The postulate records explicitly
that these assignments are not derived from the massive model, from Maxwell's
theory or from special relativity, that no Lorentz transformation law for mode
labels is claimed and that the extension does not claim Galilean covariance of
the radiation sector.

consumer_reviews.snippet:
This page fixes the framework and the quantity conventions of the
non-relativistic quantum mechanics category before any derived result is
stated. The arena is the Newtonian one: the affine time space with absolute
time, Euclidean simultaneous slices and their smooth structure
([[def-nrqm-framework-newtonian-spacetime]]), whose elementary coordinate
transformations are the Galilean maps with their parameter quadruples
([[def-nrqm-framework-galilei-transformations]]) forming a group of bijections
of the coordinate space ([[lem-nrqm-framework-galilei-transformations-form-a-group]]).
The inertial frames of the model are the adapted charts determined by an event
origin, a fixed time vector $u$ with $\tau(u)=1$, and a positively oriented
orthonormal spatial triad, changed only by the Galilean class
([[def-nrqm-framework-inertial-frames]]), and the
macroscopic apparatus and preparation devices are described by classical
trajectories with the frame time as parameter
([[def-nrqm-framework-classical-apparatus-trajectories]]); a quantum particle
is not assigned a definite worldline between preparations and detections. The
dimension group, the SI reference units, the exact defining constants of the
current SI and the dimensions and mathematical types of the framework's
quantities are recorded in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], and
the canonical commutator of the position and momentum acts is proved on the
Schwartz core in [[lem-nrqm-framework-ccr-on-the-schwartz-core]].

consumer_reviews.snippet:
Three counterexamples then refute precise statements.
[[cex-nrqm-framework-zero-mass-has-no-self-adjoint-limit]] refutes the
specified strong action limit on every Schwartz state together with a finite
free-frequency limit at fixed nonzero wave number: one explicit normalized
compactly supported smooth state has diverging kinetic-operator norm, and
every fixed normalized operator-domain state with nonzero momentum second
moment has divergent kinetic expectation. Its model root-mean-square speed
depends on mass and is not held fixed as mass tends to zero. This does not
decide other notions of convergence or rule out independently specified
massless models.
[[cex-nrqm-framework-quadratic-shear-is-not-galilean]] exhibits a smooth
time-dependent translation chart of the arena that is not a Galilean
transformation and assigns nonzero coordinate acceleration to a curve of zero
coordinate acceleration in the standard chart.
[[cex-nrqm-framework-mean-position-can-fail-to-exist]] displays a normalized
state in a one-dimensional P1/P2 instance whose first absolute and second
position moments both diverge, so its mean position exists only under the
moment condition recorded in the framework's quantity conventions. A closing scope audit
([[rem-nrqm-framework-examples-scope-limits]]) records what each check
establishes and that none of them reports or predicts a measured outcome.
